Lilith opened my eyes to the crimes of Inarius. He betrayed her, banished her. He sapped the power of her children. He’s the reason we’re weak, the reason we die. He ruined us because he feared us! We’ll show him he was right to be afraid.

How silly my idle fancies of yesterday seem now. I believed in the Horadrim, but I was misled. With them as our champions, we can barely survive. But Lilith will make us victors. All my life, I’ve been searching...but it was me that needed to be found.

How sweet this taste! Lilith asked me to aid in a ritual: sacrifice a priest from the escort. He had no fight. He just prayed as we made his blood useful. Forgive my hand, I'm still shaking. Power dances along my bones. I walk the path of our maker now.

A History of the Settlement of Malnok

Settled in the most unlikely of places, Malnok sits around a frozen lake deep in the mountains. The town is known for its rich natural mineral deposits, the mining of which became the town's primary industry with the establishment of Anica's Claim...
A torn and tattered page from a journal. It reads: "The corruption has lingered and festered for years. This is exactly what my work requires."
A journal page with dirt smudges that makes parts of the writing illegible. It reads: "So many bodies! [illegible] everywhere lie corpses. [illegible] ample material for the experiments."
A blood-splattered page ripped from a journal. It reads: "I’m so close. After so many failures, the hosts are almost viable. I will cure my illness and death itself."
A torn faded journal page. It reads: "The insects have infested my failed trials. Perhaps they are related to whatever happened to this place so long ago?"
A journal page written in red ink. It reads: "The corruption here is affecting me...this is no mere plague. No matter; soon it won't matter what happens to my mortal body."
The defenders of this keep slayed countless vampires. It was still not enough.
The vampires clearly abhor all living things. These fallen knights may have considered their quick deaths a mercy if they'd known of the fate that awaited their comrades.

... since the disturbance in the Archives. We have seen an increase in the activity of the vampires near the fortress, but we do not fear these abominations. No reinforcements are necessary; the Light will preserve us if they dare show themselves.
Trapped by the Khazra's icy storm, these villagers' shelter became their tomb.
A typical display of the Khazra's cruelty, these villagers were used as part of the ritual which destroyed their homes.
These carvings are a monument to Nostrava's skilled woodworkers. Their features are so lifelike it seems like they could almost move.
Tools of master woodworkers. Normally handled with great care, these seem to have been abandoned for some time.

Here lies Maryam, forever a light in the darkness.
Here lies Sir Thom - guardian, mentor, friend. He gave his life protecting all from harm.

It seems these villagers tried to escape the flames engulfing their home, but they found no shelter here.
A huge pile of loosely covered corpses. The marker reads: "Akarat forgives ALL heretics in death"
This ritual site appears well used. There must be a large amount of sites within these ruins in use by these cultists. What they are doing and how they move past the snakes is a mystery.
Warning! The Serpents still prowl the Temple Ruins.

To combat the humid swamps, wood is carefully bundled and left to dry before burning.

The violence here seems like it was indiscriminate. Zakarumite and Kehjistani alike fell in droves.

Etchings in stone, surrounded by runes, blood, and vines. This is where the Hands of Akarat performed a sacrificial rite to infuse the forests of Lycander with Hatred.
Covered in burns, poison darts, and countless stab wounds. This was a desperate battle.
A neatly stacked account of events, observations, and theories, detailed in tight, clean script.
Cut loose from the head, the rotten roots have fallen silent and still.
Lopped off during the fight. They twitch in the presence of the head.
The jagged glass is smeared with reeking, inky blood, obscuring any hint of reflection.
Acorns, berries, and bits of shiny metal lay piled by Ouna's altar. Some have tiny teeth-marks.
Roughly gathered in a heavy clay vase. Brilliant colors as beautiful as they are a warning of danger.
Delicate, sable-hair brushes for the application of Gelena's ritual markings. They are arranged small to large, thin to thick.
Backwater Rum, by the smell of it. Enough to fell a pirate crew.
A small figurine made of wood, bone, and twine. Who could it represent?
Folk of the swamp, and others that call it home, have gathered to serve the Tree. Have they come out of love or fear?
Drawings of the ritual circle and component elements, thoroughly labeled in Gelena's meticulous handwriting.
Blood from the Moors, tracked onto the cave floor. Something big came this way.
Each has been whittled to a point with a dull knife. Simple tools, but for what?
Tiny mice squeak inside. A fine meal for some creatures of the swamp.
A large-statured figure woven from twine. Small rib bones are attached to the head, forming a druid's crown.
Scores of pages are marked and dog-eared. Gelena has done her research.
A scattered collection of phrases and musings. One stands out among them.

SNO: Long have I been far from my home. Adrift in the doldrums at sea. I raise my sails and cry to the winds, 'Bring my love back to me.'

Translation: No sign of the hateful ichor remains. The cleansing appears to have worked.
Among the bloody scratches, the words "Where is he?" repeat. Over and over.
There are fewer bottles of rum than before. Judging by Caidin's breath, it's clear where they went.
The lands of Estuar lay stacked on top of each other, covered in Gelena's scribblings, ink stains, and scrying tools.
Many have been drawn here to serve the Tree in its hour of need. Some willingly, some not.
It's the same talisman Caidin found in Kehjistan, but it looks different now, clean of rot and gore. Somehow familiar.
The empty crate, scattered bottles, and Caidin's slurring leave little doubt of what happened here.
Now in pieces, Ouna's talisman seems no more than bone, twine, and precious stones. Its magic is a mystery.
Hatred's attack was terrible, but it has weakened the Tree. There will be no better time... I must cut the heads from the branches now, and root them in new flesh. I can do this.
These are similar to the one Caidin found, but each is a little different. More glyphs, varied stones... Improvements?
Walking sticks, leather shoes, fine robes, sweet fruits... Gifts to celebrate the beginning of new lives.
May you rest among friends for eternity.
Against the wind, rain, and swamp, the flame clings stubbornly to the wick.
They are skillfully planted in the soil of Ouna's grave. A poppet leans against the stems, wearing a folded leaf as a wide-brimmed hat.
Scattered bottles, herbs, woven poppets... Caidin left much behind.
The pages are neatly stacked, but Gelena's handwriting waivers. Returning the heads to the Tree will, in no way, be easy.
Her clouded eyes dart side to side, unseeing and confused as her lips part to speak. She makes no sound.
As soon as they appear, they fade with the wind. Or was that a whisper?
Thorned roots sprout up through the stone tiles, teeming with a strange, sickly rot.
The same rotten roots spill out from the doorway.
Wanderer, I have business in Backwater. Meet me there. -Shyan
Countless muddy footprints mark the path of Akarat's procession—Amazons, men, women, and children.
Picked off by pirate arrows, left behind by the procession. They've been stripped of all they had.
Not unlike the steps to the Temples of Life and Courage. Though these have crumbled into the sea.
She must have fallen during the ancient flood. She bears a striking resemblance to statues revered by the Drowned.
Fresh as they come, pierced by Amazon arrows and spears.
Each is marked by so many wounds, it's hard to tell which killed them.
The shield bears a message, written in flowing script: "Behind every soldier, the miller who feeds them."
Several messages are crudely carved into the flagstones. "Spearmaiden Elesa was here. Sailed to Tristram, 1264." "To Hell with Queen Barga!" "Never court a barbarian. All fury, no sense!"
Framing the depictions of the mighty Firstborn, thousands of names are inscribed—Amazon warriors who gave their lives for Skovos.
Young warriors who held the line. Few look older than twenty years.
The signal fire has burned down to coals. No more help is coming.
Fine canvas charred. Bright bronzes ashen. Acrid with smoke but for the scent of jasmine in the air.
The gargantuan corpse festers in the sun, blocking the road to Atanos. The stench alone could repel an army.
Gathered for burial, each beside their weapon.
A flag once displayed over a house threshold now marks a sodden tent where the family resides.
A few bottles of medicine, each almost empty. Not nearly enough for these wounded.
Torn heraldry saved from the Temple of Courage, stitched as best as a soldier could manage.
Scant food supplies, lousy with rot and insects.
Large enough to sink a warship, spiral-fluted for distance and accuracy.
Est'd 1062. Drinks half price for servicewomen. No mainlanders without escort.
Dozens of bottles, freshly brewed with a familiar smell...like Lorath's cabin.
The fumes from these pots sting the eyes. A large sign stands beside them, painted in Lorath's familiar hand: "DANGER! NO OPEN FLAMES!"
It appears these are not natural caverns but an ancient, sunken ruin.
This wreck is so old, it's fused into the rock. What could have brought it here?
A single word is etched into the corroded metal, its Ancient script barely legible: "ATANOS"
An aged port wine from the kingdom of Westmarch, well-traveled and yet still sealed.

...little is known from before this time. However, the many ruins and artifacts left behind tell us that humans, angels, and even demons lived together peacefully for centuries. That is, until the Purge...
Askari History Vol. 4, "The Fury and Forge of Hefaetrus"

...Hefaetrus is said to have created many great marvels, providing the advantage necessary for defeating the Lilin. However, despite his talent for it, after the war he vowed that his creations would never again be used to spill blood...

...but there were those who used this time of anarchy to rape and pillage. Though Hefaetrus had vowed to rebuild Skovos, he could not find the strength to fight for it. Zerae took arms against these raiders alone, wielding an overwhelming power...
A lone skeleton. Broken ribs seem to indicate that the ancient victim was killed by stabbing.
It's difficult to make out the fine details, but it seems this mound of stone was once a shelf for scrolls, tomes, and books.

A collection of stone fragments positioned as though someone were trying to piece them back together. Each have detailed etchings of symbols you don't recognize. Though even if you could, most are warped, cracked, and scorched beyond legibility.
The remains of several scrolls and tomes, their contents now known only to the flames.
Ancient remains entombed in rock. Their hands reach for help that never came. A lone talisman sways in the wind, offering what little comfort it can.
The crumbling remains of a once-great structure. Strange that only the statue of the demon seems to have remained intact.
The ground shifts and stirs, dredging up long-swallowed secrets. Two bodies, or perhaps more, stay locked in eternal embrace.
Large, bird-like talons carved deep grooves into the mountain stone.
Its stained-glass sides shine with their own inner light.
The bile foams here. Something stirs below.
The lava bubbles here. Something stirs below.
The water froths here. Something stirs below.
The hunk of flesh still writhes on Myveli's plate. It smells like sulfur and a hot forge.
The tablet has been smashed to pieces. A few ancient words, such as "sight," remain legible, but the rest are too broken and scattered to make sense of their meaning.
A list of Knights that died in the siege of hell.
Prayers to the dead martyrs for strength and courage.
Two small skeletons lie folded into one another, huddled tight in a shared warmth. Their fingers clutch fast, bones interlaced.

Seer Laurel's vision in Oracle Myrrhine's fifth year: "Two frightened children flee their father. Terror clings to them like a wet cloak. They cross the base of the rapids and cling to the cliffs. Stumbling, they fall into a ruin marked by the Great Eye."

A bronze suit of armor stands neatly upon its rack. Its workmanship is exquisite, though age has undone it all the same. The leather and thread appear liable to disintegrate at a single touch. Upon the breast is stamped the sigil of Philios.

The inscription upon the small effigy has been largely claimed by age. The greater part is no longer readable, save for a single surviving dedication: "To Askarra, Antia, and Seryn—Yours, until the end of days."

Multiple statues of the same angel have been carved from marble and abandoned before their completion. Their bodies are formed, lacking only the wings and the final details that would have made them whole.

Set within its stone casing, the small crystal hums with a soft, melodic vibration. The sound resembles something songlike, yet feels hollow and strange, as though it were a pale imitation of something far greater.

The lower half of a stone oval—the upper portion long since crumbled. Runes of celestial origin are carved into the surviving stone. In the tomes of the Horadric Vault, similar relics are described as wards to conceal such places from unbidden eyes.

Philios bids me write down my thoughts. How foreign to chronicle what I will remember eternally, but it is a custom of the Firstborn. We have made this vault so Philios and I might be at peace, though peace is a rare guest amid his countless creations.

I was summoned by Inarius to a secret meeting. A sickness in his mind breeds eternal dissatisfaction. I cannot endure his endless shifts from purpose to doubt. I was unwise to tell Philios it for he has already warned others, including Lilith...

My heart aches. Our sanctuary is painted with the blood of angel, demon, and Firstborn. The occluder kept us hidden until the slaughter ended. We gathered within these walls all we could save. Inarius has slithered away to his Tower to lick his wounds.
Chronicle of the Blade, Part One
I was born of Hatred herself. Lilith. I tried so desperately not to hate her for what she was. For I knew she would never change—couldn't—even if she'd wanted to.
Chronicle of the Blade, Part Two
One day, she gave me a gift: the Promise of her protection. A piece of her, honed sharp enough to tear a hole in reality. It was poison, like the rest of her. So I shattered it.
Chronicle of the Blade, Part Three
I dreamed of a Serpent. On its scales, I saw blood, truth, glimpses of what would come. And I saw a spear of light, piercing Hatred's heart.
Chronicle of the Blade, Part Four
I knew this "spear" was in some way a symbol of Mother's gift, her Promise. It had a purpose for Sanctuary, but I could not bring myself to accept that. Not at first.
Chronicle of the Blade, Part Five
Suffocated by Hate and my own hatred for it, I disappeared from the world. And in my absence, I yearned for it. I missed its people, its creatures. I missed the tatters of my family.
Chronicle of the Blade, Part Six

I grew older, and, I hope, wiser. And so I learned that perhaps I am as unchangeable as Mother is. Perhaps it is not for me to decide what becomes of her gift. It is a part of fate, and I will leave it as such.
A heap of Mephisto's fallen servants. They were not ready for the traps laid here in Young Rathma's abode.
An array of hooks, pliers, and irons meant to loosen tongues. They've seen fresh work. On the table lie teeth and fingernails newly pried.

The Midwife's pack has been turned over and gutted. There's no hint of where the other Midwives might be hiding, nor what they seek. All that remains is a faded prayer dedicated to something known as He Who Waits From the Void.
The parchment is fresh, yet the sketches and runes are copies of something far older. Only three symbols hold meaning to you: willing blood, the Void, and Lilith.
In smeared, trembling letters of blood, the sand reads: "Into the cave. Help us."
Heavy ankle fetters lie in the sand. Each ring is stamped with strange Hatred's marks. They radiate faint heat.

The woman's head has been crowned with a roughly beaten helm fashioned in the likeness of a horned demon. Her distended belly has been split from breastbone to navel. Her corpse sways in a soft, unnatural rhythm as though in worship.
The blood used to draw the circle has dried to a dark, rust-like crust. The symbols are smeared by dragged feet and violent struggle. Only a few runes remain intact.
A rough-hewn box filled with chunks of torn membranes and umbilical remnants displayed like butcher's fare. Its preserving fluid is uneven. The flesh is greying and leathery at the edges.

The woman's body lies face down in the wet sand, half-buried where the tide lapped at her. Bruises mar her arms and ankles. Her hands are curled into fists, nails broken and bloody. Her belly is swollen with late pregnancy.

...Four more from the coast and two from the inland farms. Late in term and strong-bodied. Sister Magdalena's guise as a healer remains effective, but suspicion is growing. We are close now. Only a few more for the birthing...

No sleep. No light. We sew and sew. Braid their small, soft ribs like reeds. The circle forms with every stitch. In their still eyes, He stirs. In the smallest, He whispers. Their flesh becomes a door. One child shall bear Him. The others make the bridge.

Brother Imar is the only one we can spare to pursue Istel. She is dangerous, yes, but in her blind devotion to her whore-mother, she cannot undo us. Nor Him. We have no need of her ritual any longer. I have heard His voice. Gather. Prepare. Rejoice.
Dedication to He Who Waits From the Void
Carved into the shrine reads: "Architect of hidden paths, hear your servants. Knead my thoughts into form. Hollow my marrow and refill it with your purpose. Through your designs, shape me anew."
A solitary helmet rests upon the throne. Perhaps a reminder of the countless Amazon slain in the war against Hatred, or a ghost of a queen's absence.

This great tablet records the lineage of Amazon queens from the Firstborn Era onward. Every name is carved with ritual precision and inlaid with gold filigree, making each letter glitter as the light touches them.
Crude images deface the effigy of the old queen in red paint. A tarp shrouds the statue while a worker boards it over to spare others the sight.
'"She who fights beside her sisters stands not alone, for a thousand hands steady her spear.

SNO: She who dies in battle is born in legend, to join Askarra's numbers in the stars.
Thus we stand, unbroken in oath and purpose—daughters of Antia."

Translation: This shrine honors Seryn, Mother of Oracles. The statue has been lovingly tended through the ages. Before her feet, the smallfolk lay gifts of good wine, fresh blossoms, and incense, in hopes that the Oracle of Oracles might grant them favor.
Here lies Antia, First of Queens, Spear-Mother of Skovos.
Her body bears the marks of torment: flesh branded by hot iron, armor melted into skin. All of it done with deliberate cruelty. She endured long before death, or mercy, came.
A stone shelf covered in old tablets
A long and rambling volume about walking trade routes on the Skovos Isles. It recommends staying away from Skartara, for fear of burned merchandise.
A dry tome detailing all the unique architectural feats of the Firstborn. It attempts to explain how they were built, using increasingly fantastical methods.
The pages are dog-eared, the book is coated in sand and smells of seawater. Someone's beloved beach read.
I have moved my research to a secret bookshop in Temis. Meet me there if you have more to show me.
A thick tome on Skovos pirate territory and their trade routes. On the first page is a big note reading "INACCURATE AND USELESS".
A tome detailing the known history of the Drowned. It consists of little more than a few water-damaged pages.
An ancient record of Skovos poetry. Most of the poems don't rhyme.
The merchant's face is frozen in shock, his body punctured with several large, ragged wounds.
A standard-issue mining pick, casually abandoned. Judging by the dried blood and viscera splattered on it, this is clearly the murder weapon.
A small fortune in coins and gems, in which the murderer apparently had no interest.
The pages are filled with beautiful ink drawings of a certain strange fish. Each drawing is different – as though the artist were trying to get it right.
Fishing rods and tackle, clearly handmade yet surprisingly ornate.
An old whiskey barrel, stuffed with blankets and gnawed fish bones. Cozy for such a large cat.
In memory of Adoné, who had the bravery to stand against a mob, and the kindness to guide a stranger. May she rest in the true Light.
A salt-grimed letter about failed offerings.
A letter discussing the abducted children
A letter discussing the abducted children
A letter discussing the abducted children
Discarded children's clothing, sodden and stained. Mud and ruddy rack permeate the matted refuse.
Dismembered livestock crudely positioned in circular formation. The wounds are jagged and cursory, splintering bone and weeping organs.
Coarse linen formed into crudely constructed sacks. A rust-colored fluid drips from the saturated mass, revealing children's footprints.
Scattered bottles, broken and grimed with sludge. Crimson pools of blood weave through the fogged shards of glass.
The marks of past Oracles, each one unique to its wearer. Etched below each mask is the date of the Oracle's reign; they were rarely more than fifteen years total.
I saw a serpent coiling in the fires of the Eternal Conflict,

SNO: On its scales were reflected the truth: Sanctuary can never be saved...

Translation: I saw my corpse, and from my mouth crawled Hatred,

SNO: A father burned his children on a pyre, and a mother molded a new age from the ashes...

Translation: I saw the weak made strong, a pack of lambs feasting on wolves,

SNO: Tears of blood rained on a desert jewel, and the way to Hell was torn asunder...

Translation: Then came a spear of light, piercing Hatred's heart,

SNO: And he who was bound in chains was set free...

Translation: I saw a wise man with seven arms drown the sun in Hatred's blood,

SNO: An island veiled in a fog of lies and a city frozen in fear...

Translation: From mercy's open hand came plagues of every name,

SNO: While false prophets trampled fallen saints into the mud...

Translation: I saw a child give birth to a mother,

SNO: As Hatred's sun set and that of Terror and Destruction dawned.

Translation: Drops of blood mottle an ominous urn. A carving above reads, "Blood grants sight. Blood grants certainty."
An eerie, blood-painted urn displays the grisly image of a woman chopped in half.
The blood-painted urn shows a macabre scene of a child being torn apart by birds.
The remains of bottles smashed against the wall. It happened recently—the ground is still stained red from the wine.
-- town visited by Akarat. The fifth so far that I have -- followers all say he journeys south -- Skovos Isles -- needs followers, but why? What -- lies in these lands of the Ancients?
A sketch of the Sightless Eye, ringed by notes from Neyrelle. One of them reads, "The path lies through the Eye. But how? The Oracle of Skovos will know. She is the hand that can open the way."

Rathma's Prophecy is a riddle. The "Spear of Light" is no spear at all, but something else. Something real. A blade forged by Lilith at the dawn of the world. Given as a gift to her children. Then lost. It is the answer. It must be.
Though dead, the creature's flesh pulses with unholy energy. A sense of vertigo overtakes you as you stare at the tattered flesh.
Victims of the merfolk and other creatures that stormed the ship. Most of the fallen are pilgrims who had given everything for passage to Skovos.
An inscription on the statue reads: "The twin daughters of Philios gifted Skovos with two traditions: That of the Amazons, to protect our home, and that of the Oracles, to guide its growth."
Nothing rests upon the pedestal. The shard is gone.

...the enigmatic Arch-Angel Tyrael bestowed upon us the secrets of the mysterious Soulstones. Tyrael bequested upon our Order¹ three of these Stones so we could contain the vile essences of the Three Prime Evils...

SNO: ¹ The Order of the Horadrim

Translation: Notes on the Characteristics of the Soulstones

When invoked, the Soulstones bring into being a strong "spiritual" vacuum. Any non-physical entities caught within this vacuum are drawn into the burning recesses¹ of the Soulstone and are forever trapped within.

SNO: ¹ Is a realm within the stone?

Translation: ...the Three Brothers found that they were immune to the effects of the Stones while occupying human souls. Sadly, we were forced to hunt down and kill the innocent victims...¹

SNO: ¹ Is it possible to exorcise a Prime Evil from a human soul?

Translation: ...Mephisto¹ and Diablo², once found, were easily lured into the Soulstones. The capture of their brother Baal³, however, became complicated...
...theorized that a mortal of strong will might be able to contain Baal within his own mortal soul.¹ To this end, Tal Rasha volunteered to contain the raging Lord of Destruction.

SNO: ¹ It all sounds so foolish as I write it down.

Translation: The sacrifice of Tal Rasha has kept Baal imprisoned for many years now... Should Baal ever escape, he would have the formidable powers of Tal Rasha added to his own.¹

SNO: ¹ How else can I ensure such this destruction never comes to pass?

Let those magi who are wisest speak true, and earn my strength: What moves the body?
Let those magi who are wisest speak true, and earn my strength: What becomes of us?
A handmade banner fashioned by pilgrims. Stitched into the cloth is the mantra: "Love your fellows, love yourselves, and love Akarat."

Among the debris is a torn page from a journal that reads: "Deeper reaches of the Undercroft were originally built by the Firstborn. Seems some of them were even buried here. Good chance that relics might be entombed with the bodies."
Each slip of paper bears a plea for help. One calls on the wrath of demons for swift justice; another beseeches the angels for their wisdom in a time of hardship.
The statue bears an inscription about the virtues all Askari live by: Life, Courage, Wisdom, and Unity.
The river takes, the fire answers.

SNO: Give of thyself, and be judged.
Together they bind flesh to land,

Translation: The beginnings of a dozen letters never finished: "...Lorath, I will be in Gea Kul for a diplomatic visit at midsummer...I thought of you again today unexpectedly...I have reread your parting letter more times than I should admit...Would you consider..."
Countless stab wounds mar the body.
A bloodied blade juts from the man's chest. It matches one held by another corpse nearby. Did his crewmate kill him?
A red X is marked on one region, with some scribbled writing. The only legible word is "Ailon."
A crooked missive written in blood.
Everyone was so loud but now they are quiet. I am alone. The bodies are dry. I need more.
Sturdy parchment bound in a leather volume.
The pages are damaged from seawater and blood
A gruesome collection of partially eaten corpses. Scraps of fine clothing suggest these may be the remains of the royal family.
A faded engraving from ancient times.
Only the worthy earn the Grinning One’s attention. Prove themselves. Now, they know true happiness—their bliss boundless. The Old One’s Eternal Gift.
A faded engraving from ancient times.
Only fools seek the Grinning One’s attention. Offer themselves. Now, they know true suffering—their torture endless. The Old One’s Eternal Gift.

My Bright Ray, I received your last letter from Alzuuda and the gold you sent.  I wish you would give up this mercenary life and come home.  Having you here is a greater blessing than gold.  I have kept Little Tuya safe –
A loose page from a journal.
Scrolls of incantations for the summoning of minor demons. Drawings resemble the four-legged demons in the canyons.
An expertly-carved statue of Lilith, covered in blood and viscera.
The remains of a fine stone statue, smashed to pieces.
Ogai’s jaw is ripped open, a horrid smile spread across his face. The jawbone is missing.
The body is dressed in robes identical to Ordun's. Large chunks of flesh have been brutally torn off, but the contents of his bags remain untouched.
A smoldering book wrapped in leather.
I, Andreea of Lakren's Overlook, offer a debt in exchange for my deepest desires. May this ledger be bound until my desires are granted, or upon my death, whichever comes first.
A crude Zakarum marker made of driftwood.
Towards the light where the remains of our folly wander the twisted paths, seek the high place.
A crude Zakarum marker made of driftwood.
Up the coast to where we watched our brave crusaders set forth to the western lands.
A stained scroll written by an Orbei monk.

In my dreams, a figure bathed in Light, named Izzoth, came and spoke words of great power. I have written them down and placed the scroll at Khotun’s Reach where only the faithful will find it. Seek the first trail marker at the graveyard of ships.
A sinister energy emanates from it.
You who have followed the path, speak the words of power given by the Light, and commune with the divine.  (The words are in a strange script and appear to move on the page.)
A vessel hums with the cursed energy contained within, collected from all the ills inflicted on the population by the cruel Overseer Salak.
Death and darkness infest this vessel. Overseer Hajar collected as trophies the souls of those they callously tortured and petrified.

This vessel conceals its true nature. There is little to discern one from another just by looking - only the faint scent of Overseer Kafan, full of their lies and deceit, would ever warn you that a curse was placed upon this curio.
A former local's personal journals documenting daily affairs.
An assortment of worn cookbooks. Recipes line the pages.
A few classic works of literature.
The body has been ravaged by being weeks in the hot sun. One of the many guards strewn across the marketplace, they must have fought so hard for their lives. These poor souls never stood a chance.
Looks like the City Guards put up a fierce fight and held them off so people could try to escape. Piled up boards, tables, anything they could find was used to try and stall the incoming massacre.

At the center of the map is the Temple of the Primes, an ancient complex buried beneath Mt. Civo. Notes are scrawled across the paper. They appear to be calculations for how much of Guulrahn’s populace would be needed to excavate the temple.
Sketches of three shrines, each depicting one of the Prime Evils: Diablo, Baal, and Mephisto. Below the drawings, Elias has written, “Only the blessed can open the way.”
The Shrines of the Prime Evils
Most of the pages are smeared with blood. The legible entries speak of the cannibals overrunning the city. On the last page, Oyuun has written, “She’s not coming. I pray that means she made it out.”
Filled with an assortment of knickknacks: a simple dagger, a few coins, and a lock of dark hair, bound by a blue ribbon.
An old damp ledger. Tucked between the pages is a folded note. Most of it is illegible, but you can make out a few words.
A battered and stained collection of pages.
This corpse was bound hastily, but tied with funeral charms honoring the dead. Blood stains the cloth and drips unto the earth below.

SNO: In the mountains, the Mother and I saw a village. The people, cold and hungry, prayed to a Light that would give them no warmth. But in her presence, a new fire was stoked in their hearts. They would never go hungry or feel cold again.

Translation: All brave volunteers are needed to help rebuild this broken world. Train under Lakren the master builder and help save Sanctuary.

SNO: Tools and coin will be provided.

Translation: The mutilated remains of several Triune.
The corpses of the Triune cultists sent to bring the Word of Lilith to these bandits. All valuables have been stripped from the bodies. A trail of blood leads elsewhere. Perhaps there's a survivor.

Brethren, the bandits of Onyx Watchtower are nothing more than common thieves, but they hold a location of extreme value. We will bring to them the Word of Lilith giving them a purpose in life and thereby swelling our own ranks.
A scroll of strict orders from the Abbot.
The Horadrim Elias and I are not to be disturbed for the remainder of our meeting, except by the arrival of Lorath Nahr. Should he appear, escort him to the Sacristy at once.
“You who would seek to know Darkness, kneel before the Light. Speak the words of the Litany, and accept our holy burden.”
A statue with a litany of Orbei Monastery.
Through the Day, I have prepared to accept this burden of knowledge.
A statue with a litany of Orbei Monastery.
From Morning, my eyes were opened and I saw the coming darkness.

Unto Evening, I shall keep it safe, and into the Night hereafter.
The goat thief's body has turned to dense salt. Large portions are missing, as if eaten.
A note left as an offering.
Though timeworn, you endure. Before your colorful kin, I say: Yes, I keep our traditions!
Shout your rejection, "no Mother of mine" at her towering statue in rift's hidden shrine.
Torn flesh and bite marks riddle the corpse. Jaw agape, they express both surprise and terror.
A rolled letter with Nekhii's parting words
Carved into this totem are various hieroglyphs and images of a large primate, indicating this totem celebrates the Elder Forest Spirit, Wumba.
Carved into this totem are various hieroglyphs and images of a large cat, indicating this totem celebrates the Elder Plains Spirit, Rezoka.
Carved into this totem are various hieroglyphs and images of a large bird of prey, indicating this totem celebrates the Elder Sky Spirit, Kwatli.
Carved into this totem are various hieroglyphs and images of a large centipede, indicating this totem celebrates the Elder Soil Spirit, Balazan.
Looking into the pool feels like falling in a dream: a sudden lurch of the heart, a cold kiss at the nape, yet the descent never resolves. The black void stretches without end.
With this gift, you shall always be safe.
The bone is singed. Smoke spills from its marrow. You can smell the heavy musk of rot.
The beast will use you, if you let it.
The scales are opalescent, mirror-like. And for a moment, you could swear you see something moving behind you.
I can see your fear. You would murder them.
Countless bodies. Angels, demons...all of them torn apart, burned from the inside. This is Lilith's work.
You remember this moment. Mephisto rescued you. You can see yourself, on the other side of the portal. You look so young.
A ledger listing numerous names and debts. The amount owed is extraordinary.
Tell Marcellus that we can only hold two here at once. Even if we had more cages, they're just too deadly.
A stack of papers, penned by an increasingly shaky hand. All promise payment once their luck turns around.
This Morlu corpse is recent, and bears wounds on its limbs suggesting captivity.
Short flavor text, the limit is 45 characters

Translation: The others who followed are lost, and only I endure. I will be the one to prove myself. I will be the one who binds this beast. I will be the one who dominates Laalish the Devourer when all others have failed!
Valloch, the familiar of the warlock Hattar, seems to have been waiting for you.

A grim offering. Wet blood runs from the corpse into the grooves of the pentagram.
This place was a sinking ship, and Ormus a rat hiding in its bilge. The mad feast in Travincal was felt from one horizon to the next, twisting every sorry sot caught in its gravity.

SNO: Until the Gidbinn, that is. Ormus gave it life—the ship ceased to sink.

Translation: This page details Mephisto's imprisonment beneath Travincal. In lurid detail, it tells of the ultimate failure of that prison, and the utter chaos that ensued.

SNO: You recognize Neyrelle's handwriting in the margins. "DON'T REPEAT THEIR MISTAKES."

Translation: Impaled on what appears to be his own weapon. "Heretic" is smeared in blood on the front of the armor.
Loaded with bottles, scimitars, cannon balls, sea maps, and more plunder.
Divine magic saturates the air, pooling together and swaying like frayed fabric in water.
A bartering station where pilgrims can sell their personal belongings in exchange for passage on a ship. The chests are filled to the brim with gold, gems, and other valuables.
Scrawled across the Barbarian idol is the phrase: "Only Akarat is worthy of our offerings."
Lorath took great care tending to Neyrelle. Horadric funerary runes encircle her body, and a Horadric talisman rests upon her chest.
A parchment nailed to the board lists the tenets of Akarat: "Love your fellows, love yourselves, and love Akarat. We are born of Hatred, and only he can purify us of it."
A cart laden with foodstuffs, clothing, blankets, and other supplies. The phrase "In the Light of Akarat we walk" is etched into the wagon.
A collection of handwritten papers, calling on common folk to come to Akarat's side. The pamphlets claim he can protect them from the darkness that plagues the world.
Power born of Hell begets Corruption.
The face seems younger, more childlike, than the one in the archive. Yet the body is that of an adult. Crude serpents are carved into the base, accompanied by the words: "No trespassers allowed."

An assortment of tiny wooden figures on a "map" of papyrus drawn in a child's hand. To the side are a list of rules, and two dolls labeled "Mother" and "Linarian". They look seldom used, despite the age of everything else here.
An ancient and crude painting of angels, demons, and human children. The name "Linarian" was written over one of the children, but at some point it was crossed out and replaced with "Rathma."
Page upon page filled with detailed experiments and studies of anatomy. Many of the scrolls are devoted to the study of creating figurines from clay and animating them with the spark of life.
Purge the hate from her heart, is written over and over on the statue. It seems to be a crude magical poppet. An attempt to change Lilith.
A riddle is carved deep into the stone: "I see all, yet know nothing. All of Sanctuary is beneath me. What am I?"
As before, another riddle is carved into the statue: "Sometimes I am the light that casts a shadow. Sometimes I am the shadow. Which one am I really?"
You cannot escape me. You cannot change me. If you cross this threshold, you shall know what I am.

Pages of well-worn papyrus, describing "waking dreams" of a snake-like being. The child was haunted by the entity's "whispers" and reflections in its scales. It seems some were things that had happened, while some were yet to be.

Caldeum, Kurast, Travincal? Backwater, Temis, some bloody Pools...? These locations are circled in harsh strokes. The notes in the margins attempt to chronicle your journey. "Wish Locran still did this," is written in a corner.
For the Wanderer o' Estuar. There's trouble brewing that will interest you. Find me in the abandoned city. There is a house marked with a red knot. -One of the Mother's Faithful
The statue bears the scuffs of travel, but someone has kept it lovingly free from dust and grim. Drops of blood stain her feet, both dried and fresh.
The cage is a rough construct of metal scraps, hammered together quickly. Its floor is slick with blood and sour urine. Nearby jars hold discarded flesh and rancid fluids that sting the eyes.
Lycus's contorted corpse, a wine pot fixed over his head. He was a victim of a tragic accident... not the Drowned.
A healer's tools. They look freshly used.
Herbs. Mushrooms. Organs. Not for cooking.
The blood is human. Dozens of victims. Somehow, it's still warm.

SNO: Have you forgotten that only a Bloodforged Sigil can admit you into your Lord's abattoir? Take greater care in your duties, lest you prove more useful as fodder.

Translation: Eternity. Ferocity. Divinity. These are the powers of your stolen birthright, dwindling in the blood of humanity. Claim the blood. Reclaim your birthright.
Hints about the skull of a powerful vampire that was reduced to only a skull, refusing to die. Feasting off of fear, its life force faded but power lurked just below the surface, waiting.
I've been summoned to the Tomb of Hallows! Master must be pleased with the wanderer I sent. Had a good feeling about that one.
Two barbarians, one druid, and a dabbling sorcerer...not nearly enough! Master needs more to join his Blood Seekers, far more.
Names and deeds of Lord Zir's lieutenants, referred to as the Ascended Blood Seekers. The tome shows months of work identifying and tracking their location.
Dispelled when struck by hazards. Unlocks Wardwoven Chests.
The way is blocked until the Trial is complete
Well-maintained but lifeless. No telling where it might lead.
Well-maintained but lifeless. No telling where it might lead.

An almost-familiar map. Though the geography matches the Sanctuary you know, many of the cities, strongholds, and major features are different. With some effort, you can discern the marked locations.
Amongst the rubble are broken vials, bone, and broken stone from the overhead pillars.
Scattered on the table are papers stained and brittle with age. Perhaps these once detailed magics from a world long past.
Corpses litter the floor, fresher than the athenaeum’s age. The burned bones indicate hostile magics caused the robbers’ demise. Thankfully they triggered wards before you did.
It seems this outpost was abandoned in a hurry. Various magical conduits are scattered about, abandoned despite their quality.
Conspiracy: An Account of the Vizjerei

Many Vizjerei texts speak of spirits. The scholars among you will recognize this for what it is: linen over filth. These were not spirits, but demons, offering the Vizjerei power in exchange for discretion.
This stone has a distinctive swirling pattern, with discolored streaks interweaving across its surface. If you were to guess, it was made from the shattered pieces of a dozen broken Tuning Stones.

Translation: An Iron Wolf, dead by stabbing. The killers struck repeatedly, desperately, inexpertly. Did the caravaneers do this?
A graphite sketch: a beautiful woman rises from a caravan's worth of bodies, and two armored figures bask in her light.
A map of Kehjistan, dotted with the caravan's winding route through the mountainside. Someone was tracking the caravan's progress.
An Iron Wolf, his throat slit, his limbs spread to the tangents of a ritual circle.

SNO: You can smell the acrid tang of Hell. A demon was summoned here, but it's long gone.

Translation: Telan's medallion, polished to a mirror shine.

Translation: A report from Soudeh. She notes Telan's bravery on the field and his expertise with the sword, but swears he will never be Captain. "He treats his comrades as tools," she writes. "These are the traits of a common mercenary, not a Wolf."
A battered training dummy, its torso slashed, its arms lopped off. Hundreds of hours of training, or one fevered tantrum?

Off limits! Anyone found on the premises will be arrested as Triune conspirators and sentenced under the Light. -Father Dymus, Priest of Zarbinzet
A leatherbound book marked by the sign of the Mother. One side is badly burned. Saved from a fire?

SNO: I know you've been missing Cerrigar. No one knows how to make skink, but one of the merchants was selling a Scosglen eagle. It reminded me of you. I hope it reminds you of the better parts of home.

Dwindling rations, soiled bandages, potion bottles near drained...sure signs of a losing battle.

Nef—take the stone to the bulwark walls. See what the mason can do to restore it. Be gentle with it, now! It's older than Eldhaime herself.
Not sure if you care anymore. But if you did, I've followed the trail of ledgers all the way to Yshari. That's where Cain's work rests now. -D.
Looted everything I could from that old Horadrim's hut in the Peaks. Place has been picked over, nothing but a sad old man's things are left there now.
[PH] This site is a place of reflection, to cultivate inner strength and resolve. Here we light candles to see the way forward.
[PH] A small sacrifice made in blood, but with reverence for the lives that it takes.

Translation: Although Lord Uacax was an orphan, he held great respect for his ancestors. Before embarking on his quest he honored them thrice. He returned with the riches of the earth.
On the day of his accession Lord Uacax followed the morning birds and they honored him with their song. He adopted their image as his crest.
A cunning beast terrorized the plains. Though Lord Uacax was untrained in combat he hunted and defeated this foe. He claimed the beast's weapon as his trophy.

SNO: The Butcher of Cerrigar, Garbhan is more beast than man. He has evaded our hunters every attempt to slay him. If traveling through The Harrowfields, be wary: he will smell you far sooner than you will see him.

While it is true that Blind Edlin is a story told to wayward children, there can be no denying the sound of a bell issuing forth from the Blood Vale. Whether or not the stories are true, be wary while traveling through that accursed place.

As dangerous as The Scar in the northeastern Highland Wilds is, the appearance of this cruel stranger has made it worse. Gaspar has overpowered any who have attempted to capture him, his fists wreathed in fire.
A gaunt figure has been spotted in the Dark Thicket, in the Deep Forest to the south. The possibility that the blood-mad Lord Eònan has returned from the grave is too dangerous to ignore.

Translation: Shorn limbs. Twisted metal. Acrid smoke rising from the corpse.

SNO: Legends speak of a barbarian warrior whose bloodthirst was so ferocious, he terrified even the cannibal tribes. Zarozar's spirit still haunts Desolation's Reach, searching for a worthy challenge.

A creature so merciless, those few that have survived an encounter with him claim he has a heart of ice. There may be some truth to this, as even the heat of the Boiling Planes is brought to chill he stalks nearby!
Do not travel through the Ashen Tread in the southern Scarred Coast without mercenary escort! A horrific demon calling itself Almunn scours the area for its next victim.

The Khazra Bhotak was slain by the Piercing Suns mercenary company, but somehow his ragged, bloody form has returned. Take extreme caution when traveling east through Wayfarer's Folly, for Bhotak ensures that name is well-earned.

Translation: Filled with various foods and supplies to guard against the harsh conditions.
A pungent odor rises from the pot. Some kind of fermented meat?
The burned bodies of goatmen lay in a pile. The unpleasant stench of charred fur and blood clings to the frigid cave air.
The grave of a fallen warrior of Bear Tribe. Their weapons and armor displayed proudly seems a testament to their honor.
Well-kept, but well-worn. The cold is hard on steel, as are the Khazra.
Exchange collected Midwinter Blight artifacts to earn Midwinter Proofs.

A long extinguished brazier, cold to the touch. Jagged words are scratched into the rusty metal: "Inarius is a goat."
“People of Kyovashad, the Light is in need of defenders. Those who join the Knights Penitent will be provided training, food, shelter, and a chance to cleanse your soul of sin.”
“Strong are those who stand in the Light. Stronger yet those who fight alongside him!”

The table is strewn with pouches full of sand. Scraps of paper are attached to each bag, and each bears the same note: "Father Inarius gazed at this sand and moved it with his awesome power. Three hundred gold."
The book is battered and torn. The words “Where was the Light when my girl died?” are scrawled across every page, making the original text illegible.
“By order of Reverend Mother Prava, blacksmiths shall now devote half their time to forging armaments for the Knights Penitent.”
“NOTICE: At the start of the new month, Reverend Mother Prava will hold a sunrise sermon in celebration of the Divine Advent, the day Father Inarius returned to the world."
Blessed are the Knights Penitent who stand at the Father's side, for they will earn a place in the Heavens.
Beneath the heavy tarp lie crates of vegetables and fruit, preserved by the frigid weather.
Clothes, books, and other assorted items sit in a heap. Many faithful have made the trek to Kyovashad to join in prayer or in battle.
A plaque at the shrine reads: “Take one stick of incense and place it in the fire. The Father will see your offering and show mercy to any of your loved ones that are ill.”
A plaque at the shrine reads: “Children of the Light, be not afraid. Pluck your finger and let the blood drip into the flames as a sign of your faith and courage.”
The wood is branded with a phrase: “Let this be the first step on your journey to the Light.”
“Take the fight to the denizens of Hell, before they bring Hell upon us!”
A place of prayer, maintained for locals and travelers. A fresh candle sits atop heaps of spent wax. The Light is never allowed to go out.
The official seal of the Cathedral of Light, cast in heavy bronze. The surface is heavily tarnished, touched by countless pilgrims at the end of their journey south.
Crowned by the Cathedral Cross, the great pyre stands as tall as any roof in town. Charred corpses of the condemned remain lashed to the timbers – a clear warning for all who enter Margrave.
Piled high and still smoldering, countless corpses await final burial outside the walls of Margrave.
Hooks, prods, and cruel shapes hang from the rack. Some look like old livestock tools, fitted for human captives.
Whatever creature fed on this man, it had claws the size of daggers. The people of Margrave have more to fear than bandits in these woods.
Citizens and pilgrims of Margrave - At the toll of the bell, all men, women, and children must assemble around the Pyre. Together, we bear witness to the wages of sin.
Beware! Many lives have been lost to this canyon. Some say vampires lurk in its shadows.
A pot full of old vegetables and lentils, but barely any meat.
The epitaph reads:  "We should have left this place long ago. I will wait till the ground thaws, you were a good man who deserves a proper burial."
Scattered notes and ledgers. The one at the top reads: "I've lost everything since the Knights fled from the vampires up north. My family is gone too. I am just alone amongst these drunks."
A merchant's neglected old crates. Many haven't been used in a very long time.
May the Light protect those who seek the light of Inarius. May you find peace while on your travels to Kyovashad.
If ye cheat while gambling, you'll be banned a month and short a finger. Twice, either hand, yer choice. Thrice, and you meet the end of a rope!
Knights who serve the light shall forever bathe in the glory of the heavens. Join today!
Crates of rations, dried venison, medical supplies, and strong ale—a garrison preparing for a long winter it seems.
The barrels are stacked neatly, with tight corks. The drink inside is clearly high quality and valuable.
The shield bears the scars of many battles. An inscription reads: "Faith in the Light shields against the darkness."
These rotting, stinking corpses of the undead are a grim reminder of the dangers just outside the city.
This bell looks like it was reclaimed from the Drowned. Taken apart and repurposed, its death knell has been silenced for good.

A game of chance in which players bet on dice marked with the four card suits (crowns, stars, snakes and lions) plus a skull and an anchor. Originally played by Westmarch sailors, the game has become popular in Backwater as well.
All manner of alcohol hailing from all of Sanctuary’s sunless corners, collected here. Even the dregs of society need a taste of home it seems.
Once a piece of shipwreck, now a jobs board. Runs the gamut from lost items to bounties on heads
Littered with countless holes from bouts of knife throwing. A blood stain of dubious origin trails from the dummy.
Tools, weapons, and clothes are of little use to the dead. Folks take as they please from these piles.
The table shows deep gouges, scratches, and stains, likely from games both revelrous and mutinous.
This severed hand still weeps blood. It was only recently separated from its owner.
A bubbling greyish-brown liquid simmers away. While aesthetically repulsive, the scent is sweet and vaguely alluring.
A fresh pyre prepared for those who recently succumbed to disease. It appears the people of Wejinhani still honor the dead, even if they can't be buried.
A carefully organized table of ingredients used in the creation of various healing aids. Moss, spiderwebs, bark…from the look of it, there is little from the swamp that isn't used.

Mother,
I'm sorry for disappearing after saying those awful things. I know it was hard watching me die in front of you, so I sought aid in the swamps of Hawezar. You were right. Nothing could be done, but I had to try. Please don't hate me.
Myfi

Elewka—Marsh Foot—Swamp mangrove oil, 2x daily—Full recovery
Nikoyo—Serpent's Chills—Beyond aid—Pyre burning set
Msias—Bone Mold—Removal of arm advised. Agreement reached
Zaita—Rotting Spasms—No cure. Make as comfortable as possible
A large basket of spike fiend quills of various sizes. The tips appear to be coated in some sort of sticky substance. Were these removed from someone or are they used for healing?

A tattered recipe book containing detailed drawings, diagrams, and recipes for different healing agents. The margins are covered in notes written in various styles. This book has clearly seen the hands of many generations of healers.
A rusty cage once used to hold deserters and enemies of the Zakarum.
A quintain formerly used by the Crusaders to prepare for battle. It has since wasted away with the rest of the fortress.
A statue of a saint of the Zakarum faith. Her name forgotten to time.
A statue of Akarat tarnished by time and nature. Surprisingly, the tome he holds is still legible.

SNO: Embrace the Light with all that you are and you will overcome any evil that stands before you.

Translation: All empty. Where faith fails to provide solace, perhaps drink is a handy substitute.
Worn Crusader helmets bearing no name or special ceremony. Likely a reminder of what happens when your name is lost to the Order.
Coin, fruits, and other small tokens fill the bowl. The people here are few in number, but devout.
Various maps of the Hawezar swamps covered in circles that have been crossed out. It looks like most of the region has been scoured.
The sickly-sweet odor of Hawezari flora wafts from the incense. Cut off from major supply routes, incense herbs must be foraged.
Moss and dirt cover most of the bench. Despite its age, the seat still sees regular use.
A lone lit candle sits amongst a sea of empty votive holders. Some still hold the faith close to their hearts.
Dog-eared and tattered, the worn pages show the precepts of Akarat. How many generations of Crusaders have read over these words?
The Crusaders who first settled here shaved their heads to stave off lice. The practice has since taken on symbolic meaning, indicating one’s piety and devotion.
These weapons shows clear signs of neglect: dents, chips, and gouges mar the metal and deep cracks etch the leather scabbards.
An old relief that tells a tale from the Zakarum faith. Its imagery faded and worn, much like the morale of the Crusaders.
Bandit gangs mark their turf in this city with flags. These colors signal one of the most ruthless crews, the Fifth Eye.
If there were coin, the Zakarum priests would distribute it to the poor and lame. As of now, it stands empty.
Freshly caught, and overly fragrant. It seems fish makes up a large part of the diet here.
Flies feast on a pile of luxurious fruits and cheeses casually forgotten by the wealthy.
It serves as both a barrier and as a decadent display of wealth.
There’s a good chance the contents would be considered less than legal in most other ports on Sanctuary.
The body hangs in a prominent place, where it can be easily seen and smelled. This corpse was meant to send a message.
What little meat is left on this starving animal’s bones has been stripped and eaten.
Strange bittersweet scents cling to the pipe. The substance inside is probably banned in other cities.
Drying vomit fills the bottom half. The stench is overwhelming. Disease lingers in this part of town.
Storms, raiders, and beasts alike prey upon ships coming in and out of the port. Those that make it back to shore frequently need repairs.
Priests hand out helpings of soup to the hungry. Prayers, conversations, and good cheer are shared amongst the community around this counter.
This forgotten corpse serves as a reminder that even though it is a beacon of life in a harsh land, death still surrounds the oasis.
The sign points the way to the healer. "All sick and lame are welcome."
Armor dedicated to those who came before and those yet to come.
A wish from a simpler time when these waters held magic, not bodies.
The plans are brilliant yet desperate. The armies of despair fill the small map of Kehjistan.
A small child's toy made from a grown man's nightmare.
Access the Pit and the Tower
After the body was stripped of anything valuable, it was propped up for target practice.
Streaks of red line the bottom of the bowl. Smudges of red powder decorate the outer sides, where it was handled.
“BEWARE! Your life is forfeit beyond this point. In the Fields, man preys upon man. Turn back if you wish to live!”
A fighter probably gripped these beads in prayer. Now, they lie in a pile of items scavenged from corpses for resale.
Available to all who need it, this stone is used to sharpen blades before battle. It’s weathered from years of regular use.
Abandoned armor of Knights Penitent, battle-scarred and soot-stained.
A young man of Tarsarak, convicted by the Knights and hung for all to see.
Provisions, water-skins, saddles, tents, and weapons. Tools of the trade for any desert guide.
An old Kehjistani banner, carefully restored. The gold-leaf script reads: "Long live Alcarnus, shelter from the winds."
Heaps of stained clothes, shoes, and other articles. Remnants of those judged guilty by the Knights Penitent.
Dwindling sacks of metal ore. With the mines closed in the south, such materials have grown scarce.
By order of Inarius the Father, anyone known to have served the demon Lilith must be delivered at once to the Knights Penitent. Those found giving aid to these heretics will face the Light in kind.
A ward constructed of cattle bones and twine, placed by the gate to deter evil spirits from town.
Those visiting in years past rung the bell to show their honor for the gods.
Not all those who venture into the crypt return.
The cabinet doors are locked tight. It reeks of decay and a smear of blood from under the door shows it's been in use.
The holy symbol of the god for which those who visit seek to find.
The pilgrims choose to leave their trail shoes and start on a path anew on the way home.
An old cart being used to carry the bones of those who died here many years ago. Each skeleton is adorned with battle-tarnished armor, signifying them as necromancers who died defending their home.
A chill breeze touches your ear as you pass the small brazier, and for a moment you swear you can hear the whispers of the dead emanating from within the brazier's soft glow.
A ballista used in centuries past to defend humanity from the giants that roamed the land. It is now used to defend against the monsters and wildlife that threaten Ichorfall.
This crane was once used to harvest ichor. It has since been destroyed by the perturbed wildlife in the area, possibly due to the presence of the giants.
Centuries ago, giants roamed this land. The death of the giant beasts resulted in an abundance of ichor. Humans have taken advantage of this by harvesting and utilizing ichor from the corpses.
Ichor is a valuable commodity in many areas.
A meticulously written list of "suggested" prices that seem excessive, if not unreasonable.
A collection of dusty tomes: heretical, exegetical, hermeneutical, and pharmaceutical.
The meager spoils of a day's work fishing. The basket is nearly empty, bearing only a handful of rotting fish.
An aged set of figurines made of various stones including obsidian, quartz, and jade.
A silent witness to the joys and sorrows of this small town. Once a memorial to the dead, now fallen into disrepair and disuse.
A worn sign reads, "HOLLOWS beyond barrier. All roads OVERWHELMED. Leave at your own risk."
A relic from the days when spirits were worshipped by all who tread this ground.
The lacuni destroyed Kichuk's farmland and slaughtered its livestock. It will take time for the survivors to rebuild their humble town.
With the bridge to the swamps of Hawezar now repaired, illicit goods from Backwater and their questionable carriers have a new route to trade.
Likely scavenged from a corpse. The children of Kichuk have no other way to make coin than by picking valuables off the dead.
Sometimes, a corpse is for the living. For these children who have lost everything, this gaudy display of violence returns a semblance of strength to them.
Cast bronze weapons and utensils, forged in ancient fires but weathered by time and use, now bear a mystical patina.
Lift your heads, beat your chests and drums: Harsus flees. Adorn yourself with smiles and cheer: the toad-faced demon was beaten. Raise your heads to the sun. Aya! Aya! Raise your heads to the sun.
Chili-charmed crocodile—fear vanishes in its savory spell.
Where life is found, so too is death. An inevitability that gives us strength and fortifies our resolve to continue on for those who cannot.
Musty, tattered pages read like a journal cataloging the Prime Evil's effects on Sanctuary, mentioning an unfamiliar magic called "Skatsimi".

Wooden talismans inscribed with tales of great feats of the first druids. These totems share the history of the druidic people of Sanctuary as well as their guiding precepts.

Various totems around Túr Dúlra mark locations for druids to stop and acknowledge not only the blessings provided by nature, but the road their predecessors walked and the hardships their people endured.

Translation: Tendrils of Hatred writhe and pulse around this weathered stone shrine. Perhaps something can be done to drive this corruption away.
There is no such thing as perfection. One fails, one falters. We must reach within for the Light. The Light does not falter.
If Akarat can find goodness in someone like me, it means all of us have the capability to find the Light within us.
A merchant may gain all the riches in the world and yet find crickets in his heart, chirping, yearning for something more.
There must be respect when discovering the unknown. Though we are new to it, it does not mean we own it nor immediately influence it.
Healing is not only from herbs and elixirs. Healing can come from within. There is healing in one's soul and spirit.
Every moment spent with my dearest friend Akarat was a moment filled with gentleness and laughter.
What is humanity if we are not willing to give a saving hand to a drowning man? Would we not be just as the creatures that plague Sanctuary?
Forgiveness can be given and received in many ways, but always must come with sincerity.
Akarat and I shared a love for the enchantment when discovering the unknown.
My spirit felt at home the moment we entered the jungle of Nahantu. It was as if I had found something I never knew I was looking for.
The angels in the High Heavens and the demons in the Burning Hells share the inability to find the Light. That is humanity's power.
The darkness can swallow you whole, encompassing every corner of your mind and soul. Though it feels the Light is gone, it will never abandon you. Let it guide you back.
Akarat believed that the purest hearts can handle anger, fear, and corruption.
Direction does not only belong to a map. We have a moral compass that guides us. To goodness. To the Light.
Malevolence comes from corruption, influence. Spirits will not be malevolent unless they become corrupted.
A storm will be turbulent. A storm will be tranquil. A storm is like finding the Light—a complexity to understand as it is.
The crimes we have justified, whether theft to feed a child or a bloody blade over words, find a path back to you. One must accept the consequence.
When one's mind opens to the possibility of future, that is when dreaming truly begins.
If I dig my soles in Sanctuary's dirt and take in deep breaths, I can feel the Light within me. We are connected.
We build towers to compete, yet the truth is they may both crumble if we cannot find peace.
He is like a feather—strong and durable, yet soft and beautiful. If we allow ourselves to be feathers, we can soar.
When you spend most of your life sleeping with one eye open, you find resting comes in other ways.
It is to challenge and to be challenged when the growth sprouts its roots in a soil of possibilities.
Exploration is the allowance of giving oneself to a world of unknown possibilities.
A wolf and her pup deserve the opportunity to love and live as any mother and her babe do, with no fear of chase weighing on their minds.
Lies spread fervently, like wildfire. Truths slowly unfold, like a sprouting plant.
It does not matter if thy family is by blood or chosen. Family is where you feel the most at home.
It is not only the tongue that spreads His teachings. It is our songs, writing, and dances.
Life can feel like air. Once a soft wind blows, it will never blow the same again.
There is much to understand about the human spirit, but it is certain that it is a magnificent discovery.
The body is barely recognizable under its armor. Broken limbs, punctured organs. This Knight was tortured, then slaughtered.
This table has been hacked to pieces. The remains of a homemade stew glisten on the floor, the serving bowl split right down the middle.
Here fell the High Priestess. May her memory be crushed under the weight of this city.
Something glints in the ashes—a half-melted coin, emblazoned with the head of a bearded man. His eyes look into yours with all the love in the world.
A Zakarum banner, centuries old, tattered but clean. This family must have kept the old faith.
The blood of dregs and nangari—each swimming around the other, never mixing.
A sketch of a snake, its scales carved with runes, its fangs bulging unnaturally. On the next page, a prison—circle upon circle of cages and the snakes trapped within.
Something ripples beneath this dreg's skin—corded muscles, convulsing in waves. You're hit with a sudden rush of nausea.
A dagger was slid between this nangari's ribs but the blood runs clean. No pus, no maggots, none of the dregs' telltale growths.
The emaciated corpse of a lacuni warrior. Her skin is stretched tight against the bone, her fur dry. She starved to death.
An old mining shaft, recently collapsed. Beetles and roaches crawl up from between the rocks.
This trough overflows with insect shells, their meat sucked out the ends. The lacuni must have been eating these, but where did they find so many?
Stones carefully cover his body, warded with Horadric runes. It is the best that we can do for him, for now.
Just as a leech requires a host, so do creations siphon from their creators until nothing remains. What are we, if not parasites?
Life does not exist without pain. I cannot spare a child from suffering, yet I can save them from it altogether. I am the end of this line.
No matter how steadfast the traveler, every compass needle waivers when finding true North. What will become of our children when we can guide them no longer?
The brightest light leaves the darkest shadows. Will the good in our children be eclipsed by the darkness that lives within them?
Strength and determination are admirable qualities. Mixed with the stubborn resolve of humanity, it can be dangerous if left unchecked.
Sanctuary shall never be peaceful nor safe as turmoil plagues humanity. A curse we passed unto our children from our own shortcomings.
Unlike Mother and Father, our time on this plane is short. Any moment lived without passion is a moment squandered.
Endless bickering is fermenting hatred in the hearts of the nephalem. They are so drunk on their own egos, they have become blind to the true source of their suffering: themselves.
As there is beauty in fragility, so is there catharsis in letting things go. If there is such struggle in maintaining this legacy of humanity, is it meant to be?
A father must hope their children can reach greater heights than he ever could. Inarius is no father, but a selfish creator who only seeks his own glory. Why has he forsaken us?
Wise, unwavering, and always seeing our fullest potential. Without Lilith to nurture humanity in the way we need, we would cease to be.
Passion and pride often cast problems in a favorable light, until it is too late to correct course. What have we truly made, in the nephalem?
The Daughter of Mephisto, slaughtering any who dared question the existence of her "children". She betrays her own for the safety of these fragile creations?
Though unproven, there is potential Lilith sees in her curious children. These "nephalem" must not be underestimated, lest they be our undoing.
Those who claim they cannot see "right" from "wrong" must also be blind to day versus night, to winter versus spring. Morality is objective. Any who say otherwise are fools, or liars.
Angels and demons alike fear our potential. What was once quiet pride has turned to reserved judgment. How long before their fear of us turns violent?
It seems a tempest is brewing in Sanctuary, and these may be the final moments of calm before it breaks loose. How much longer can this go on before it's too late?
The demonic blood in the nephalem taints their hearts. They are too eager to forget that the suffering of one is the suffering of all.
Humanity is nothing more than Lilith's hubris personified. She will never keep them in check, as that would risk wounding her precious ego.
Angel. Demon. Everything. Nothing. Humanity feels like a rudderless ship, guided by the passing whims of our creators. But what if we were at the helm instead?
What are we, truly? With the blood of angels, demons, and something more in our veins, are we not an evolution?
Dissent within our own merely empowers our enemy. We must come together to fight for ourselves, or else be torn apart by fear and pride.

Passion, when honed, can mark the difference between the victorious and the forgotten. Left unchecked, it tears allies apart before enemies even strike. We must work together in this rebellion or cease to be.
Immortality is a blessing and a curse. Perhaps worst of all is facing the agony of losing a child, without the promise of death on the horizon as a reprieve.
We are a mistake—conceived from vanity, selfishness, and a desire to escape misfortune. Humanity was not made in Lilith and Inarius' image, but to reinforce their vision of themselves.
