Four men run through the dark tunnels of an ancient ruin, chased by demons. They come to a massive stone door. One of the men, a terrified Zakarum priest, deciphers the door's runes to find that blood is its key. He and two of the mercenaries spill their blood to open the way, leaving behind the last man to the demons.

SNO: The three men now stand in a cavernous chamber. Suddenly, their torches go out. One mercenary screams, wounded in the dark. The other swings at his attacker, only to find that it is the last man they left to die outside the door. He lets down his guise, now taking the form of a tall, pale man. By way of unseen magic, the two mercenaries hang in the air. The pale man speaks the beginning of an incantation. Coaxed to an eerie calm, the priest completes the incantation, his own body floating to hang mid-air. The men's blood wriggles from their bodies to form a thin membrane. A fist pushes from the other side of the membrane, then bursts through.
The horned demon Lilith, Daughter of Hatred, rebirthed in bloody sacrifice, comes to stand before the pale man. He kneels in respect, taking her hand as he welcomes her home.

Sanctuary was never meant for humankind. It was forged as a refuge from the war between the High Heavens and the Burning Hells. Instead, it became a new battleground in this Eternal Conflict. A secretive group called the Horadrim has kept mortals safe. But now this once-powerful order is a husk of what it was, and Sanctuary's ancient creators have returned to claim the hearts of humankind. This is the story of their downfall.

A lone Wanderer travels on horseback through a snowy landscape. One night, their horse bolts away in a fit of terror. The Wanderer searches, but only finds the horse's mauled, half-eaten corspe. Tired, cold, and now on foot, they seek refuge in a small cave. In their delirium, they see a vision of a wounded wolf, its skull bared and inscribed with runes. They scramble to their feet, afraid for their own sanity.

Translation: The blood petals reveal a vision from the past. At church, Nevesk's priest gives a passionate sermon, shaming his flock for their daily sins. But one voice challenges him. The priest sputters and the crowd watches in wonder as the demon Lilith gently descends upon the podium. Her form is terrifying, but she speaks softly, like a mother to her children. She warns of coming danger: the return of the Lords of Hell. If the people are to survive, it is not faith that will save them, but sin.

SNO: The priest cries out, ordering the crowd to resist her temptation--but a woman strikes him down before he can finish. Driven to a frenzy by Lilith's intoxicating presence, the townspeople gleefully beat him to a bloody death.
A pale, hooded man watches the violence from a distance. On her way out, Lilith orders him to continue their preparations in the Dry Steppes. "Now our true work begins."

Translation: The Wanderer searches the small cabin, but they are soon interrupted. The hermit who lives here has returned. Lorath Nahr stands in the doorway, carrying the carcass of a deer slung over his shoulder. "If you're going to trespass into my home, rifle through my things… then at least have the decency to join me for supper. I'm bloody hungry."

Donan yawns as he sits working at his desk late into the night. Suddenly, he is shocked into wakefulness by the appearance of a doorway in his chamber, covered by a curtain of flesh. Donan pulls it back to reveal none other than the demon Lilith. She stalks into his study, cornering him. He shakes in fear. "What do you want?"

SNO: Lilith is clear. "Astaroth." Donan insists that Astaroth is dead, but Lilith knows that Astaroth cannot die--at least, not by his hand. She leans in close to whisper in his ear. "You have grown so frail..." She caresses his lip, cuts it open on one claw. She offers to make him the hero he once was. Despite his terror, Donan is resolved to deny her. He shouts out. "Away, demon!"
Lilith and the doorway disappear in a fluttering cloud of blood petals. Donan stands alone in his study, left with only the dreamlike memory of her visit and the bleeding cut on his lip.

Translation: In an ancient chamber beneath Eldhaime keep, Lilith ponders Astaroth's soulstone. She offers him a deal: if he will give her safe passage to a place she is no longer welcome, then she will give him freedom... and more.

SNO: She turns to face Yorin, who cowers on the ground. "Donan's progeny. His pride and joy. Your retribution..." She grasps the boy by the neck and lifts him, pinning him against a wall.

Astaroth accepts her terms. Lilith smiles as she holds up the soulstone, brimming with energy. She plunges it into the front of Yorin's skull and he screams in agony. Searing heat radiates from the stone, charring his skin and filling his body with fire.

Translation: Donan rushes through the smoldering streets of besieged Cerrigar. He wails Yorin's name in search of his son. Blood petals float down from the sky. "He has been waiting for you." Lilith's voice answers him--she stands atop a ruined tower. Donan demands to know where Yorin is, and Lilith orders him to come forth.

SNO: A massive demonic beast with many toothed and snarling heads walks out from the smoke. Standing atop it is the fiery demon Astaroth, freed at last. The stone that kept him still juts out from his forehead. Astaroth taunts the man that imprisoned him for so long. "He called out for you... wept until his tears became fire."
Donan falls to his knees, utterly broken. Lilith departs as the Wanderer approaches Astaroth, ready to fight.

Translation: The Knight Vigo stands guard at the Yelesna mines. A young girl, Neyrelle, argues energetically with him, demanding that he unbar the entrance to the mines. She claims to have seen a horned demon enter, and her own mother is trapped inside with it. Vigo is unmoved. His own Knights, trained professionals, are stationed in the tunnels. But Neyrelle is convinced that they are just as much in danger as her mother. Exasperated, she turns to the Wanderer for help.

The Wanderer strides into Inarius's chamber. The angel is massive, floating above the ground, his wings of light stretching out in tendrils to all corners of the room. His judgment is clear. "This is how you choose to approach me?" The Wanderer kneels in respect to ask him for his blessing, so they might cross the black lake and pursue Lilith. Inarius muses on his own struggle to end the Eternal Conflict and his banishment from Heaven. He lingers on the futility of Sanctuary and its mortals.

SNO: With fiery determination, the Wanderer stands. "I can stop her." But Inarius is unmoved. He dismisses them from his chamber.

Translation: Lilith stands over her son's corpse. She tenderly crosses hims arms over his chest as emotions come over her: first sorrow, then rage that his life, his future, was stolen from her. She doesn't know if he would've supported her vision for Sanctuary, but he was robbed of the choice all the same. She grasps the staff that impaled his chest and crushes it in her fist to reveal a key, hidden inside. The key to the gates of Hell. As she strides away, she makes a vow.

SNO: Your sacrifice will not have been in vain.

Translation: An offering table lies at the center of a massive ritual chamber. The Tyrant King Brol patrols the area, and Lorath hides from his gaze in the shadows of a corner of the room. Elias stands over the table, which bears an unconscious woman. He lightly taps at a tattoo needle to etch ink into her skin--a ritual circle of some kind. A massive cloud of blood floats overhead. A masked cultist approaches and slits his own throat. Blood spills from his body, then floats to join the cloud above him. Elias reaches to swirl the tattoo needle's handle through the cloud, siphoning blood into its chamber.

SNO: But Lorath has seen enough. He runs out from his hiding place and grabs the needle. With no hesitation, he plunges it into Elias's throat. As Elias collapses, so too does the blood, which falls splattering all over the unconscious woman. She awakes with a blood-curdling scream. Lorath rushes the panicked woman from the room, leaving the Wanderer to face Brol alone.

Translation: A wounded monk scrabbles across the floor, panting and screaming in his frantic attempt to escape. But the wolves that chase him offer no mercy. They sink their fangs into his flesh and begin to eat him alive. Lilith and Elias stand nearby, observing, discussing the coming of the lords of Hell.

SNO: Elias believes that if they are to be saved, it will be by Lilith's hand. But she is clear that she did not come to Sanctuary to save--only to empower. "In my shadow, the strong will oppose the might of Hell itself. Let the weak fend for themselves."
Elias kneels before her. "Andariel lives. The Horadrim die. Whatever the cost."

Translation: At the desert chapel, the Wanderer grasps the Sightless Eye, peering into it to see a vision of Lilith and Elias. She contemplates the return of the Prime Evils, noting that her father's essence is reforming. She feels it, like a thousand old wounds ripping open again. Now, while he is vulnerable, is the best time to strike. Elias encourages her to make her father's power her own. But she holds up a hand to quiet him--something is amiss. Someone is watching... She looks directly into the Wanderer's gaze and pushes them out of the vision.

Lorath, Neyrelle, and the Wanderer stand before an altar bearing a bowl of lit incense. Purple smoke coils up and out from the flames, diffusing to fill the space. Neyrelle wonders what happens next, but Lorath only answers that they must wait for the path to appear.

SNO: Time passes. The trio are lulled to sleep by the smoke, sprawled out over various parts of the altar. Lorath shudders in and out of groaning wakefulness. He catches glimpses of something strange... a massive form, shifting, slithering.
Eventually, Neyrelle wakes him. "I think it worked."

Translation: Elias stumbles back, injured and bleeding. "How many times must we do this before you learn? My life is not yours to claim." The Wanderer knows different, though. They reveal that they've been to the depths of the Sunken Temple. They know Elias's secrets. Taissa quietly laughs nearby.

SNO: Elias looks at his severed pinky as the realization dawns that he is truly mortal again. He growls in frustration and casts a spell, disappearing into a cloud of smoke. Taissa sprints after him.

Translation: I can sense your fear, father. Lilith stands before the gate to Hell, holding the key she took from Rathma's staff. The gates slowly swing open, bathing the Daughter of Hatred in glorious red light. She steps through.

The Wanderer peers into the Sightless Eye again. They see Lilith, still wounded, but standing tall as ever. She is meeting with Astaroth to collect on his debt. Astaroth questions her chances of victory, given her injury. But, cold and hard, she demands his compliance. Safe passage to the Cathedral of Hatred, in her father's domain of Hell: that was the deal. He bows his head in obedience, leaving to arrange it for her.

SNO: Lilith then senses the Wanderer's spying. She meets their gaze with fury in her eyes and her face fills their mind. She has caught them.

Translation: Donan lies on the ground, mortally wounded. Neyrelle, eyes red from crying, turns away to leave. She has watched enough of her loved ones die. Lorath wearily sits near Donan, who says he better not bury him here. But Lorath quips he's too damn old to haul his body out of Hell.

SNO: They speak of old men's regrets. Lorath says Donan should have turned to him instead of the Cathedral, that he would have shared Donan's burden. Donan says, "I know." He wonders how things may have been different, with Scosglen, and with Yorin. "Was it enough? Will he think it was enough?" His last breath leaves him. Only his corpse remains to hear Lorath's answer.

Translation: Neyrelle grasps the soulstone. With determination, she plunges it into the orb of Mephisto's essence. She struggles to hold on as demonic energy ripples through the room. He gives her one final warning. "You have sealed your fate..."

SNO: The soulstone now glows blue with his essence. A portal out of Hell opens beside her--one last gift from the wolf. "Let us pray that worked. Come on." But the Wanderer cannot leave yet. "Lilith will hunt us down. I must end it." Neyrelle vows to find Lorath, and to wait for the Wanderer at the chapel. She turns to the portal, where the Herald waits beyond. "This better not be the last time I see you, understand?"

The Wanderer nods as she turns and leaves. After a brief moment, Lilith arrives at the Cathedral of Hatred, seconds too late. Furious, she prepares to destroy the Wanderer. "You will learn pain only glimpsed in myth."

Translation: Blood petals fall inside the Cathedral of Hatred. Lilith kneels, dying. She laments the futility of trying to escape the Eternal Conflict. "I gave you free will... and you've squandered it... wasting it on a crusade you don't understand..." Fury and hatred contort her features. "Without me... you would have no... victory. And its cost will be more... than you can pay."

SNO: First, Lilith's body turns to dust. Then, every blood petal that surrounds her follows, becoming grey and ashen. The Wanderer is left alone in the Cathedral that was once her home.

Translation: At Donan's grave in Scosglen, the Wanderer hands Lorath a letter from Neyrelle. "I spent a lot of time learning this code, so I hope you remember how to read it, Lorath. Because you are the last Horadrim now." Far, far, away, Neyrelle travels through an icy wasteland, soulstone in hand. She trips and falls, dropping the stone, before scrambling to snatch it back up. The wolf watches her.

SNO: My mother would have wanted me to stay with you. She believed the Horadrim have all the answers. I don't know if she'd recognize this person I'm becoming. It's hard for me to think about her right now. But then I remember you and Donan. You weren't 'all-knowing Horadrim.' You were bitter. You were uncertain. But you were always true friends. That's what I hold onto because there is so much further to go. She sleeps on the floor in a corner of a dark warehouse, alone but for the wolf. She walks over dunes of sand, the heat of the sun beating down upon her. She sneaks onto the back of a traveling wagon under cover of night.

Your imperfection gave me hope. And we will need it to face what comes next. To face him... and his brothers. I don't know how much time I have, but there has to be a better answer. And I have to find it. Alone. I know you'll want to go with me. But people have already died because I was not careful enough. I can't risk you too. If I've misjudged, the world is going to need you to survive and clean up the mistakes I leave behind. Lorath solemnly burns the letter in a brazier. He nods to the Wanderer before walking away, leaving them alone at Donan's grave.

I know you don't want to hear this, but you don't get to quit. Not again. Wish me well, Lorath. Because if everything goes as I am hoping... We will never see each other again. Neyrelle pays for passage by boat. With soulstone in hand, she sails away over waters unknown.

Translation: At the Cathedral, Brother Iosef kneels before the Reverend Mother Prava, the leader of the church. She blesses him before turning to address the Wanderer. Iosef is dismayed to see them without Lorath, but the Wanderer explains he is busy with preparations to pursue Lilith. Prava had hoped for Lorath's help. But in his place, she asks the Wanderer to travel to Yelesna, where a demon sighting was reported. The details match the demon the Wanderer saw visions of in Nevesk.

The villagers of Nevesk offer their thanks to the Wanderer with ale and stew, celebrating and dancing into the evening. But something's not quite right… time slows down as the Wanderer sways and collapses, out cold. The food was drugged. The townsfolk watch in eerie silence as one villager loads the Wanderer's body onto a cart. As he wheels them out, we see the words of Rathma's prophecy overlaid on the scene:

SNO:
I saw my corpse,
and from my mouth crawled Hatred,
A father burned his children on a pyre,
and a mother molded a new age from the ashes,
I saw the weak made strong,
a pack of lambs feasting on wolves,
Tears of blood rained on a desert jewel,
and the way to Hell was torn asunder,
Then came a spear of light, piercing Hatred's heart,
And he who was bound in chains was set free.
-- Rathma's Prophecy

In a blood-spattered, corpse-filled barn, the villager forces a bloody concoction into the Wanderer's mouth. Odd visions of a horned demon flash into their mind. Suddenly and silently, Iosef, a man of the cloth, sneaks in. Unhesitating, he swings his club into the villager's head, killing him instantly. He yells at the Wanderer to waken--the townsfolk are coming, and they must fight if they are to survive.

Translation: Over supper, the Wanderer recounts the strange visions they've had. Lorath surmises that the concoction the Nevesk villagers forcefed the Wanderer was actually the blood of Lilith. It forged a bond between Lilith and the Wanderer, and gave them the ability to see visions of her. But to be bonded to a demon is as dangerous as it is useful.

SNO: Lorath explains that Lilith is the Mother of Sanctuary and that it is prophesied that she would return, though her purpose is unclear. The Wanderer decides to find out what Lilith wants, first. Lorath offers them his aid and suggests they begin their search in Kyovashad. "If we can't stop Lilith, we'll all be damned."

Translation: Neyrelle finally finds her mother, Vhenard, kneeling at the center of a sprawling ritual circle filled with demonic runes. The circle was started in white chalk, but transitions to blood past a certain point--Vhenard must have run out of chalk. She is relieved to see Neyrelle, but her voice quavers. Something manic hides inside of her. She explains that she opened the way past this barrier for Lilith, but she could not follow after her. She lacks "the divine element." Neyrelle tries to get her mother to see sense, to stop writing in her own blood, but Vhenard explodes. Her love turns to vicious anger. She whips out a knife and accuses Neyrelle of trying to steal her work. She vows to finish the runes in Neyrelle's blood.

Neyrelle channels dark magic into her mother's corpse. Vhenard rises shakily to her feet, so glad to see her daughter again. Neyrelle is emotional, desperate to save her mother from death, but Vhenard knows her spirit must pass on. And Neyrelle must move on too.

SNO: Vhenard turns to the Wanderer. "You have the divine blessing. Your blood is the key." She jerkily stumbles to the ritual circle where the Wanderer spills their blood. Magic flows through her as she opens the way, revealing a bridge over the black lake. As she dies a second death, cradled in her weeping daughter's arms, she says a last goodbye.

Translation: The massive suit of armor collapses down to one knee. The Wanderer unlatches the torso plates, which slide open to reveal Vigo inside. His body is pierced all over by the armor's inner spikes. The Wanderer is alarmed, but Vigo is at peace. "This was a just punishment." He asks after Neyrelle and is glad to hear she is safe. With effort, he wrenches an impaled arms off of its spikes and holds out a charm to the Wanderer. This was Vhenard's bribe to him. He asks the Wanderer to pass it to Neyrelle. "I should never have taken it." The Wanderer comforts Vigo as he dies, paying the ultimate price for his sin.

Donan is engaged in a tense discussion with his son, Yorin, when the Wanderer arrives with a message from Lorath. Hearing that name shocks Donan. "Has the old man finally come down from the mountain?" The Wanderer explains that the demon Lilith has returned. Yorin pipes up, noting it might be related to what his father saw. Donan hesitates before admitting that there was an incident at his estate, though it would be best to meet and discuss it there.

SNO: Donan turns back to Yorin. "As for your request..." He allows Yorin to travel to the town of Braestaig, where Knights Penitent have been stationed. Yorin is overjoyed to get his father's permission, and swears to be safe in his travels.

Translation: The Wanderer meets Asgail, chieftain of Braestaig. "Donan sent me." Asgail scoffs. "At least you're not another Knight Penitent." A nearby Knight takes issue with her comment. He asserts that they're the ones protecting her village. Yorin steps in to dissipate the conflict. "Let it be."

SNO: Asgail explains that a strange fog bearing mad spirits approaches Braestaig. But the Wanderer isn't here for that--they've come to ask after a demon that passed through. Asgail says the demon went uphill, to Airidah's domain, but that area is deadly. Yorin offers to take the Wanderer to Airidah himself. The Knight forbids this, concerned for the young man's safety. But Yorin insists he will be safe. "Donan puts his trust in this traveler. So shall we all."

Translation: Yorin examines ancient druid runes carved into the closed door. He haltingly translates some of them and discovers that a chant is required to open the way. Enemies approach. The Wanderer must fight them off while Yorin completes the chant.

Airidah sits on a cliff ledge, staring out into the fog. The Wanderer approaches to say that the people of Scosglen are dying at the hands of dead spirits. But Airidah is unbothered by this. "That is the way of nature." She believes the weak will be devoured, and the strong will rise to save Sanctuary from Hell. The Wanderer accuses her of believing Lilith's lies, yet Airidah is firm that this was her choice. "Lilith only granted me the power to do what must be done."

SNO: The Wanderer demands to know what Airidah gave Lilith in return. Of course, she won't offer this knowledge freely. Like everything in nature, it too must be earned. She invites the Wanderer to prove themself in combat.

Translation: The Wanderer returns to Nafain, who still hangs bisected and bleeding from a tree. He asks eagerly if the Wanderer stopped Lilith, but they answer no. She was already gone, and what's more, she left with a beast born from Nafain's own blood. He despairs at this news. He admits he told Lilith that Astaroth was hidden at Eldhaime, in exchange for the power to drive out the Knights Penitent from Scosglen. His fate, here on the tree, poisoning the very earth he called home, was not what he envisioned when he sought Lilith's aid. He asks the Wanderer for one final favor: death.

SNO: They grasp his spear and stab him. Nafain's wolf lets out a lonesome howl as he dies, at last.

Translation: The Wanderer returns to Eldhaime, where they find Donan gathering the bodies of slain Knights. The manor is in ruins after a recent attack by Lilith. She could've easily killed Donan, but she chose not to--he is convinced she's toying with him. Donan grunts in effort as he heaves the spear out of an impaled Knight corpse, pinned to the wall. He drags the body to lie beside the others as he admits the truth: he didn't vanquish Astaroth as all the stories claim, but instead he imprisoned the demon in a soulstone. Nobody knew this secret, not even his son. He built Eldhaime over the stone to contain its evil. That's where Lilith's gone: to the stone's chamber underneath the keep.

SNO: But she hasn't won yet. Donan asks the Wanderer's help in stopping her. First, they must find Yorin.

Translation: Astaroth's defeated form lies prone on the ground. Donan falls to his knees beside it. He tenderly grasps the soulstone and pulls it from the demon's forehead. The massive body disintegrates into ashen cinders, revealing a small human corpse. Yorin.

SNO: Donan weeps. He cradles the boy to his chest, shaking and grieving. "I'm sorry, my son. I'm sorry..."

Translation: Inside the tent, a massive demon's corpse is held up against a large cross, its limbs tied down. Lorath approaches and notes that the demon was clearly Elias's work. "But where is he? The answer lies in the stomach."

SNO: He plunges a dagger into the demon's belly and cuts open a gash. He roots around in the wound and pulls out what he finds. A noble's severed hand. A lone boot. A medallion bearing the crest of the ruler of Guulrahn--now, the former ruler.

The barbarians protest at Lorath's crass treatment of these artifacts of the dead. They say the dead deserve respect.  "The dead deserve nothing when the living are in danger. Now, Guulrahn has a new ruler and we have Elias to thank for it." He turns to the Wanderer and asks them to meet him in Guulrahn.

Translation: Lorath stands at a cliff ledge that overlooks the ruined city of Guulrahn. The palace, where Elias has run to, lies in the distance, impenetrable. Zolaya, a woman who sits sharpening a blade nearby, interjects. She knows someone who can get them into the palace, through a secret tunnel. But this person, Oyuun, is missing, trapped in the city with the cannibals that overran it.

SNO: Lorath is skeptical--he's not even sure the tunnel exists, let alone if Oyuun still lives. Zolaya shakes her head bitterly. "You don't trust me." Lorath says of course not. She's a thief, and it's clear to him she has some other reason to seek out this Oyuun.

Zolaya scoffs as she turns away. "Not your business." But the Wanderer steps forward and asks where to look for Oyuun. Zolaya answers with hope that Oyuun had a house in the market. Lorath tells the Player to try to come back alive.

Translation: Oyuun stumbles forward, exhausted, into the open arms of Zolaya. Zolaya is overcome with tender emotion as the two embrace. Oyuun thanks her for waiting for her, despite the danger. "Oh, you stubborn cow, of course I waited! Where would I go without you to tell me?" She gently cups the other's face with her hands. Lorath watches from a short distance, a sniffle in his voice as he turns to the Wanderer. "You're a lucky fool, I'll give you that."  It isn't often he sees two lost souls reunited.

SNO: Zolaya explains to Oyuun that the Wanderer needs help getting into the palace. Oyuun tells what she knows: that there is an old escape tunnel with an entrance in the caves nearby, marked with the Overseer's Cross. She thanks the Wanderer as the two women climb atop a horse, before riding far, far away from Guulrahn and its horrors.
Lorath watches them go. "I think that was the merchant's horse. Best not to tell him."

Translation: In the eye of a whirling sandstorm, Elias stands before Taissa's unconscious, levitating body. He taunts the Wanderer for leading him straight to their camp due to their fumbling in the Sightless Eye. The Wanderer demands that he not hurt Taissa, but he only laughs. "Hurt her? I elevated her!" Taissa's blood-ink tattoos glow as Elias explains their purpose: they form a waypoint across realms. A large summoning circle appears on the ground, radiating red light, and Taissa's body floats over and drops onto its center. Neyrelle runs up to her and begins dragging her body away.

SNO: Elias isn't bothered. "It matters not. Her part is done. Your part is done too." He walks out into the roaring winds of the storm, leaving the Wanderer to face whatever horror will next come crawling out of his summoning circle.

Translation: The Wanderer peers into the Sightless Eye again. They see Lilith, still wounded, but standing tall as ever. She is meeting with Astaroth to collect on his debt. Astaroth questions her chances of victory, given her injury. But, cold and hard, she demands his compliance. Safe passage to the Cathedral of Hatred, in her father's domain of Hell: that was the deal. He bows his head in obedience, leaving to arrange it for her.

SNO: Lilith then senses the Wanderer's spying. She meets their gaze with fury in her eyes and her face fills their mind. She has caught them.

Translation: The Wanderer grasps the Sightless Eye. Mephisto speaks in their mind. "Take it and set yourself free."

Neyrelle grieves Donan's passing. "He gave everything. His home, his son. What was it for?" But she is interrupted by the appearance of a fiery portal. The Herald of Hatred stalks out from it, pleased to see the Wanderer still lives. Neyrelle is immediately suspicious. The Wanderer explains that the Herald helped them escape Lilith's trap. But Neyrelle recognizes the wolf for what it is... Mephisto. "You trusted a Prime Evil?"

SNO: The Herald speaks without emotion. "Trust had no part in it. Your friend saw reason instead. As should you. If Lilith takes my essence, Sanctuary is lost." Neyrelle hardens. She asks what he's proposing. But he has no proposals--he only offers his aid. The portal he came through leads straight to the Cathedral of Hatred, where his essence lies, reforming.

Translation: The Herald of Hatred approaches the Wanderer inside a cave that looks just like the cave they first met the wolf. He offers to free them from Lilith's trap. But they are skeptical--they ask why Mephisto keeps offering his aid. The wolf speaks plainly. "Look where we stand. I saved you in this dismal little cave because I sensed you could end Lilith. And that is all I want."

SNO: He says that one day, they will be enemies--but for now, they need each other to defeat Lilith. "Look me in the eye." The Wanderer falls to their knees, paralyzed by Mephisto's gaze. Demonic magic passes between the two. "The path ahead is steep. My blessing will guide you." The Herald walks away as the Wanderer shakily climbs back to their feet, now blessed by a Prime Evil.

Translation: In Hell, Lorath pushes for the group to use the Sightless Eye, as he believes it's the only way to find Lilith. Neyrelle is hesitant--she knows that the last time it was used, things didn't end well. While she and Lorath bicker, Donan wanders near a pillar made of corpses. But suddenly, one of the corpses snatches him and swipes at him. It wounds him deeply in his gut. He stumbles away, clutching his injury.

Back in the chapel, shaken, the Wanderer tells Lorath what they've seen of Lilith's plan to consume Mephisto's power. Lorath takes a moment to think. He has an idea for how to stop her, but they'll need the help of an old friend. He scribbles out a letter and passes it to the Wanderer. "Deliver this message to Donan. He'll have gone to Kyovashad for guidance."

Donan and the Wanderer enter the vault's main chamber to find Neyrelle, hunched over a dusty tome. She startles at their arrival, scrambling up and wielding the Horadric Staff. "Who is he?" she asks the Wanderer. But Donan cuts in. "'He' once lived in this vault. The one you're trespassing in. Explain yourself." Neyrelle says she is a student researching the Horadrim. Donan is skeptical--he hopes that doesn't mean Lorath has taken her as another apprentice. But she clarifies that she is on her own. "I don't need a teacher to study."

Neyrelle emphasizes that Lilith is coming for Sanctuary, and she is doing all she can to prepare for that--with or without help. Donan doubts her ability to stand against Lilith, but decides to leave her be for now. He came to fetch something important from within the vault.

Meshif sits on the ground, badly hurt, as Lorath attempts to stop his bleeding. He greets the Wanderer gladly when they approach despite his wound. Lorath urges him not to talk, but he asks after Elias's fate anyway. With pain, he reaches behind his back to pull out a bottle of booze. He takes a hearty swig.

SNO: He offers the bottle to Lorath as he speaks. "Skewered like a quill rat. So it goes, eh Deckard?"

Aye. So it goes. Lorath drinks in Meshif's honor as his body goes limp, dead at last. After a moment of silence, Lorath tells the Wanderer he's taking the Sightless Eye to study it, learn how to use it against Lilith and Elias. They'll meet at the desert chapel.

Translation: The Wanderer finds Lorath out cold, lying in a pile of mud. Unceremoniously, they dump a bucket of water over his head. He groans. They remind him that he asked them to meet him here. With slurred speech, he says he remembers--he's just surprised they're not dead. They ask what happened to him. "I was attacked, obviously. By vast quantities of alcohol, wielded by my own treacherous hand."

SNO: The Wanderer cuts to the chase, and asks who the Pale Man is. Lorath is hesitant, but he admits that the Pale Man was once a Horadrim by the name of Elias. Moreover, he used to be Lorath's own apprentice. "He was the one who brought Lilith to Sanctuary." This revelation was what sent Lorath spiraling into his drunken bender.
Lorath wants to find him, figure out what else he's done, and ultimately, kill him. But first, he asks the Wanderer to find a woman who has some information for him.

Translation: The Wanderer stands over Iosef's corpse, conflicted. "He saved my life in Nevesk. They were not our enemies." Lorath grunts, exhausted. "They were fools... I don't have the time for it." He mounts a horse, which bears a cart carrying a wrapped corpse. He plans to bury Donan with his son in Scosglen.

SNO: The Wanderer quotes Lorath's own words back to him. "I thought the dead deserve nothing, while the living are in danger." Lorath chuckles. "Wise words. But I... I have a promise to keep." He goes on to say that's why the Wanderer must ride north ahead of him, to the Horadric Vault. If the Cathedral hasn't caught her yet, that's where Neyrelle will be. "Find her. Once you're together, meet me at Donan's estate." Lorath rides off.

Translation: Taissa, Donan, and the Wanderer sit in a small circle, sipping Taissa's brew. As time passes, the mind-altering tea takes hold, and senses become hazy. Taissa rolls on the ground; the Wanderer sits staring into empty space. Donan, though, becomes disoriented and paranoid. He hears his dead son's voice, even sees a vision of Yorin appear before him. Cut open by grief, he laments that he ever let Yorin leave Eldhaime in the first place.

SNO: Why did you let me go? Yorin asks. Donan quavers. "You were ready... you needed to go."

I did. And I do again. The apparition of Yorin turns to walk away, but Donan falls to his knees, begging him to stay. Yorin walks away for the last time. Donan falls to pieces, sobbing through his pain.

Translation: Lorath and the Wanderer kneel over Neyrelle in concern as she writhes on the ground. "It burns! My arm..." Lorath explains that she's been infected by the Drowned. He rushes to start a fire from driftwood and thrusts the blade of his polearm into the flame. "I must remove the Drowned necrosis!" Neyrelle is confused. The Wanderer cuts in. "Lorath, are you certain?" Lorath says he's certain she's dying. He ties a tourniquet on her arm. He fetches his polearm, its blade now red-hot from the fire. She whimpers in agony, clutching her arm, but Lorath pushes. "We have no choice. Hold her!"

SNO: The Wanderer wrenches her arm out and pins it down. Lorath aims his blade at her elbow. He pulls back, and swings down overhead with effort. Neyrelle screams in agony and passes out.
Lorath gently bandages her stump. "You will be Horadrim, young one. I will not fail you."

Translation: Elias, defeated at last, lies prone on the ground. Taissa hovers over him, but Lorath interjects--he must speak with Elias before she kills him. A crow perches on a nearby branch, watching their exchange, waiting. Lorath speaks to Elias like a father to a lost son. "Oh, Elias. Was all this worth it, then?" But Elias has no regrets for his deeds. He's proud of bringing Lilith to Sanctuary, of preparing to fight against the coming Lords of Hell. Something Lorath dared not try. "'Was it worth it?' That is a coward's question, Lorath. It suits you."

SNO: Lorath wrenches away, done. Taissa steps in and slits his throat. "The Tree does not forgive debts." She cups his face as he dies, gurgling, choking on his own blood. The crow swoops down and viciously pecks at his neck, severing his head.

Translation: Inside his workshop, Donan takes several deep breaths, readying himself to mend the stone. He jumps into action. "Mallet," he demands. The Wanderer passes him the tool. Donan speaks the Horadric tongue as he begins striking the stone, ethereal sparks flying from each impact. "Sulfur," he asks next. His striking grows to a frenzy as he yells out the Horadric chant. At last, with a final swing of the hammer, the stone emits a powerful pulse of light. It is whole again.

SNO: Taissa is amused. "Was it so easy, then?" Donan pushes back, saying she has no idea the toll such a task of magic takes. The Wanderer cuts in to dissipate the tension. Their next goal is clear: they must return with the stone to Zakarum keep.

Translation: The Wanderer approaches an open coffin that leans upright against a carved stone statue. They hear the whispers of the Tree. "Fear not this cradle... Colder beds than this await you yet, traveler..." They step into the coffin and the lid closes shut over them.

SNO: The coffin slides into the water. The Wanderer breathes heavily, faster and faster, as the coffin begins to bob. Their breaths turn to struggling gurgles, then quiet drowning, as the coffin slides under the surface. The Tree whispers a final message. "His debt must be paid."

Translation: Lorath, Neyrelle, and the Wanderer approach the Tree of Whispers. Severed heads hang from the tree's branches. Suddenly, they all turn to face the trio. Many rotting mouths speak in a disjointed chorus. "Why have you come?" Lorath answers that they seek a man, Elias. The heads hiss. They explain that the Tree deals in thoughts: it offers an insight, in exchange for a head. It seems Elias is the first to escape payment. Neyrelle asks what insight the Tree gave him.

SNO: A head answers that he sought the way to summon Lilith, but made a stop on his journey to a place beyond the Tree's sight. Lorath intuits that stop is why Elias has been impossible to kill, up til now. Another head rasps that that is why Taissa failed to deliver his head. The Tree points the trio to a coffin beyond the wrecks. "Find out what secrets linger there, for the Tree knows not."

Translation: Prava, ringed by Knights, opens her arms to welcome Donan and the Horadrim. "The Father will deliver us, together." But Donan angrily points out that Inarius seized their soulstone. To Prava, this was only the will of the Light. "How can you doubt us after everything we've done for you and Yorin? At least he doesn't have to see you like this."

SNO: Her insult, delivered with his son's name in her mouth, enrages Donan. He moves to attack her, but Lorath jumps in to hold him back. The Knights draw their spears, stopped only by Prava's order to stand down. She steps in closer. "Sin reaps consequence. I have faith the Father acted righteously." For once, Lorath is the peace maker. He points out that they share a goal: to stop Lilith. Prava rallies the troops to meet Inarius at the gate to Hell.

Translation: Inarius's voice echoes over the city as the Horadrim step through the gate. A battalion of Knights listens in rapt attenion as he vows to slay Lilith, as decreed by propechy. He orders the troops to rally at the palace. Today, they march on Hell. "And after that? Your plan?" Lorath boldly questions the angel. Inarius is unmoved. He makes it clear the angels have no need of the Horadrim. But Lorath pushes. He asks Donan to brandish the stone. "We don't need the bloody angels either."

SNO: The stone wobbles in Donan's grasp, before springing to Inarius's hand, pulled telepathically. "The hubris." The angel criticizes them for boasting of a mere fragment of what was once the worldstone. He floats upwards and away, leaving the Horadrim without a stone or a plan.

Translation: In Hell, Prava leads legions of Knights to battle. She steps barefoot through the fires, her feet charred, preaching in Inarius's name. The angel himself joins his armies, his light spreading to illuminate the masses of demons that await them. Prava kneels and bows in a show of utter faith as Hell's legions rush to meet her. Miraculously, she is kept safe by her Knights' spears and shields.

SNO: Inarius catches sight of Lilith and leaves to chase her on his own. She confronts him away from the fight. She asks what it is he's truly after. He is adamant that his place is in the Heavens. But she is skeptical. "Is that why you seek to destroy all that we created?" Inarius roars that Sanctuary is an abomination. But Lilith presses harder. "And our son?" Inarius confesses his deed, that he killed Rathma to satisfy the heavens. Lilith speaks quietly. "Tell me... did they rejoice? No? They do not want you." Inarius, enraged, stabs Lilith through the gut.

He turns away now, yelling out to the unhearing Heavens, demanding to know what he must to do ascend once more. Lilith stabs him in the back. He screams, begging for Heaven's protection as she pins him down and rips his wings from his back. She stalks away, leaving behind his smoldering corpse.
Outside, the battle still rages. But without Inarius's protection, Prava and her Knights begin to falter against the swarming legions of Hell.

Translation: At the desert chapel, the Wanderer grasps the Sightless Eye, peering into it to see a vision of Lilith and Elias. She contemplates the return of the Prime Evils, noting that her father's essence is reforming. She feels it, like a thousand old wounds ripping open again. Now, while he is vulnerable, is the best time to strike. Elias encourages her to make her father's power her own. But she holds up a hand to quiet him--something is amiss. Someone is watching... She looks directly into the Wanderer's gaze and pushes them out of the vision.

Everything started with Lilith and Inarius, the creators of Sanctuary. They each had their own twisted plans, Lilith most of all. The world's only hope was a Wanderer who'd been fed the demon’s blood. This bond with Lilith was the key to unraveling her plans.

SNO: Teaming up with Donan, Neyrelle, and Lorath, the Wanderer learned that Lilith wanted more than simply to empower humanity. She aimed to consume her father, Mephisto, as was being reborn in Hell. She hoped to claim his power—for Sanctuary, but even more for herself.

Yet Mephisto had his own schemes. He sent his Herald to help the Wanderer stop Lilith. The Wanderer pursued Lilith without Mephisto as far as they could. Into the very depths of Hell. And Donan paid for it with his life. Unfortunately, in the end, they were forced to accept Mephisto's help.
Mephisto wanted freedom. But Neyrelle imprisoned him in the soulstone, denying Lilith her prize. The Wanderer struck her down. And with her last breath, she warned of a dire future.
Without me, Lilith said, "you would have no victory."

Neyrelle set out to prove Lilith wrong, determined to bury the Lord of Hatred for good. But Mephisto’s corruption took hold. Luckily, the Wanderer found her and helped her to endure. Together, they found what Neyrelle had been searching for. The Tomb of Akarat—final resting place of Sanctuary’s holy prophet.
The Wanderer defeated Mephisto's Herald, but the Lord of Hatred himself slipped through their grasp...and into a new vessel. The body of Akarat.
Now the Lord of Hatred walks Sanctuary as a false prophet. Damnation in the guise of salvation.
There is no time to waste. Duty demands the Wanderer face Mephisto. The fate of Sanctuary hangs in the balance.

Translation: The souls of the damned cry out, struggling in inky black waters. Mephisto's spine, a series of jagged bones, breaks the water's surface, followed by his giant, monstrous form. Souls that clung to his body rain to the shoreline of a beach, splattering the ground. "All those who touch the stone meet the same fate," Mephisto declares to a tiny, insignificant figure standing defiantly. Neyrelle.

SNO: No. NO! I need more time! Neyrelle stumbles, crashing back into reality. She's in a library, countless books and tomes scattered about, while pigeons peck at the ground. She coughs blood. "I just need more time..."

She is not alone. Wearing the guise of Akarat, speaking in his voice, Mephisto taunts her. "Nothing in those scrolls will save you, Neyrelle, but I can." Neyrelle remains defiant, but Akarat sneers. "You've seen what awaits... But I can make better use of you."
I will stop you! Neyrelle cries, but an unseen force freezes her in place. She's back in the dream world, her feet on the edge of the cliff. Leaning back. On the cusp of plummeting.
Mephisto's smirking head looms before her. "You think you have power here?" She falls. Down, down, down, before—
CRASH. Back in the library. Back in reality. But the lines are harder to separate.
I could do this for an eternity, Neyrelle, Akarat's voice continues.

You're right. I am a part of you, Neyrelle pants. "I was trapped in your mind. You dream. I saw the sun, blotted from the sky. And the darker it got, the brighter the rage of man burned. Hatred would reign. I was lost, but in that chaos, I found your greatest fear. And I will tell everyone." Her hand slides over parchment, the pigeons pecking at scraps on the ground.
Oh child, Akarat says, confidence very slightly shaken. "What could I possibly fear?"
'And the weak were made strong. The pack of lambs would feast on their shepherd,' Neyrelle recites.

Mephisto recognizes Rathma's prophecy, and shows rage for the first time. But Neyrelle continues, undaunted. "'Then comes a spear of Light, piercing Hatred's heart. Razed to the ground by a murdered son. And the daughter shall mold a new age from the ashes—'"
Mephisto, in a fit of fear and rage, snaps Neyrelle's neck. On her lips as she dies is a small smile.

You could have been so much more, Mephisto says, disappointed. He sees, wedged in his side, a knife. Neyrelle stabbed him. At first, he laughs. As if such a act could harm him. But then he gets a closer look at Neyrelle's notes. Sees a sketched figure with a blade shooting a beam of light. "Oh, what have you done?" he asks, fear slipping into his voice for the first time.
Let them come, he says, hatred restored, as he sets the library ablaze. "Let them rise up, feeding the flames of unrest. It will not matter, for I am the light, and the way."
Meanwhile, pigeons with notes tied to their legs have been sent. Neyrelle's final message will be heard.

Translation: Over blue oceans, the Isles of Skovos come into view. The sun shines brightly as a sailing ship pulls into harbor. Much of the corruption on mainland Sanctuary has passed Skovos by, yet if you look into the distance, you can see that not all of the Skovos Isles are clean and clear. A volcano looms, lava flowing freely.

SNO: After passing under a stone bridge, two giant statues, one of angel and one of a demon, come into view. They serve as guardians of the capital city of Skovos. Towering structures loom behind the statues, the harbor between them. It's beautiful, and imposing. Like Skovos itself.

Translation: From a high vantage point, the Wanderer watches the Amazon Queen welcome Akarat to her shores. He addresss the gathered people. "The Pools of Creation, the path to a better future, is near. And by the grace of Queen Adreona, we will reach it!"

SNO: While the crowd cheers, Lorath walks onto the stage. He insists that Akarat is not who he claims to be. Adreona asks for proof, and Lorath offers only his word—his word as her dear friend.

However, when Lorath opens his eyes, he no longer addresses Adreona, but Akarat himself. Akarat's voice and demeanor has shifted—no longer the kind prophet, he speaks with Mephisto's voice. Rising from the darkness is Mephisto's true, demonic head, and its tendrils lash at Lorath. In desperation, Lorath slashes Akarat's throat, blood spraying as Akarat falls.

Except, it isn't Akarat. The vision fades, revealing that Lorath has killed Adreona. The crowd is wild, but Akarat calls for no more bloodshed. He kneels behind Adreona's head and cradles it, pressing his lips to her forehead. Holy light emenates and Adreona's eyes open once more, the slash on her neck reduced to a scar.

Now convinced that Akarat is truly the prophet he claims to be, Adreona takes his hand and rises. "Let him walk free," Akarat says of Lorath, "so that all who look upon him will be reminded of what hate can do."
An Amazon warrior drags Lorath away, while Adreona and Akarat turn back to the crowd. The Wanderer leaves, worried about Lorath.

Translation: The Wanderer finds Lorath's Horadric Talisman on the ground outside of an abandoned camp. In the sky, crows from the Tree of Whispers fly overhead. Worried, the Wanderer leaves the Talisman and runs, hoping to find Lorath before the crows do.

SNO: Lorath wanders the camp, lamenting that his efforts to stop Mephisto have been for naught. Crows circle him as he falls to his knees. "This is my fate."

Suddenly, the winds change. The crows scatter and a towering, familiar figure stands before Lorath. "Mephisto! No more damn tricks!" Lorath yells, swinging a torch at the supposed apparition. Instead, the torch is easily caught.

True holy light bursts from the figure, revealing white, lightning-like wings. The figure extends a hand, holding the Horadric Talisman that Lorath dropped. There can be no doubt. "Tyrael." Lorath falls into the fallen angel's arms, burying his face in his chest.
I'm sorry, Lorath says. "I've made a mess of things."

Translation: A howling gale whips across the islands of the Wanderer's mind. They stand alone, staring at a giant being, horrible bones and claws, tearing a hole in their mind. Lilith approaches, recognizing the being as Mephisto. He is linked to the Wanderer through Lilith. There is only one thing to do.

SNO: If you are to live, you must sever the bond, Lilith says, manifesting a dagger from a single blood petal. The Wanderer, reluctantly, takes the dagger, just as Mephisto's head crashes into them.

They fall down in darkness, hearing Lilith's echoing voice. "I gave my children a world. And the strength to make it their own. And all I have to show for it...is you." Lilith reaches the Wanderer, and wraps them in her large wings.

Fight, Lilith commands, while her wings disintegrate from the storm Mephisto rains down. "Sever the bond!" The Wanderer, with great strength, plunges the blade into Lilith's breast. "Take your birthright and make this Sanctuary yours."
She releases the Wanderer and dies, fading away. Her bond with the Wanderer has been severed, allowing them to escape to reality.

Translation: The Wanderer finds Adreona, back turned, silhouetted against a dying campfire. Her arms are wrapped around Lorath in a lovers' embrace. Crows circle, cawing loudly. The Wanderer asks for Lorath but Adreona answers, while blood falls at her feet.

SNO: The man never knew when to stop, she says, breathing heavy. "Damn fool."

She turns to face the Wanderer, revealing Lorath's severed head in one hand, her blade in the other. Blood from Lorath's neck continues to fall. The crows caw louder, eager to carry their prize back to the Tree of Whispers.
Adreona turns Lorath's face to hers, and with scorn, she declares, "A failure to the end." She tosses the head aside, turrning her full attention to the Wanderer. There is no saving her now.

Translation: Mephisto lies dying beside the Pools of Creation. "So much effort simply to return where we began," Mephisto taunts. "You, alone, just as I found you. You sacrificed everything, but changed nothing. I will be reborn in Hell, and you will be forgotten."

SNO: But the Wanderer is undaunted. "You're not going back to Hell."
The Wanderer plunges Lilith's reforged dagger into Mephisto's heart. Screaming in pain and anger, Mephisto is pulled into the Void, where he will be locked away for untold ages.
The cycle has been broken. The Wanderer has won.

Translation: The Wanderer raises a torch to the Tree. The white flame licks at the bark. The tree groans, nervous. And then, as if lit by accelerant, the fire catches. It snakes up the tree's side faster than the eye can move, up into the branches. The heads shriek. The crows burn.

SNO: I brought him into this mess, the Wanderer says.
No one brings Lorath into anything, Tyrael answers. "He made a choice. As all Horadrim do. I loved them for it."
Lorath's head is quiet. No shouts, no screams. He closes his eyes, at peace...

Translation: The Wanderer peers into the Sightless Eye, as if peering into a well.

SNO: Look, the Oracle says. "Do you see her?"
A vision of a hall of flesh flashes before the Wanderer's eyes, with Lilith's shadow at the far end. They peer deeper, as if falling in.

Translation: The Wanderer approaches Lilith crouched in the center of blood petals. The Wanderer attempts to rouse her, but her body disintegrates. Yet her voice, her presence, remains.

SNO: Your father walks Skovos, the Wanderer says. This gets Lilith's attention. With a small smirk, she realizes why the Wanderer has sought her out.
You need me, she says, looming over the Wanderer from behind.

Translation: In a dreamlike corner of the Mindscape, Lilith approaches an ancient doorway, overgrown with long-thorned brambles. Rathma's voice echoes from behind the doorway, an ancient and painful memory.

SNO: She reaches, tenderly, for the door, pulling from it a memory of a strange dagger. "I gave him a weapon," Lilith says. "He rejected it." As she speaks, the dagger she holds shatters to three pieces.
But, if it can be restored, then this...this is what will end my father's reign. The pieces of the dagger vanish back into the memory, leaving Lilith alone with the Wanderer once more.

Translation: In a tent, while she leans over a table of maps and plans, Lorath pleads with Adreona to reconsider her support of Akarat. "I know Akarat's tricks. He is death."

SNO: He approaches her from behind, slowly, cautiously. Their hands meet, and Lorath, softly, pleads. "I let him use me. I’m sorry."

But his touch is a step too far. Adreona grabs him by the throat and raises him off his feet, choking him, her face full of rage. "You call Akarat death?" she says. "Only one has ever left me bleeding out on the floor."
Lorath turns blue, his eyes rolling in his head. Adreona continues, "You are a failed guardian. Of your land, your people, your legacy. I won't be."

Tears well in Lorath's eyes, and she throws him to the floor. Without giving him a second glance, she storms out of the tent, leaving one parting message, "Stay on Athulua and condemn yourself, but I will suffer sparing you no longer."
Adreona is gone. Only the Queen remains.

Translation: Tyrael approaches the writhing mass blocking the entrance to the Pools of Creation. Instructing the Wanderer to move quickly, he grips El'druin, his sword, and leaps at the entrance. The barrier’s faces release unearthly screams as El'druin stabs into its center.

SNO: Angelic light bursts from Tyrael's sword, holding the barrier open. His grip on El'druin shakes but holds firm. "This is your birthplace!" Tyrael shouts. "Take it back!"
The Wanderer approaches the opening in the barrier, knowing that they haven't a moment to waste.

Translation: The Wanderer approaches Akarat, as he leads another follower into the Pools of Creation. The Wanderer calls out, "Mephisto! That's enough."

SNO: Akarat stops, turning to the Wanderer. Reality warps around them, and Akarat's voice transforms into Mephisto's. The demon taunts the Wanderer, until they can take no more, and they stab Akarat in the stomach with Lilith's blade.

They return to reality, with the crowd looking in horror as Akarat, stabbed, stumbles toward the Pools of Creation. He recognizes the blade, and removes it from his body, his disguise faltering. He tumbles into the waters, and from his body, the waters turn back with corruption.

Translation: The pieces of Lilith's blade have been gathered, and all that remains is to assemble it with the Horadric Cube. Lorath and Tyrael work in sync, reminiscing about the past and trading light jabs.

SNO: After Lorath helps Tyrael complete a pivotal part of the process, Tyrael remembers when he and Lorath first met. Back then, Lorath had asked Tyrael how it felt to become mortal. Tyrael muses, "You were compassionate.
You showed me how to be human. That’s how I knew the Order was in good hands, when I left. And it still is. Look. We’ve shaped the blade that will banish a Prime Evil."

Lilith's blade is indeed complete. They take a moment to admire their work, but the moment is short-lived. The Wanderer gets painful visions of their mindscape, corrupted by Mephisto. They collapse, Tyrael and Lorath coming to their aid.

Translation: In weary, aching silence, the Wanderer falls to their knees beside Lorath's body. Tyrael walks heavily to join them, head bowed in grief. "Your duty is done," Tyrael says, a prayer for Lorath.

SNO: The Wanderer's rage gets the better of them. "'Duty.'... He gave everything he had for it, and this? This is his reward? Betrayed and murdered! Damned to eternity on the Tree of Whispers! And all the while...Mephisto laughs, as we fall."

Tyrael approaches the Wanderer, and offers Lilith's blade to them. "Lorath would tell us to leave him here. To ride out with your Mother's weapon, and drive it into Mephisto's heart. To save as many souls as we can."
The Wanderer somberly takes the blade—they know Tyrael is right. Recalling Lorath's words, they say, "The dead deserve nothing...while the living are in danger."
Tyrael nods. "So he said. But we will bury him at least."

Translation: Sometime later, the Wanderer comes across a Lilith statue, enveloped in bright sunlight. Red petals, from a tree growing around the statue, fall at Lilith's feet. The Wanderer looks into Lilith's stone eyes.

SNO: She created this Sanctuary, even though she knew that all of it could be swept away at any moment, Tyrael muses from afar.
The Wanderer continues on their way, out of Lilith's shadow.
But she believed someone would choose to walk in her footsteps—someone would stand in defiance of fate itself and protect this fragile world.

The Wanderer stands at the side of a ship, sailing through the sea. They drop a few red petals into the water--petals that they had gathered from the statue. Then they look ahead, to their destination, Temis, radiant and bright. A new dawn, a new day, a new era.
You could call it madness, Tyrael concludes. "I call it hope."
There's a soft breeze in the air.
A blood petal rests in the wanderer's palm. It lingers for just a moment... before disintegrating into the wind. They push themselves up onto their elbows and sweep their eyes across the horizon.
Their mindscape is empty. Serene. And so quiet.
The wanderer stands. They are alive. And alone.

Translation: Neyrelle sits on a small boat chanting in the old Horadric tongue and clutching the soulstone tight. She sweats and shakes as she struggles to contain the stone. Black ichor leaks from it, staining her fingers. Concerned, the boatman offers his help. When he reaches out to touch her shoulder, she explodes. "Stay away from me!"

SNO: All of a sudden, she hears the voice of her mother, Vhenard. "Neyrelle! Is that how I raised you?" The stone hovers in front of her face. Neyrelle, chastised, explains she must carry the soulstone alone. Vhenard, now present, tenderly voices her concern that Neyrelle's burden is killing her. She cups her daughter's face and comforts her. "I'm here, little magpie. I'm so proud of you. But now, I need you to give up."

Vhenard's flesh turns black with ichor. Neyrelle starts with realization. "Of course it's you! You monster!" Mephisto. He pulls Neyrelle further into her vision, one where she is suspended in a web of blood and tissue, all her limbs pulled taut. "You made a choice. And I warned you, little magpie, there would be consequences." The sinews that bind her limbs rip them open, splitting each down the middle. She screams in agony. Mephisto orders her to surrender, but she fights fiercely not to give in.

All at once, she comes back to herself, sitting on the boat, her limbs still in one piece. She shudders as she calms. "Maybe you're right. Maybe I could use some help." She turns to face the boatman, but finds that he is dead, speared through the chest by a massive tendril of ichor. She holds back tears as she resumes her chant, takes up his oar, and continues down the river into Nahantu.

Translation: The Reverend Mother Prava addresses her flock. She introduces the Burned Knight Urivar who, like her, is a survivor of the battle in Hell. Urivar wears a porcelain mask that covers extensive burn scars. Another Knight leads a bound man before the crowd and pushes him to his knees. Urivar condemns the bound man, a mercenary in the service of Lorath, for trying to hide Neyrelle from the Cathedral's judgment.

SNO: Prava asks the mercenary if he repents of his sins. Desperate to live, he eagerly repents. Prava orders his release. But Urivar interrupts. "Father Inarius' mercy was great, but did he not also preach justice?" Against Prava's will, he riles up the crowd until they too scream for justice. The mercenary begs for his life to no avail. Urivar picks up a torch and sets him on fire.

Translation: Raheir invites the Wanderer to sit while he and his young daughter, Fayira, work on finishing a shield. The Wanderer asks after Neyrelle. Raheir reveals that she passed through town a few weeks ago, on the waw to Nahantu. The Wanderer is taken aback. Raheir knew that she carried the soulstone, yet he just let her go off alone. "You didn't even offer to help her? What is wrong with you?" Raheir tactfully asks Fayira to retrieve a tool for him. After she leaves, he explains that she is his adopted daughter. She and all of Gea Kul are a responsibility he's taken onto his shoulders, just as the Wanderer and the Horadrim have chosen to carry Sanctuary on theirs. "I will not trade one for another. Would you?"

SNO: Chastened, the Wanderer says no. Raheir respects their anger. "You care too much, my friend. But that is a glad thing." He offers his aid to them. Suddenly, the sounds of battle erupt from outside the workshop. Raheir grows serious. "They've returned."

Translation: The Wanderer watches as Varyana kneels next to Grelkar's corpse. She pulls out her dagger and plunges it into the body. With effort, she begins to carve it open. Curled over the corpse, she tosses out an organ here, a wet chunk of flesh there, chanting in a strange language. The Wanderer steps forward in concern. "Varyana? What's happening? This is... it's too much. You don't need to do this to yourself." Her response is hissed. "Don't look at me."

SNO: At last, she stands, holding up the liver. She bites into it and violently tears it apart. Suddenly, she seizes, taken by visions. "Zolmog… Tyrant King… crown of teeth… throne of bone… king of flesh made flesh…  Zolmog anointed in Guulrahn…" She shakes and pants in exhaustion as she comes back to herself. Her visions have set her course: "We go to Guulrahn. Now."

Translation: The Wanderer examines a doll while a creature watches from the rafters above. It shouts, "Leave!" The Wanderer demands to know what it's done with the boy. In a burst of flame, the creature hops down to face them. He is small, with clawed feet and demonic horns. "He's dead! I tore him apart." He takes an interest in a doll. "Where did you get that?"

SNO: The Wanderer asks if the doll is his. Warily, the boy approaches with palms held out. "It was a gift from Father... please." He snatches the doll and runs to a dark corner of the room. The Wanderer wonders where his father is, but receives no answer. Unable to leave a child alone, they ask the boy to come with them. He's nervous to leave. "You saw what happened. When I get scared... the monsters appear." The Wanderer assuages his fear, saying that they know of a place he needn't be scared. A place with good people.
The boy hesitantly asks if the Wanderer will be there too. "Of course I will."

Translation: A prisoner lies bound on an altar, surrounded by three bandits. The ringleader stands before the altar, holding a dagger high, poised to make a killing strike. But the Wanderer interrupts. "You're... bandits? You're cultists!" They say in realization. The ringleader threatens them, saying they're outnumbered, but suddenly, arrows fly out of the darkness and stab the two other cultists.

SNO: Subo steps out of the shadows. He offers the ringleader a chance to run. "Leave. And live." But the cultist chooses to fight. Subo looses three more arrows, killing him swiftly. He gets to work freeing the prisoner. The Wanderer is irritated he failed to inform them this was a rescue mission. His response is dismissive. "I assumed you were paying attention. And everything worked out fine, didn't it?" The two prepare to leave. But before they do, the altar bubbles with dark energy. It breaks apart in a mess of rubble to reveal a demon, summoned from the blood spilt there. They will have to fight.

Translation: The Hatred corruption melts away from the Akarat lion as he collapses, spent. Neyrelle rushes over to him. "Shhh. It's all right. I know you need to go now. You've done more for me than I could ever imagine. I promise... I won't forget. I promise I won't give up." She cradles his head gently. "It's time for you to go."

SNO: The lion dissipates into golden light, revealing Akarat's human spirit form. "When death first came for me, the embrace of the Spirit Realm awaited. But now.... Now, I am afraid. Remember this in the days to come... that, in the end, Akarat was afraid." Neyrelle tearfully asks if she will ever see him again, to which he says yes. His spirit fades away, leaving Neyrelle alone with her tears.

Translation: Eru, haggard and injured, walks out to meet the Wanderer and Neyrelle. Neyrelle demands to know what Mephisto gave Eru in exchange for his betrayal. He admits that the Prime Evil swore to spare Nahantu and the Spirit Realm from his corruption. "Even knowing I will never see it... I would not unmake my choices."

SNO: Neyrelle warns him that Mephisto always breaks his promises. "Just tell us what you did with the stone and the body. We can still make this right." Eru explodes in frustration. "There is no making this right." He goes on to say that he chose to break their trust, and every day after, he must choose to do it again by withholding that information. He doesn't believe he's strong enough to do that.
So he's come here, to offer the Wanderer and Neyrelle their vengeance. He prepares to fight, to die. Neyrelle fires off a bolt of magic at him. In his wounded state, it's enough to knock him out.

Translation: The Wanderer approaches the corpse of Ah Bulan, but Eru stops them. "No. I was the one who failed Ah Bulan." He kneels beside the massive body, singing a mournful dirge in the Nahantu language. He pulls out his ritual digger and begins to carve open the spirit's chest. The light of spirit magic emanates from the wound. He reaches inside, and with tender care, pulls out the glowing heart of Ah Bulan. He passes it to the Wanderer.

SNO: Eru places his hands on the once-great spirit, sobbing through the last words of his song.

Translation: At the stone pillars, Eru and Maka begin to chant in the Nahantu language. A magical surface shimmers between the pillars--the makings of a portal. When the Wanderer walks up to the surface, they see a reflection of themselves on the other side. Maka walks around the stones and grasps the empty air there. She suddenly drives a knife into the air. The Wanderer screams out in pain as their reflection is stabbed.

SNO: Eru coaches them to let the pain carry them through, instead of fighting it. Maka twists the blade and Eru pushes the Wanderer into the portal.

Translation: In the Durance of Hate, Akarat's corpse lies surrounded by statues of his Dedicants. The black ichor of Mephisto's corruption stains the floor and fills the circle, submerging Akarat's body. The ichor seizes once, twice, three times, before settling again. Now, Akarat rises from the pool, baptized in black sludge as he is born anew. Hovering, he opens eyes devoid of pupils.

SNO: Mephisto speaks. "Wrapped in the guise of man, I shall walk amongst the innocent. And there will be no salvation in the Light."

Translation: Akarat's corpse lays at the center of a dais, perfectly preserved inside the Vault of Light. Neyrelle approaches with the soulstone in hand. She kneels before him, hesitant. The Wanderer stands nearby in support. "You can let go now."

SNO: She turns to them, determination in her face. She places the stone at the center of Akarat's chest and a wave of light pulses outwards from him. Slowly, the tendrils of Hatred that plagued her begin to recede from her skin.
For the first time in a long time, Neyrelle smiles.

Translation: While the Wanderer gazes over the edge of the bridge at the dead boatman below, Urivar approaches from behind. He commends all that the Wanderer has done for the church--even though they traffic in darkness. He threateningly asks of Neyrelle's whereabouts. When the Wanderer refuses to help him, two more Knights drag in Raheir, bloodied and beaten. He's missing his right arm--all that remains is a smoldering stump. Urivar presses. "How many lives will you trade to protect Neyrelle? Is her life worth more than his?"

SNO: The Wanderer prepares to fight, but they are distracted by the sound of Neyrelle's voice. They turn to see a vision of her on the river, chanting a Horadric chant, protecting the soulstone. Urivar approaches from behind and suddenly stabs them in the back. "No one is above the laws of Heaven." He kicks the Wanderer over the ledge of the bridge and they plunge into the river below.
As they float down the river, we see a portion of Rathma's prophecy:
and from my mouth crawled Hatred,
A father burned his children on a pyre,
And a mother molded a new age from the ashes,
I saw the weak made strong,
a pack of lambs feasting on wolves,
Tears of blood rained upon a desert jewel,
and the way to Hell was torn asunder,
Then came a spear of light, piercing Hatred’s heart,
And he who was bound in chains was set free.
A short time later, the Wanderer lies unconscious on the river bank. An old man runs up to them and summons magic into his palms, pushing life back into their body. They wake gasping.

Translation: Inside the Vault of Light, the Wanderer thanks Eru for his help. But he only replies, "Don't." He kneels at the other side of the dais, dripping blood, his sacrificial knife on the ground. The Akarat lion roars as Eru lifts his head to show a bloody circle of ritual cuts on his face. "I do this for Nahantu. Spirits, forgive me."

SNO: Dark magic pulses through him and a rift opens in the Vault. Explosive waves of energy pulse through the room, throwing everyone backwards. The lion lies prone on the ground. As the Wanderer recovers, Neyrelle screams that Eru has the stone. He stands before the rift, Akarat's corpse cradled in his arms. The inner conflict is clear on his face. "You deserve better from me." But he turns away, to face the hulking shape of the Harbinger of Hatred. "I've done my part. See that you do yours." He leaves through the portal, taking the stone and Akarat's corpse with him.

The Harbinger stalks forward, larger and more monstrous than ever. The Wanderer screams in anger. He relishes their fury--their hatred. "One moment of betrayal and my blood sings in you. Few mortals are so worthy of their birthright. Come, child of my child. I will give you the violence you long for."

Translation: Neyrelle sits alone atop a pillar, crouched over the soulstone, chanting in the Horadric tongue hoarse and low. When she sees the Wandere, her voice quavers with emotion, though her chant never stops. The Wanderer is horrified. "Neyrelle... what has Mephisto done to you?"

SNO: The Herald of Hatred stalks out from the shadows. His form is massive, over twice the size it was before. "We have each played a part in what has happened here." He speaks of when they last met, in Hell, when the Wanderer left Mephisto's fate to Neyrelle. "You abdicated your choice to this child, and she has already been poisoned by the stone."

The stone responds to Mephisto, humming and floating with energy. Neyrelle's chant intensifies as she struggles to control it. "She will die before she surrenders. A wasteful outcome for both of us. How long do you think she can survive?"

Translation: Suddenly, a golden lion drops down into the fray. It roars menacingly, emanating the light of spirit magic. The demons that had attacked the Wanderer before are killed instantly. Eru whispers with emotion, "Akarat."

SNO: The lion turns to the Wanderer. "Only she can unmake her prison. Seek Ah Bulan, for he has strength to lend her."

Translation: Urivar stumbles back, drenched in his own blood. Gurgling, he hisses out a portion of Rathma's prophecy. He drops all pretense. "That fool, Inarius, dragged the Cathedral into Hell because of a poem scribbled out by a half-breed abomination." He turns his ire to the Wanderer next. "Then you escort that girl to our destruction and call it righteous. And you think I am the one who is mad?"

SNO: He lays down his sword and takes off his mask. Passionate, he says he offered the people order and salvation. He kneels and opens his arms in invitation for the end.

Translation: Neyrelle's chant is hoarse and low, her gaze unfocused and half-lidded. It takes all the strength she has left to contain the soulstone, which floats independently before her. The Wanderer approaches with the heart of Ah Bulan and explains that consuming it will free her. They kneel to her level. "Neyrelle... It's me. I'm here for you. You don't have to keep doing this alone." She gasps shakily, seemingly aware now. The Akarat lion steps near, offering his support too.

SNO: With determination, she grasps the heart and bites into it. She struggles to chew and swallow its pieces, gagging on the viscera. When her strength returns, the soulstone clatters to the ground, tamed once more. It hovers obediently into her outstretched hand.
The lion offers his back. Neyrelle climbs atop him, free to ride out of the Durance of Hate at last.

Another set of eyes, at last. We've been searching for Timue with little success.
We're hunting a man named Elias.
Dissuading. Timue is fated to direct people toward the Tree, but she knows it often ends in death for these people. It's her fate--but she doesn't necessarily enjoy it.
We think Elias made a pact with the swamp to become immortal. Taissa said you could help--
Taissa? Only she would be coldhearted enough to send a child to die out here.

Interrupting, annoyed. She has a tense relationship with Taissa--she feels Taissa has abandoned her. "Child" refers to Neyrelle. Timue knows death comes for those who seek out the Tree, and she doesn't want Neyrelle to die.
One of you will. That’s the way it always ends. Go back where you came from. I won’t have a child’s blood on my hands.
Cryptic. Making up her mind for the last part of the line--she doesn't want to send a child to her death.
I saw my mother possessed by Lilith. Driven so mad it killed her. I’m not a child anymore.
Considering this revelation from Neyrelle. Giving in, but not exactly happy about it. She's still concerned of putting a child in harm's way.
If this Elias made a pact, it was with the Tree of Whispers.
Considering this revelation from Neyrelle. Giving in, but not exactly happy about it. She's still concerned of putting a child in harm's way.
There are many paths to reach it, but the nearest is in Yngovani.
A sacred incense is kept in the temple there. Retrieve it, and your path to the Tree begins.
Taissa came today and I asked why she was away for so long. Years...we argued years ago and she didn't come back.
She said she was here two weeks ago. I don't remember.
I remember the swamp men. They danced with me. Taissa says they didn't. She says--I must write it all down.
I must remember. Even if there are wrong things. False things. There is Taissa. I must remember.
“Taissa said you traded with the swamp for long life.”
Yes. I was infected with the swamp’s poison, and I made a pact with the Tree out of fear. So now I give it knowledge, and in exchange, it keeps me one step away from the grave.
I wish it would just let me go, but a pact made cannot be broken.
A bit sad and forlorn. She isn't always happy with her fate.
The swamp is always watching. It knows why you've come. It knows each and every bone that has sunk to the bottom of the black mud since time began.
It sees all and more, and its wisdom grows with every fool who makes a pact with the Tree.
Referring to the Tree of Whispers
She was like you once, standing here in my hut, asking to be set on the path.
A little sad thinking about it. There is chilly air between her and Taissa currently.
And you will be like her—taking the answers you need and then never looking back.
What is so important about this temple?
The swamp nests in the roots of the Tree of Whispers, this is how each path begins. The temple at Yngovani rests on one root, but it is no less or more important than any other root.
Cryptic. This is in reference to the temple at Yngovani that Timue tells you to seek out.
These bandits will not leave well enough alone.
Subdued but troubled--she knows that an ill fate will befall the bandits who stole from her village.
We have lived peacefully in these swamps for as long as anyone can remember.
But now violence comes into its heart and it means to rob our god.
They don't believe us when we say the swamp always--ALWAYS--extracts a price.
The villagers, those fools, they wouldn't listen when we demanded the gems to open the temple. Death found them. It's the way of things.
Dying, but if we can try a faster read that would be great
But I hear them still, their warnings. Four of us are dead now, and I am soon to follow.
At the end of this line, the bandit falls over and dies
I think I have what we need.
Good. You found the incense. I'll keep it safe for us.
While you were gone, Timue warmed up to us. (laughs) Well, to Lorath. He's surprisingly nimble with old women.
(laughs) She says there's an altar, that's what the incense is for. It's not far from here.
Why do you think Elias sought immortality?
The ritual to summon Lilith would have been demanding. Perhaps he was afraid he wouldn’t survive it.
And I’m sure he expected to make enemies along the way.
Do you think Elias knew Taissa before she went to his palace?
Many things I wish I didn't.
(sigh) What a loathsome place to come seeking knowledge.
He must have thought he had no choice.
The door bears an image of a snake. Her eyes are missing—perhaps returning them here is the key to opening the way.
To self upon seeing a great door leading into the temple. It has the image of a snake, but the eyes are missing.
Hm. Only two kinds of people come looking for old Timue: those running away from trouble, and those running toward it.

Character note for these re-records: Timue is no longer forgetful. Her mind and purpose are clear. However, there is a bit of a sage/oracle-flavor to her. She knows much about the swamp and its power. Her fate is that she must guide people toward the Tree of Whispers who are seeking it--but she knows that will often end badly for them. A hint of sadness to her life.
Which kind are you, I wonder?
Can you feel it, wanderer? Like surf along the coast, the tides of Hell rise up, bleeding into Sanctuary.
Tortured Souls bearing Tortured Gifts roam these lands. Take those gifts, and use them to fight back the armies of the Seven Hells.
Vessel of Hatred: Bonus Rewards (Previously Claimed Tiers)
You should've just given up the gold...
