It was foolish to invoke Etsuk Supa without the idol in place. This hunger was supposed to make me stronger, not consume me.
I don’t know where to find the idol, but maybe...maybe if I can quiet the hunger a bit, I’ll be able think more clearly.
Weary, but sees a sliver of hope.
(coughs, wheezes) The purification...the transformation...this gnawing hunger...
Ragged, rough, physically can't handle what's happening to him.
My body...my flesh…can’t handle the strain.
Thank you, my friend, but I must return to the hunt. Farewell.
(groan of pain. discomfort rather than agony)
Etsuk Supa, grant me the strength to complete this task.
Together we will tear the khazra to pieces!
Finally! Let us fulfill my ancestor's dream!
Ha! I thought you'd never ask!
Of course! Let the hunt begin!
This is the boundary of my hunting grounds. Until we next meet!
My hunting range ends here. Fare thee well!
I can’t travel outside my territory. But return anytime, friend!
You pass the boundary of my lands. I must leave you. Bring me a snack next time, would you?
Please. Help an injured man repay a debt.
Bandits mugged me. Crushed my knee. I would’ve died, if the Iron Wolves hadn’t stepped in.
The one named Asyfa carried me here. She gave me my life. I want to give her this amulet in return. (sniff) Ah, a paltry repayment, but it’s all I have. She’ll be back at their camp, west of Caldeum.
A man in Tarsarak wanted you to have this.
Jilan? He looked too poor to pay. Guess I was wrong.
Not a bad piece either. Dirty, but no fake. Thanks, wanderer.
Depends who’s asking. For a foreigner like you? We’re mercenaries. Payment up front.
See, coin’s hard to come by since the plague turned Caldeum tits up.
Since the plague, yes. Wiped out half the city before they tossed out the poor, and us with them.
All that wealth, locked up to gather dust. Breaks my heart to see it.
Coin still moves in Kehjistan. But it’s the bandit scum in Gea Kul pushing it. Blood money, that. (spits)
I was a street urchin once, got into a bad deal. The Wolves saved my hide.
They raised me. Kept me fed. And the job usually pays. So for now, I stay.
What is this place? Who are you?
Primus, the communing pillar is quiet. I don’t know what has happened. We slaughtered the slaves like you said, but still the Three are silent. What have the faithful done to displease them?
Concerned. Speaking to someone in authority
No! Don’t go near it! We can no longer control – (pained screams)
Alarm. Shouts out to someone in the distance, then is cut off and attacked.

Ser Matias, stay alert. The Triune have been investigating the inactive plate by the Hell Gate. If they are interested, foul magic is afoot. We are trying to decipher the text. If you discover anything relevant to this, report back.
A grizzled, older Commander gives orders
Thanks. I hope they don't get used to it.
The new militia recruits have been training night and day. They deserve a little praise, but I can't let them see me as soft.
Mind giving them a cheer for me? Easy coin for you, a boost of confidence for the recruits, and I get to go on being the hard-ass. Everybody wins.
Yes! I'm not waiting until some gods-forsaken horror kills me! Hells, maybe this saves my life!
This vile-looking tar, huh? Well, here’s to your health...and mine.
(coughs) That’s not... (gags) This can't be right… (gags, chokes)
Please. I... I haven't slept in days. Is there anything you can do?
Hmm. Take this amulet, it will ward off nightmares.
I want eyes on the road west. Sentries at the walls.
The sinners will come running. Let none through.
Nothing to do with you. Stay off the road west to Caldeum.
Where are your demon-loving friends hiding?
You’ll burn. Lilith will lift up the worthy, and your ilk will burn. (spits)
Look at me. To Inarius, I’m gutter trash.
But Lilith promised strength. Freedom! Who would you choose?
Why would Elias want blessings from the Primes? They are his enemies.
The blessings are just a means to an end. Elias needs the temple, a place of demonic power where he can summon Andariel.
“Is there anything I can help with?”
Some of our finest hunters did not return from the hills. Became prey themselves when the fog came with hunger.
Now their bodies lay bare for scavenging. It’s wrong in all ways.
Frustrated. Angered by the irreverence of their death.
They should be marked with charms of passing. The rites of the Old Ways to see them to peace.
You’re well familiar with our lands, and as brave as those we lost. Could you see them to proper rest?
Though light fades… (cough) we do not disappear. (exhale)
(breathing heavy) Unseen, unheard… we are always here. (cough)
In memories… of those held dear.
Relaxed speech, at peace. Dying words.
“Fearing the death of her people, Airidah only brought more in haste.”
I would have held her hand. Showed her it’s all right. No one needed to die. We’re strong together.
“Airidah thought it was a necessary price to prepare for what is to come.”
Dad says you can’t reach the road ahead if you forget to mind your feet.
So… how do you reach the road if you lose your feet?
(sigh) I hope she sees the wrong now.
“A dying man spoke your name and gave me this torc before passing.”
A torc of protection. I make these for folk who travel the hills alone. Keep them safe with the old blessings.
Airidah said all death has meaning. But… where is the meaning in this?
Focused, earnest confusion. (Child grappling with meaning of death)
They were good. Kind. No different from me or dad.
Though light fades, we do not disappear.
In memories of those held dear.
Tell me, why did you murder that person?
Those like us have but one rule, never succumb to the demands of another. Demons are ours to command...right, Warlock?
It’s no mistake you witnessed this fool’s demise. I sought you out because I desire a student in the black arts. But so few are worthy of my gifts.
If you would be my disciple, seek out my sanctum and I will unveil much more. Come, Valloch, let us be on our way.
Ah, you accept my invitation. Good. These cultists you see serve me in my pursuit of forbidden knowledge, but they do so at their own peril.
It is well that you have bloodied your hands in these halls. It only reaffirms our bond as kindred: we suffer not the demonic.
Hattar, why have you invited me to this place?
I knew you could not resist my offer. I’ve watched you, observed you from the shadows. Your power over the dark arts is notable...but are you willing to be truly great?
(laughs) Come now, I would not ask you to break our edict. Demons must always remain our slaves, never become our masters.
What I offer is the knowledge to bind demons like the ones you see before you. My will alone sustains them.
I've sparked your interest, I see! (laughs) Go, take the Binding Stone, and we shall begin.
Excellent, you appear to be ready. The demon Ae'grom can be found in the Dindai Flats, the demon Laalish lingers near the Blistered Barrens, and the demon Abodian resides in the Forsaken Ascent.
The lairs of each are hidden, but the path you travel is ancient. The way will be revealed to you.
The lair is barred by a powerful sigil, one nullified only by blood. As promised, I provide you a way forward.
In the chambers beyond, Laalish has enslaved those like us. Now nothing remains but a fleshy husk.
Slaying these Sorcerers will grant you access to the deepest recesses of the halls. Beware, conventional attempts to fight the demon will fail.

To succeed, you must weaponize the demon’s name against the Possessed Sorcerer trapped in the final chamber. The binding can only occur after the host has been destroyed, a fleeting opportunity for you.
The Hellhound resides in a place most cannot reach, beyond a portal bathed in fire. To pass through requires a suitable offering be made in exchange for protection from the flames.
A fiend of pure malice stalks the Forsaken Ascent. Slay the beast and rip out its heart for your offering.
Well done. I have opened the way. Burn the heart in the infernal flames to ward your flesh, then you may yet bind the Hellhound!
I’ve done as you asked, sacrificed everything… I've nothing left to give you… Almost nothing…
It…has broken me… Its power will be mine only if I find a worthy sacrifice.
There is no going back now, I have succumbed to the demon’s will. The only way for me to know peace is to do as it asks, and I…intend to.
Know that if I fall here...my fate…the hell that I live…is your future.
No! No! I cannot! Will not! No! (screams)
(Speak the words of the binding ritual and begin.)
All these bodies. We’re serving the wargs a damn feast.
You did the right thing. She chose her end when she partook of sin.
Rise, and wear your burn with pride!
From flesh, to flame, to the Father’s holy Light!
My leg! You animals doomed me!
first line to merchant; second line to crowd
Lady, I told you. There’s no more room in the hold.
Please, you have to bring him with you! I can’t let them take his body!
No coin, no deal! You want a blade, you pay the price.
The Great Eye is silent, Athrpa. In your eagerness, you have become blind.
CYRA is a tired mom in this scene. She's been arguing with ATHRPA for a while.
And in your restraint, we are all blind. If the Eye is not restored, we will never see clearly again!
Farewell. The loom is set, and the weft runs deep.
Goodbye with a twinge of sadness. She is leaving ATHRPA and the PLAYER to their doomed fates.
Commanding. Orders to a group of Amazon guards. It's a small group and they are nearby, so she's projecting but not screaming.
You are known to us. Oracle Cyra is ahead.
Oracle Cyra, is there a problem with the Sightless Eye?
Since the Eye was returned, it no longer grants us visions. Its purpose has been altered forever. The loss is bitter, but this is not our end.
CYRA is hopeful the oracles can succeed without the artifact.
You would forsake it entirely? What of my vision?
She is speaking to her boss, so she can't be disrepsectful, but she is passionate.
I’ve seen many threads woven through your fate, and too many fray. I know your visions drive you, but this need not be your undoing.
Kindly and persuasive. CYRA has seen into the future and knows what ATHRPA wants will lead to her ruin. This saddens her.
You have brought the Eye here, so you do not mean to deny me outright.
(sighs) You may try awakening the Eye again. May fate lie in your favor.
A formal introduction would be nice.
(laughs) I have belonged to the wilds for many years now. The ways of court are long lost to me. I am Athrpa of the Oracle order.
Light chuckle. She's been so focused on her visions and mission that she hasn't had pleasantries in a while.
"Why do you live apart from the other Oracles?"
It is the best for all of us. They rarely agree with my views, and I’ve grown tired of their endless opinions. They are content wasting precious years on diluted visions.
A little heated and jaded. She doesn't outwardly hate the oracles, but she has been frustrated by them over the years.
I have no place among them.
You are very harsh on your order.
They drink from a cup already half-drained, and think it inexhaustible. The Eye’s magic flows in our blood, yet with each generation it wanes. Who can say if the gift will not vanish entirely?
A little heated and jaded. She doesn't outwardly hate the oracles, but she has been frustrated by them over the years.
No more questions? Then I shall go and prepare the way.
What is your opinion on Athrpa trying to fix the Sightless Eye?
Tread carefully with Athrpa. The first lesson all Seers learn is that seeking specific visions is ruinous. We are mere vessels for visions, not their keepers.
But…what if Athrpa could restore the Eye? Think of what it would change—
Do not mistake the Oracle's indulgence for trust. Lest Athrpa do something drastic. Think on it no more.
Why do you want the Sightless Eye restored so badly?
The Great Eye was bestowed to us by Philios the Firstborn and Lycander the angel. It allowed us to see fate without a great loss of youth and search for specific visions.
After it was stolen, our sight dimmed. Now the artifact does not heed us.
Frustrated that the Eye doesn't work for the oracles anymore.
Only the Eye can unlock my visions. Should I not give all to restore it back?
What are these visions of yours?
If only I knew myself. When I close my eyes, when I dream, I see fire. Eyes. A hunger unsated. But I cannot make sense of it. The Eye would show me all.
Dejected and tired at "If only I knew myself." When recounting parts of her vision, she emphasizes words.
I’ve spent my years naturally studying the oracles of old. The First Oracle documented the Great Eye first awakening. Here, read it for yourself.
Emphasis of "years naturally." Most oracles rapidly age themselves by using their magic. ATHRPA has refused to do that.
The writings speak of the Temple of Life, but the text is incomplete.
That text was copied from a tablet beneath the Temple of Life, where the Great Eye was first awakened. That is where I must go. I would gratefully accept any help you could offer.
Sincere asking the PLAYER for help.
No one has stepped into that chamber since before Queen Xaera’s reign. This is not the time, Athrpa.
No one is asking you to enter, Linos.
We need to get inside this chamber.
So, you've been dragged into this as well? I can see your minds are made up. Stubborn as ever.
First sentence is addressing the PLAYER. LINOS is begrudgingly being helpful.
Take the key, but mind the door behind you. It was sealed for good reason. The dead do not always have the courtesy to stay buried.

Athrpa has lived in that western alcove since before I became lead archivist. She used to spend hours in the archives. People can live their whole lives without ever seeing a member of the order but she walks among us. I always appreciated that.
LINOS is genuinely fond of ATHRPA and speaks about her kindly.
Just don’t play her in astragaloi. (chuckles) She’ll rob you blind.
The Eye stirs them! Strike before they gather form!
A combat bark. Rallying allies to act immediately.
The Eye will stir them again if we linger.
The fighting is over, but the danger is not. ATHRPA fought with the PLAYER, so she might be a little breathless.
What is your plan beyond this door?
This Temple was once used as a proving ground for young Seers. Inside lies the Chamber of Calling where a trial was held to test those with sight.
We must pass that trial to access the writings concerning the Eye.
I'm still with you. Where to now?
I am going to Vision’s End to figure out what to do next. Find me there.
Everyone is telling you to give up this quest for the Sightless Eye. Maybe you should listen.
Spoken like someone who can choose to walk away. The visions will not end. I did not ask for sight. I am a Seer because my mother was one, and her mother’s mothers.
Only fools think this is a gift. To sense, but not see. To know, but not understand. I need to see all! I’ll go mad if I don’t.
Tell me about Lycander the angel.

Every child on Skovos knows the legends of Lycander, the angel who rebelled against the heavens and came to Sanctuary. She returned to the heavens to protect the knowledge of our existence, so the stories say.
The air hums. Like a breath held for centuries. It’s waiting. Watching.
Soft and reverent. Sensing an ancient, unseen presence. More awe than fear.
This is the Chamber of Calling. All who enter here are measured.
Solemn authority and clear projection. It is likely to trigger in combat, so it can have more projection than a 1-1 conversation.
You've never done this trial before? How are Seers tested now?
Without the Great Eye, the old ways became unnecessary. Our visions are less intense now, so the trials became gentler.
I wonder how many of us would still wear the title of Seer if this was the test we faced.
What is this 'Chamber of Calling' exactly?
Young Seers were once brought here. The trial awakened their sight. If they could not withstand their first vision, they were culled. It was a mercy.
As First Oracle Seryn wrote, "We must be able to command the visions, not merely see."
I have always wondered if I would endure.
Soft and reflective. She is genuinely unsure
The well runs deep, and I am its cup. Pour me out, and see what remains.
Soft and deliberate, like a practiced prayer. She says to herself to steady herself before the trial.
I will endure. I will remain. Let it pass. Through me. Over me.
Tense and resolute. Spoken through clenched teeth trying to control her breath. ATHRPA is in pain.
Breathless after combat/trial. She is amazed she successfully passed the trial
Now, can we find the writings you seek?
The deeper oracle archive lies ahead. Come.
Failed Seers. Shades without sight. They linger here bound to their trials. The Sightless Eye calls to them...or perhaps they call to it.
ATHRPA is forlorn for the dead.
This should be the archive. It is said Lycander herself graced these halls.
Another locked door? Is this another trial?
This seal is bound by our wards—woven to deny outsiders. It may be undone by drawing the proper sign. I will show you the pattern—watch my hand and mirror it.
Let us look for the First Oracle’s writings. But tread lightly. This place remembers.
These writings speak of invoking Lycander's name in the presence of the Sightless Eye.
Could it be so easy to awaken it? There is enough divine magic left in this place for one last ritual. Let us try.

...Thus did Philios, our father, set down this Rite. Stand before the Great Eye and channel the divine into its heart until it stirs. Speak the name of Lycander, who my father once loved. The Eye will awaken to the worthy.

...In time, all who gaze into the Great Eye unravel. Even my own sister Seryn cannot tell reality from vision anymore. She looked too deeply into the well and found herself lost. Her successor has been named...
By the sight beyond sight. By the Great Eye. Hear me!
Commanding an artifact to heed her
Rest spirits! Your time has passed!
I hear you mortal. Speak your purpose.
You invoke the Burning Hells too lightly, mortal. Words are not hollow here. Choose yours with more care.
There was once a time your kind bowed to neither angel nor demon. I would not see that change. But speak quickly. The magic wanes.
Warmer and softer than her normal commanding tone. She has a love for humankind. Goes back to normal when saying "But speak quickly..."
Elder one, we seek to restore the Sightless Eye. We have shrouded visions without it. If we cannot see fully, we cannot protect ourselves.
You are trying to command that which was never meant for you. What you call the Sightless Eye will only answer to the one who created it. He put the Eye to rest long ago. As should you.
You have heard Heaven’s council. The veil closes. Be free from this burden.
Pleading with Lycander, who is no longer present
There's not enough magic left here to do it again...
What can help awaken the Sightless Eye here?

We depleted the divine magic in the Temple of Life, but there may be another source to awaken the Eye. The tales say Philios first locked the Sightless Eye in a vault close by. Where it is, I do not know.
Another of my order, Laurel, has had visions related to Philios. I hope she has seen where the vault lies. Let us seek her.
A warm, excited greeting. She hasn't seen her friend in many years.
She says the name fondly, but is saddened that her friend has magically aged so much. She urges Laurel not to exert herself.
Elder, Athrpa says you have had visions concerning Philios. We need to find his vault.
Elder? Athrpa is the old one! Oh, the mischiefs we had in our youth. Don’t tell me you are still obsessed with that one vision.
Light-hearted, then sobers and becomes more serious when talking about her friend's vision obsession.
All of my visions were chronicled. I did not see Philios himself, but I saw two children fleeing a father. By accident, they stumbled across an ancient place. The full vision lies over there.
Two. Your mind is muddled from visions.
(laughs) You’ve been away too long. I hope you’ll come back for my last vision.
Flesh can only bear so much. At our last vision, our bodies surrender. The ceremony for our passing is called the Rhysis Nematou. The Severing of the Thread.
I am the last of our year to be severed…save Athrpa, of course.
Don’t have the vision until I return. I will set all right with the Eye.

Dear heart, my life has been full. I have walked many paths, lived many lives through the visions. I wish you could set aside your stubbornness and taste this same fulfillment. Do not dig forever in the earth when you could lift your eyes to the stars.
The vision account mentions the base of the waterfall. Let's begin there.
The path is laid, and so we must follow.
I’m glad to be away. I always dread coming back to this place.
Why do you hate coming back here so much?
Seeing Laurel like that…it isn’t fair. The visions are cruel things. Most children’s first memories are of their parents. Mine are of flame and ruin.
Ugh, why am I even saying this? I need to stay steadfast.
Pushing down her vulnerability and refocusing on her mission.
This is the waterfall. Philios’ vault must be near. Let the Eye lead our steps.
These must be the children from Laurel’s vision. I am sorry, little ones. Your death will have meaning.
There is strong magic here. My hair is standing on end.
Here is the intended resting place of the Sightless Eye. It feels steadier here. Like it remembers.
Are you going to do a ritual similar to the Temple of Life?
There isn’t enough magic in this chamber to do the same ritual. I feel the magic elsewhere in this vault. Tangled and knotted from unuse. I need to collect it to do the ritual again.
(inhales) Blood for binding, breath for sight.
Let us find the rest of the magic.
I feel magic ahead. A deep well waits for us.
Be reborn once again through me.
Is the magic hurting you? Perhaps you should rest.
This burden is mine alone. Pain is a small price to see my vision. I continue.
Through gritted teeth. She is in pain but is pushing past it.

Today marks the anniversary of our father’s death—the world still feels colder without him. Father would be proud that we have made Skovos our home. But he might feel differently about the fate of his Eye. Seryn and I have slipped into the vault to reclaim the Great Eye. She hopes it will help us against the encroaching dark.
The magic has knotted. We need to untangle it.
In pain and fighting through it.
Raw and sharp from sudden pain
I sense the last well ahead.
You look pale. What happens now?
I am going to force this power into the Eye until it awakens again. Let us return to the chamber where we began.
Determined. Remnants of exhaustion and pain still left over.

...The Eye holds wonders beneath its surface. Future memories not my own, as vivid as one of Mother’s story tapestries. With practice, I have learned to shape its gaze. I have looked so far beyond tomorrow that I beheld the end of all things and the silence beyond.
How do we infuse the collected magic into the Eye?
As in the Temple of Life, I will channel the magic into the Eye. I need a steady hand to guide the current lest it overwhelm me.
Great Eye, you will heed me!
Commanding, lightly strained from physical effort.
Shouted through pain and physical strain.
By fate, we did it. I will finally see.
Breathless from physical strain. Awestruck the ritual actually worked.
Ahh! It’s tearing me! It’s too much—
Don’t interrupt! It’s clearing. I see—my vision—clear—I can see it!
Frenzied and straining. "Don’t interrupt!" directed towards the Player
You were told to leave the Eye.
Curse you. I almost had it.
A moment more and your mind would have melted.
I would have words with you both.
Stern mom energy. Signaling a serious conversation to come.
Is that really you, Lycander? Why have you come here?
Rectifying a mistake I should have settled years ago.
I was so close! The magic is gone again.
I see that you will not be dissuaded. I foresee your doom, but doom is your birthright. Leaving you both to flounder on your own is more dangerous than helping you.
The Eye is tainted with Hatred. A sickness festers at its core, and it must be cut out—purged with my blood.
But know this: such a cleansing is no repair. The Eye will hold but for one vision.
I will aid you on this foolish quest. My workshop still exists somewhere beneath the ruin and reshaping of Sanctuary. I do not know what name the place bears now—too much has changed.
All I can remember is that it was where Lovers Say Farewell. Find it, and I will meet you there.
I once walked these walls. Such familiarity makes my arrival effortless. I defy the Angiris Council by my coming, but I am not the first.
You called the Sightless Eye a mistake. Why?

Philios gathered the Eye’s vessel, and I lent my foresight to shape it. The Eye was made so we may communicate between realms. I feared the High Heavens would sense Sanctuary by us using the Eye, so I urged Philios to hide it.

I did not foresee that my gift would transfer to mortals. More than once, I thought of reclaiming it. Yet humankind was made for longing—the endless hunger to know. Whether that restraint was insightful or foolish, ask Wisdom himself.
Are all the stories between you and Philios true?
I cannot say what stories you have heard, nor how time has colored them. We fought together. Bled together. Broke bread. Laughed. Against all reason and strife, we loved.
Amused she is being asked about her love life. She speaks about her old lover with softness and affection.
I first met him tending to his garden. The way the light bathed him, he looked like the sun.
Philios could be blusterous and proud, but beneath all that thunder was his truest nature. A maker. Above all, he loved to create.
You have the gift of foresight?
What gift I possess is not prophecy as you mortals understand. It is the burden of possibilities. Visions of what might be.
For your companion, I see a few paths ahead. Few are fair.
Do you regret leaving Philios? The High Heavens found out about Sanctuary anyway.

To have loved him once was enough. Philios was never mine to keep. We were chapters in each other's stories. His life after our parting was full. He found love anew and they grew old together. He held his children and grandchildren in his arms. Those were gifts I could never have given.
A place where Lovers Say Farewell—do you know of this location?
Hush all of you! I can barely think straight with this headache.
No, I don’t know of that place. I will have to consult records at the Temple of Life.
Your vision—you saw some of it. What exactly did you see?
Eyes in the dark. A hunger that has no mouth. Silence. A crownless king. A conqueror welcomed with open arms. I have to hold onto it!
Increasingly intense as she describes the horrible visions she saw.
Focus! Feel your breath. The cloth on your skin.
A steadying command to pull the other character (Athrpa) back from a panic attack.

It was the clearest I have ever seen. The images had come into focus. Clear as you stand before me now. But just as it was there, it was gone. I can still taste it. Like ash. Human flesh. Ruin. Something vast behind the sun.
Deep breath at start. Haunted and shaken.
Mainlander! Our seer friend is by the archive!
Let me guess, we need to fight through a spirit-infested crypt to find the place Lycander mentioned?

Oh, I spared you that. I spent the night combing through the archives, cross-referencing Firstborn texts with old Oracle pilgrimage maps. Archivist Linos helped where he could. There is a place referenced as the Hollow of Farewells.
Oh, I spared you that. - Amused.
It would be near the Firstborn graveyard now. I’ve traced the general region.
The archives carried me back to the Firstborn age. My studies of the Eye rarely reach so far into the past. Sanctuary used to have one ocean. The world has shifted much since…
Skovos was not always temples and stone. The Firstborn Daedessa wrote that they once walked across these lands barefoot.
There were gardens here once. Carved terraces overflowing with hyacinths.
This is the place. I feel the Sightless Eye remembering.
We found the spot, but I don't see any vault. Another illusion?
From what I know of Philios, he would never have sealed this place without having a way back.
Look! Scratches at the base of the statues. Like they were dragged, or maybe turned? Hmm. "Where lovers say goodbye..."
Where lovers say goodbye. Perhaps the statues should be rotated away from one another.
Are you...are you all right? The vision you saw, when is it going to happen?
The ruin I saw will not come to pass in our lifetime. Nothing we do will stop it. But at least I know.
Calm acceptance. Strangely unemotional about the end of the world.
I am going to return to Vision’s End. To Laurel. I have had my last vision. I will be there for hers.
For the first time since I can remember, I can enjoy the summer’s breeze. (sighs)
Peaceful and content savoring a simple joy she hadn't allowed herself before
Athrpa has spoken little since her return. All I know is that the Eye can no longer be used for Visions. I had hoped you would succeed, for her sake. She wanted it so desperately.
Gentle and reflective. She's saddened her friend wasn't able to accomplish her goal.
I am glad she could be here for my severing. The burden is heavy alone.
Oh, we must be the first to enter this place in millennia. The Archivists will be overjoyed.
Shouting out for Lycander to hear
We are all here now. How do we clear the Hatred corruption in the Eye?

You are surrounded by objects which teem with the same light imbued in the Eye. Gather them. We will use them to anchor the ritual. When the rite begins, the Seer must hold the Eye open. Only one may enter.

Saying farewell to this place is harder than I imagined. I must seal it to ease the aching—it only reopens the wound. Our decision to part was one of wisdom, but wisdom is a cold companion. I hope she does not think of me. For her sake. Goodbye, my light.
Here yawns the maw of Hatred. No light will follow you there.
It is not enough for demons to corrupt their own pits. They must poison this as well.
That bile is the anchor that tethers Hatred. Scour the halls and burn it away.

Nothing gets by the one at the top.

Last fool to try is still hanging by the docks. Now get the hell out of my face. Unless you’d care to join him?
Feels so soft... like a flower, almost? (giggle) Do you hear that?
It’s better in here... (giggle) Soft and quiet.
Hm, these people are so strange. You’d think they’d at least bathe.
They’re sick in the head, darling. Some are born wretched.
It was only his coin we wanted. Why’d he have to draw his sword like that?
Didn’t mean to kill him. Didn’t want to.
New in town, huh? You pay your protection fee yet?
If not, hope you know how to use that weapon. (snicker)
Don’t you look at me like that. If--if you seen what I seen, heard what I heard confessed to me... you’d be knockin’ these back too.
Ha! The bandit gangs are the law. I’d tell you to watch yourself, but you seem like you can hold your own.
They’re all stragglers from Caldeum. Plague there wiped out half the city before they shut the gates.
Seems like here’s as good a place as any to die.
Oh, it doesn’t support itself. It supports the black market and the cold bastards that run it. Ain’t you seen the slums?
What do you have for sale?
Ah, a traveler! Healthy, finely garbed, and with a keen eye for quality. Do I have the goods for you!
Taste the western continent! Spices, perfumes, liquors, and furs from all over Sanctuary!
Twenty happy customers, cured of the plague! You could be next!
A fair price is all I ask, folks. For only ten gold, I’ll make you healthy again!
Here, this will help with the pain.
I... I can’t. I told you, you can’t ask that of me. I’m so sorry.
Smell that? (deep inhale) That’s what a damn good time smells like, my friend.
Have you coin for a drink? Wet these old lips one last time, wanderer.
Death comes for me. Strong water eases the passin'.
Please, I just need someplace clean to stay. A few nights, at most.
To where? The plagued streets? The bandits beyond the gates? Please!
Five... ten... twenty... should be enough for passage.
Somewhere better, child. Somewhere safer, where you won’t get sick anymore.
I found a body in the water the other day. It was so big, bloated like a ball!  (laughing)
After the battle, Fragom the Forged sat in the shade of that palm there by the stream to wash blood from his face.
After seeing himself in the clear water, he knew he'd never leave.
Welcome to the safest place anywhere in the shadow of Caldeum. Azmodan himself would step lightly in the home of the Iron Wolves!
Our scouts are occupied in the north and the west. If a threat appears in the south, we've no one left to confront it.
Pull with your shoulder, not your wrist! Wasps take us all, will you never learn?!
What do you mean they attacked again? I just cleared that field!
I'm paying you to keep them out, not sit here and eat while they swarm over and over!
Yeah, yeah. I'll head over there again, just let me finish my meal first.
...so Kelim takes this wasp head and shoves it on his helm! Blood and pus running down his face, he starts buzzing like a madman!
Son of a bitch was chasing me with that stinger!
(laughing) Staga, you were trying not to bloody well puke while you ran away! Left a trail behind you.
We do what we can for them, but the evil that infests that temple is not easily cured.
Why aren't the Iron Wolves protecting Caldeum?
The Wolves have lived in the shade of Caldeum, protecting Kehjistan from all that threaten her. Yet even they can only do so much.
Is there a safe path... anywhere?
The path south has become overrun. Everywhere is dangerous now.
How did the Iron Wolves come to settle in a place this beautiful?
Yes, the oasis is beautiful, but more than that, it felt safe. That's why we stayed.
I came here looking for help, and found a dream.
Yet we are together, so would you truly want to wake?
Nay, my love. Though I fear the day we will.
Is it true they have an angel in the north? We can't see Akarat. I'd like to see an angel.
Curious. Shy about disappointment in his own religion. Eager to see something real.
Let me guess, just passing through? (sob) Oh, yes, I'll never be married...
The years pass, death comes, I remain...just a withered old fool and her memories.
(chuckle) That's a fine costume. The desert sun is going to love you.
Mildly amused by the Player's outfit.
Have you news of the Knights?
Heretics they called us. Their damned angel can rot in Hell.
Bitter, simmering anger. "They" were knights that seized the town and killed several of his neighbors.
You, perhaps you can settle this. Horses or camels?
Friendly. Eager to settle a silly argument.
Camels have three eyelids to keep out the sand! Horses? (laughs) Pfft!
Passionate about camels. Emphasis on "three eyelids".
What can you tell me of Tarsarak?
Behold, the armpit of the desert. Our families came from Alcarnus years ago, after that city went to hell. They camped here by the crossroads, set up trade...it's been a struggle ever since.
War in the Steppes, bandits in the south, and Caldeum has closed its golden gates. The few customers we get usually want a guide to take them to "safety." Akarat knows where that is.
We have many funerals to attend, thanks to the Knights and their angel. We'll be singing laments from dusk till dawn...in the Zakarum way.
Grim. Bitter. Contempt for Knights and angel. Pride for "the Zakarum way."
We are the children of Old Kehjan. Cruel bastards come and go, but our people stay rooted in the sand. We'll flower again, same as always.
(sigh) No, I'm not a guide. But you can't throw a rock without hitting one around here.
Last night, I dreamt that the sandstorm came and buried us here. (sigh) If only.
Forget this town, I'm going back south. Violence, intrigue, women, men...paradise.
Come on, you must get up. I'll buy you a round at the inn.
Kind. Taking pity on the local drunk.
You go and get it. I'll wait here.
Dismissive. Depressed. Staring at the ruins of a house.
Poor Caldeum. We used to dance by the fountain in the bazaar. I hope it's still there.
You lost someone too, didn't you? I will add you to my prayers.
The Knight's have left alot of destruction.
We'll need to venture south to cut timber, quarry stones...maybe we rebuild it nicer, eh?
Bracing for hard work ahead. Trying to be optimistic.
Have you seen the Iron Wolves?
(scoff) Iron Wolves. Mercenaries with a silly name, sniffing after coin.
They saved my cousin's life, and she's worthless.
Yes, heh, can't argue with that.
Nodding. Nindaal's cousin is an absolute mess.
The mines have been closed for weeks. How long until your loafing brother finds a job?
He'll be out of our house soon, my flower.
Tired of his brother and this argument.
Ichor mining’s dangerous work. Lost a lot a friends to it—may they rest peacefully.
Unfortunately, there's too much gold to be made to find work elsewhere.
Before the mining site north of here was overrun, we used to not have to haul ichor so far.
The Spiritborn have always been powerful and mysterious.
I crossed paths with one, once... I'll never forget that day.
Years ago, my family lived in a little village just north of here. It was beautiful, before the lacuni...
We lost everything when we were driven out.
I've sailed to every corner of Sanctuary delivering ichor. The salty air and sea breeze—ah, there's nothing like it.
Perilous? Maybe. But I wouldn’t give up life on the sea for anything.
There’s rumor of a dark, festering evil lurking in the center of Nahantu. You won’t find me anywhere near it. You should stay clear as well.
A warning - she's suspicious and is influenced by the rumours.
Ichorfall was built off the hard work of mining and trading ichor.
I feel immense pride to see the town grow over the years.
I trekked from Kurast to Ichorfall to make some gold from mining ichor.
I...I left my family behind. Akarat willing, if I persist, it will be worth it. For me...and for them.
(Broken up) Beat down by exhaustion of trying to make ends meet, but stays hopeful. They do this job for their family.
My ama would often tell the tale of our ancestors, who helped take down the giants when they walked this land.
Serious with an undertone of playful and fondness.
Sounds like just that, a tale.
Did you hear someone’s been maintaining the old ballistas...in case the giants return?
What insane gossip. No one has seen a living giant in centuries.
I can still feel her small hand clutching mine, as she was snatched away by that vicious creature. I tried to hold on...I tried...
My heart breaks for you...someone needs to end that damned bird.
Genuine. Muttering angrily when it comes to the bird.
I just want my daughter back.
My brother left to join a commune at the old church ruins to the south of here.
I just hope he keeps his wits about him.
The discovery of ichor, and its highly corrosive properties, has led me and others to find all kinds of uses for it.
We use it for excavations, potions...poisons. Even been found to have some magical properties.
Lowers their voice and begins to let you in on the secret with magical powers.
Who knows what other uses we will discover in the future? It is quite a fascinating substance.
Indah wastes her time with this grunt work. A wise man told her, Indah’s future is greater than mere fish and rope!
(sigh) Didn’t I tell you not to bother Ormus when the council visits? He has more important things to attend to. And so do you!
But Indah hates mending nets. She finds it "tedious and unlikeable."
Here, sit. Best seats in the house. The slimy bastards come right up to the barrier. You can see them dig and pound and shake. Heh.
Barrier won’t hold forever. But until then, it’s a hell of a show.
I’ll be damned. Seems like the Hollows are finally losing numbers. There’s still stragglers out there. But I feel it in my bones.
One day soon, I’m going to stand up and walk right out of here.
I wouldn’t go much further than here, stranger. Hollows’ll tear you apart, turn you to sludge.
All I’m saying is, if it’s death you’re seeking, there’s better ways to go.
Does the inn get much business?
Heh. Look around. What do you think? Hollows are destroying everything. My customers included.
Is the town faring all right?
We’re still alive. Well, some of us.
But food’s running out. Can't fish, can't trade. Soon the rest will all be gone. Then what?
How has this town managed to survive the Hollows?
We're safe here, thanks to that old dagger. That’s what keeps the barrier up. So they say.
But it won’t last. I keep a bag packed, for when the time comes. You should too.
Oh, Gea Kul. That sour, coin-hungry temptress of the sands. If fate wills it, I’ll be back in your greasy arms before next sundown.
No boats, no fish. Looks like seaweed broth for supper tonight.
You and me both. My daughters are getting sick of the stuff.
(sigh) I’m thankful the barrier keeps us safe. I am. But...
It feels more like a cage than a shield. Day after day, staring at the same starving people, the same rotting wood...
Look at it. A hunk of old metal. But, Akarat’s breath, the magic pulsing off of it... you can feel how old it is. That’s the power of a Skatsimi artifact.
My grandparents practiced Skatsim. But they converted to Zakarum, they wanted to protect us. Was that truly the right choice?
Supposed to count torches for another burn. But I can’t get the first time out of my head.
The shrieking... it was horrible. Birds, monkeys, bats. The fire cleared the Hollows that night, and everything else with them. But they came right back the next day. This can’t be the solution.
Eru promised he would come back. But he lied. It's been forever.
Come now, Eru’s a man of his word. I’m sure the Hollows have kept him busy. Next time the council visits, you’ll see.
I remember you! Not many come back after they leave. Are there any other survivors out there? Have the other towns been overwhelmed?
Wait, no, don't tell me. I’m going to see for myself, soon. They say the Hollows are thinning out. Isn’t that amazing? I’m going to be free!
The Gidbinn is dying. The barrier flickers, now and then. And the only people that would know anything about how to fix it—my ancestors—are long gone.
Now these fine folk depend on it. But their ancestors were the ones that drove out mine. Is this fate just? Or is it as cruel as it feels?
I only lived because I ran and hid. Can’t say I regret it now. Came back to find this place a hellhole.
In case you need a spot for lying low, I holed up in some old ruins southeast of here.
Do you have any food? Please, I’m so hungry... I gave my meal to my little brother.
He’s too young to understand we just don’t have enough.
Things were so different before. I remember I was upset ‘cause my aunt was mad at me. Caught me stealing sips of her wine.
I wish I could tell her I’m sorry.
Too many dead to bury. Had to burn them. Horrified the kids all over again. Didn’t feel right.
There is a quiet place, down south. A garden. Think I’ll do a proper service for them there.
I saw those Knights carrying supplies yesterday. I yelled and yelled, but they didn’t even look.
They have so much food. Crates and crates of armor and swords and stuff, too. Why can’t they share?
They told me not to stand watch. Said it’d give me nightmares. It’s dumb, I have those anyway.
At least next time the monsters come out the cave, I’ll be ready.
They’re kind of scary, huh? My ma always said to look your fears in the eye.
She stared down the monsters. Then they clawed up her face... she should’ve ran, instead.
I heard they harvested the adults like cattle taken to slaughter. Left only the little ones to grow bigger. Not enough meat on the bone.
Great, that’s what Sanctuary needs. A town’s worth of orphans skittering about, picking folks’ pockets.
Shh! You’ll make ‘em cry if they hear you.
Let it out, child. That’s the only good way to get rid of bad feelings.
Mama and Papa are dead, aren’t they?
Yes, they are. But their blood flows through your veins. You carry them with you, see?
Bridge to the swamp is back open.
And the trade routes. Still thinking about leaving?
Graveyard on this side, death trap on the other. Akarat’s breath, does it even matter?
Papa, I’m not ready for sleep.
Shh...don't wake your sister. You know, children who don't listen will be turned into flower food by Dregs.
(gasps) I don't want to be flower food.
Beware the shadows and dark corners of the city, stranger. If you hear your name called, don't answer. That's how they get you.
Genuinely offering advice. This kid has seen things and has lost friends to the shadows.
Ack, spiritborn? We are Kehjistani, you were raised in the Zakarum faith.
Confused, but not angry. Just wants to understand.
I dream of Umbaru, I see myself there. I've not turned my back on Akarat, just seeing his light through a new lens.
Calmly explaining. Really wants his father to understand, but isn't angry or forceful. You can hear the happiness in his voice as he shares his perspective.
I speak of heritage. The one that is within you as it is in your mother. Give me time. Your mother more so. We will come to terms with this.
Sighing. Fatherly and caring. Tired, but knowing.
When I was just a child, I met a traveler just like you, passing through. (sighs) Has it been that many years already?
How fare your travels? I'm relieved to see you return unscathed. At my age, such reunions are uncertain. You must be blessed by Akarat himself.
Are you familiar with the mysteries of the Dark Citadel?
The Dark Citadel? Feh. I suggest you not let your curiosity get the best of you. That's not a place you should go alone.
I could talk your ear off about Kurast, but it is not the same as experiencing it.
I implore you to explore the city and unravel its history. You will find your own fondness for it, I’m sure.
You don’t look familiar. We rarely get travelers these days. Makes us wary when someone new comes around.
Wary and to the point. She has no time for strangers. Polite, but only just.

Zagraal's monstrous head now decorates our city. A victory long overdue. I’m curious if that creature’s end was your doing?
Hiding her excitement that the deadly khazra has been defeated.
Word is there’s been more foreigners seen in these parts with sooted armor and charred skin.
Idle tavern gossip. Just trying to fill the air and pass the time.
That's rumor talk if you didn't see it for yourself.
To the point and a little annoyed. He's tired of gossip and only wants facts.
There’s news about the khazra that killed poor Teyaca and Balam.
Were you not gathering some folks together to kill it?
Curious, but skeptical. Isn't sure where his friend is going with this.
That was my plan, but something got the goatmen first. Only things remaining were blood and bones. Never seen anything like it.
A tinge of worry to her confession. One part awe and one part fear.
There was a text I read that delved into Kurast's past. A city of prosperity and glory...
Hard to imagine, since all we’ve known is a half-destroyed city.
I could picture it. Everywhere rich in silver with lush greenery.
Psh, if only. Your head may still be stuck in that book. The city lacks life now. Few people live here, let alone pass through.
Diwata told me she spotted a creature in the woods yesterday. The way she described it...I can only imagine it's the one that eats goats!
Etsuk Supa? I figured it was just some folktale of a dog creature.
You might think it's just a story, but I’m determined to prove the jungle legend exists.
Well, I admire the dedication, friend.
My Lolo would always share stories of how he and my grandmother fled Kurast. The way he spoke...things must have been horrible.
Disbelief and awe. Struck by how beautiful the city is and how vastly different it looks to how her grandparents described it in stories.
I can tell the city has its scars but it’s beautiful, nonetheless.
We thought it was gone. We thought him gone, yet Hatred claws at her gates again.
Stunned and distraught. Small, not boisterous. Deeply worried.
How can we survive another siege?
The door was here yesterday. Or was it a pillar? Damn. I swear, the walls never seem to stay the same.
Confused. Convinced the layout of the city changes. Not crazy. He is sincerely trying to figure this out. Voice is mumbling.
I carry the curse of my ancestors, as did my parents and their parents.
Fatalist. Convinced he has no say in his future. Very doom and gloom.
Jinxed from the damned jungle, a life that never seems to stray from misery.
It is a shame, I tell you, having to sell in this deserted city.
I wouldn’t be here if the markets elsewhere weren’t so damned expensive.
There’s word swirling around town claiming folks are being snatched up. Their souls being used for some sick dark ritual.
Best to keep a lantern or a friend with you tonight.
I'm tired of cleaning up trash and living in this rundown place in Lower Kurast.
Upper markets thrive while lower markets are left to wither away into desolation.
You there! Have my spices caught your eye?
They are original Kehjistani spices that will not disappoint!
Turns out there was more truth to your story of burned invaders than I want to admit.
And you thought I was just spreading rumors. The jungle should kill them off in time.
Bickering and a bit standoff-ish. Playfully scolding.
Maybe not. I’ve heard they joined forces with the Dregs.
Do you think Etsuk Supa will gain an appetite for the Hollows?
Wondering out loud. Curious and a bit lost in thought.
(scoffs) If it were you, would you choose to eat a stag or a rotting goat?
Teasing, knowing how his friend would respond.
Well, something is thinning their numbers. If not them, what then?
Matter-of-fact. A little concerned, a little intrigued.
Papa, I’d really like to see the pretty flower fields like we did last year.
Sweet Chakhir, it is no longer safe to go. There are many more Dregs than before.
Then when Mawar grows up, Mawar will fight all these Dregs, so we can have our flower tour!
Hopefully by then you won’t need to do that. But for now, let's not wander outside the city on our own, yeah?
The city feels safer than before. Did we get more guards?
I’m not sure the city has enough money for more guards.
Regardless, there’s been a significant drop in threats from the outside.
Indeed. I hope it stays this way for a while.

I overheard my Lolo once say bargains with demons are a one-sided dance. You think you dance together, but with every deal there will be an invisible string drawn from you to the demon: a master puppeteer.
I never imagined Kurast having anything but a fate of misery...perhaps it isn’t as sealed as I believed.
Like a single ray of sunlight through dark clouds. Still gloomy, but starting to come out of it. There is some hope after all.
The way I see it, as long as our souls hold any value, there will always be the threat of it being taken.
My prayers to Akarat have been answered! Zotia offered me work at the inn.
I never imagined myself to be one of optimism, yet here I am.
Uh, Grandmother said I shouldn’t talk to strangers.
(gasp) Excuse me! Where did you come from? Did you have to kill monsters to get here?
Ahali! What are you doing?! That's a stranger.
You're such a baby, Chula. Old Yungun told me the elders only make those rules ‘cause they’re scared. He said outsiders have the best stories, if you know what to ask.
Ahh. Season after season, the beauty of the falls never fades.
I'm sure the spirits smile to hear you say that. What have you brought to offer today, my dear?
Tch! Not now. The outsider is watching.
Is it true? About the runaway. I heard they found his body. I heard it was spirits, of all things, that killed him!
Can’t say for sure. But I do know his mother wouldn’t appreciate you prying about it.
Oh, you are right, Coyo. Gossip rots the mind.
But, if you really want to know... then I might tell you to travel the eastern roads, south of lower Kurast. I might mention it’s there the corpse lies.
Did you see the lake split?
With my very own eyes! Thought I was going right mad. Never seen anything like it, in all my years.
Glad the waters returned, though. Don’t want to put the fishers out of a job; Samuk wouldn’t survive without them.
It's eerily quiet down by the docks...
Eh, outsiders just don’t understand. Everywhere else in Sanctuary, folks thieve and kill and burn. They’ve forgotten the spirits. Not us.
Take what you need, offer what you can. The spirits gift us food, and in turn they take... less necessary things. Memories. Thoughts. A worthy trade for survival, if you ask me.
Kind of you to ask. But we take care of our own. We’ve no gamblers with unpaid debts, nor drinkers lost in the bottle. No murderers, thieves, nor swindlers, neither.
Samuk thrives with the spirits’ aid. The best thing you can do for us is to keep our secret. Not many know of our little town, and we’d prefer it stays that way.
This doesn't seem like much of an inn.
Ha! It isn't. Aside from the occasional pilgrim, you're the first outsider we've seen in a long while. I keep a spare cot around for visitors just in case. Nobody else here will.
That, and I'm the only one in Samuk who knows how to brew a good drink!
Ah, close your eyes. Listen. Breathe in the air. Oh! Can’t you feel it? Akarat’s footsteps, beneath our very feet!
His blessings curl in the soil, dance in our breath, they parted the very lake! Ha, and to think I almost gave up pilgrimage in Kurast. A sorry fool, I’d have been.
Outsider, huh? One foolish enough to brave the Tangles. Only the pilgrims try. And less than half survive.
At least they’ve reason to throw their lives away. You, though. You’re no pilgrim. So what are you?
Momma says that tying our hair into the wards makes them stronger.
Hmm, need to be sure my daughter has all the warding materials. She'll be a fine protector of our glen when she's old enough.
I think I'm too old to experience such darkness again. Or perhaps it is because I am old that I must...
(inhales) Good. They’re burning the pine resin. I hope it will keep us safe.
Inhales before the line, taking in the smell of the burning resin. Relaxed and hopeful.
It always has before. Trust in the old ways.
Can't hunt like we used to. Wasn't safe before. Damn deadly, now.
Do you think the Knights are helping?
Charms and totems have always protected Braestaig from the spirits of the hills.
What good are “fortifications” against creatures who can walk through walls?
What do you have on offer?
We've got ale. Bread for you too, since you're not a Knight Penitent. No bath though, go to Cerrigar if you want that sort of service.
Are you worried about the fog?
We've got folks up there, in Clocheen. We're worried about them. Eh, who wouldn't be?
They think by flashing Yorin's pretty young face, we'll put our fate in their hands, heh. But glenfolk've always taken care of our own.
The shadow has passed, but the loss remains. We’ll make do as we always have...and grieve the missing in our own time.
Light watch over us. We live in dark times and I do not know that we will see the light any time soon.
I will send scores of spirits to their rest! With the Light beside me, I am untouchable.
The Light will protect your soul, but not your hide. Remember that well.
How are you feeling about the upcoming fight?
How is sparring and training with dummies supposed to prepare me for fighting ghosts?
What if they turn me into one?
Do you think the Knights are prepared?
The Knights Penitent think they understand what's out there. Think their Light's enough to face it. They're in for a shock.
How are the Knights handling the spirits?
I’ve heard the Knights praying more and more. They’re scared, and they should be.
I’ve never seen the spirits of the Hills act like this.
Have you heard anything from your sister in Clocheen?
No, that damned fog has me so worried for her.
The fog disappeared and so did the Knights, praising their “Father” for his deeds all the way.
The demon set the Glen ablaze.
Playful singing. To the tune of "London Bridge"
Donan and the Druids made it pay.
Playful singing. To the tune of "London Bridge"
The Days of Ash have gone away.

Talk of this "horned woman" is stirrin' up old fears. It's no good for the market.
Folk need to see their chief ain’t afraid.
Speaking to the chieftain. Concerned. Respectfully urging.
Aye. Take a letter to Donan. I would have his opinion on the matter.
Anxious. Giving an order, but avoiding responsibility.
Ghosts of my kindred, spirits of the wild, forgive my weakness...rise to our desperate need!
I saw what you and Donan did for us...what he had to do to his son.
Grateful. Heavy. Grief for Donan's son.
It is a cruel fate for an old warrior to see his legacy perish. (sigh) He did not deserve it.
I am glad to see you return. Our city is healing slowly, yet surely.
When next you see Donan, tell him I hope that he is healing also.
“What is the meaning of this tree?”
She was raised here by Vasily himself, first of the druids.
He planted scores of oaks just like her, all over the ‘Glen...only two remain.
Cathedral said we’ll have paved roads, yet here I am! Keepin’ the mud tidy.
To Player, complaining while she sweeps.
I saw you pass Vasily’s Tree. You kicked a runestone on purpose, you steel-plated bastard!
To the foreign knight. Furious. Chastising.
To the local. Flat. Uncaring. Intimidating.
I lived down there when I was a boy. You should’ve seen how green it was...how proud we were.
It’s Astaroth! He’s returned—to finish us!
No more cities! We’re taking what the fires left and heading to the country—far as we can get.
More water! Wet that wood over there! Don’t let the embers catch!
Urgent. Barking orders at villagers nearby.
No! I can’t fight, I won’t...sh-she's here! SHE’S HERE!
It--it was a beast! A hound of Hell!

A gentle whisper glides upon the winds. The words elude the grasp of mortal ken. They weave through the soul like a melody forgotten, and from this arises a name: Adarja, the First-Breather.
In Natsalarwaka, no blood shall mar the earth. Even bitter enemies must forgo their blades before entering the haven. Breaking this accord will invoke Wasipotsu's wrath. - Oral Oaxazi Scripture
At midday thundered the first brother, Nyamoyo, lord of predators. Survival is his blessing, hunting is his prayer. Honor him and prowess shall be your reward. - The Nitī Sē, Verse IV
At midnight laughed the second brother, Nebahayomo, spirit of cunning. Trickery is his blessing, suffering is his prayer. Honor him and shrewdness shall be your reward. - The Nitī Sē, Verse V
One of a pair of twin daggers, forbidden from ever meeting. Bitter voices whisper from the blade.
A single petal of the Mother's own blood, slowly wilting under glass.
Tread carefully on the plains of Hell, for each step sunders the soul and shatters the mind.
Despite the Light's blessings, countless Knights Penitent were hewn apart by the infernal hordes. Remnants of their steel lie scattered through the Hells – dwindling lights in the chaos.
The prince of Hatred, fair as maggots over carrion. He claims no throne, crafts no realms, reigning over only a blackened, bitter heart. Some legends name him banished, while others dread his return.
It is a small sacrifice. But who would not regard their own hand and prefer it remain whole? Even against the promise of such power? -Elias of Aranoch
I know what I must do. Phoba, Fer, Mlor, aligned upon a single, terrible course. Yet despite myself, I find the certainty not only comforting but beautiful in its simplicity. -Tal Rasha
Every facet, precise. Each turn of the stone, a symphony of refracted light. How miraculous the properties? How thrilling the possibilities? -Zoltun Kulle

The {c_highlight}Vulnerable{/c} status effect increases the damage taken by enemies for a short duration. It is represented by a {c:ff8158a9}purple{/c} glow around the Health Bar for enemies and a cracked Health Globe for you.
The {c_highlight}Knockdown{/c} status effect prevents enemies from moving or taking action for a short duration. It can be removed through Unstoppable or Immune effects.

The {c_highlight}Dazed{/c} status effect prevents enemies from attacking or using Skills for a short duration, but does not stop them from moving. It can be removed through Unstoppable or Immune effects.

You become {c_highlight}Fortified{/c} when you have any amount of {c_highlight}Fortify{/c}, which is drained to restore Life over time. Certain Skills or item effects can grant Fortify, which cannot exceed your Maximum Life.
The {c_highlight}Tether{/c} status effect prevents enemies from moving out of its radius. It can be removed through Unstoppable or Immune effects OR by destroying the tethered target.

The {c_highlight}Fear{/c} status effect prevents enemies from moving or taking action AND causes the affected target to run away for a short duration. It can be removed through Unstoppable or Immune effects.

The dreams continue to haunt me. My search for answers leads now to the Fractured Peaks, where  a wise man from a forgotten order is rumored to live as a hermit. If he cannot rid me of these visions, perhaps he can help me to understand them.
I agreed to search the broken tower north of Nevesk. If whatever lurks within is connected to my visions, then I must face it.
The broken tower brought me no answers--only more questions. At least tidings of the demon's defeat should set the villagers at ease.
The villagers betrayed me. My reward for slaying the demon was a poisoned cup and a cold, stone table upon which to be sacrificed. With the help of the old monk, I fight my way to freedom.
The monk rescued me from the villagers who hours ago seemed harmless - even kind. He told me they gathered at the nearby chapel to pray for salvation from evil. I must follow this thread to the end.

I told the monk of the horned woman I saw in the chapel. His eyes grew wide with fear, but told me little. He instructed me to find a hermit living in the hills to the east and bring him to the Cathedral of Light for questioning. I will find this hermit. I must have answers.

Removing Elias' finger from the altar caused the temple to sink further into the murky waters. I was able to escape, but only barely. I should return to Lorath as quickly as possible.
The ancient coffin has brought me to some kind of ancient, sunken temple. Elias' secret hides in these forgotten depths somewhere.
The soulstone has been repaired, and Elias' immortality broken. The time has come to attempt to attune the soulstone to Mephisto's essence once more.
We survived Elias' ambush, but he is attempting to escape. I must catch up with him before he can.
The secret of Lilith's path into the Burning Hells died with Elias, but everything he knew, now belongs to the Tree of Whispers. If we're lucky, it will tell us what we need to know.

Aspect of the Swamp! Savior of the Shore! Deliver us from the bonds of the Naga, and mete out justice for your people! -Unknown, translated from Nerglish

An oddity of the astral plane, this creature once stood in the way of the Black Swordsman's party, seemingly intent on blocking their path. Why? No one knows...
His sleek shadow stretches across your table, his many eyes gleaming with mischief as he makes a mess of your valuable things.
Much hides behind those sly winks.

No one understands the true nature of the spirit inhabiting these armaments. Still, it is clear that the warrior who dons this armor and wields these weapons becomes a nigh-unstoppable engine of destruction.

When Zakarum forces sacked and plundered Klath-Ulna's village, little did they suspect someone survived that massacre. Yet he did, returning to visit that treatment in kind on Zakarum-held settlements, defiling their holy symbols and stripping them of their gold.
Created for Lilith's mightiest warriors, this armor stokes the hatred inside the wearer and channels it for battle.

When commonfolk see this lost soul, they fear it's an omen of death. But the Children of Bul-Kathos see a sibling gone mad...too far gone to return to the tribe.
When the barbarian slew the mighty nangari, a corpse spilled from its belly. Digested. Adorned in bronze and steel. "You served the snake well," sneered the barbarian. "And in such fine armor..."

Stoic, merciless, and unaffected by their own emotions and opinions, these imposing figures are a reminder of what happens if one strays from the flock. Carrying always with them the tongues of those fallen beneath their blades.
Even the most destitute settlements have their versions of justice, and with that "justice" comes a need for those who execute its judgment.
A silent warrior with a forgotten name wanders the wastes of Arreat. He hunts game, sleeps on bare stone, and tinkers with the metal his foes leave behind. "A good life," he'd say.
Its eyes burned like forge-hot iron. Its breath reeked of charred flesh. It was not a human but an eater of men.
Beware the demon in the shape of man.
In the fighting pits of Old Kehjan, a condemned barbarian reigned supreme. History recalls but a single name, chanted by ravenous crowds: Tyrant.

Suits of this macabre armor have recently been unearthed in deepest Kehjistan. During the Sin War, they belonged to a cabal of powerful religious zealots who followed the Cathedral of Light and the Prophet. Unfortunately, like many other heroes of the time, they were eventually corrupted and turned away from the Light.
From the moment I don the armor, something in me changed. My fear gave way to rage and the clamor of battle became music to my ears. -Tylk the Battler
Bloodhawks are vermin. They're filthy, vicious, damn difficult to kill...I like bloodhawks. - Katra of Oxen Tribe

Through a carefully guarded process, rare crystals found only in Kehjistani mines are fused with demon bone to create armors of superior quality. The shards are living crystals that chip and crack during combat only to later grow anew.
An alchemical fusion of metal, crystal, and bone.
Some believe that to eat the heart of their enemies is to absorb their power. But to consume the flesh of the infernal is to transcend the mortal and become something different.
Though the exact origin of this armor is lost to the annals of time, some scholars believe it dates back to the Sin War.
In the ancient days when the Mage Clans clashed, Bartuc, Warlord of Blood, built an army of horrors—throngs of demons, summoned from the Hells, and human warriors every inch as wicked.

Let the Light of Inarius burn away wickedness. Let not temptation lead you from his holy radiance. Let righteousness sear away corruption and sin. Cast out thy darkness, for only Light must remain. -Reverend Mother Prava

Ongr and her fellows had claimed victory in Aranoch, yet found themselves stranded in open desert. They walked for days to reach the mountains, and one by one they fell...all except Ongr. To the cruel sun above, she pledged her life—forsaking the night forever.
The bronze-plated armor was created by a long dead tribe to honor Bul-Kathos and his battle with the Hydra. Even in cold climates the armor is warm to the touch.
Found in the overgrown ruins of an Old Kurast arena, this armor appears fit for a champion. Jeweled pictograms tell of great victories, long faded from memory.
Even after his escape, Varian was Lo'Gosh, and Lo'Gosh was Varian. When his kingdom needed it, the wolf would be waiting.

My foes crash against me like waves, Alarfell intoned. "But I do not erode. I increase." His unearthly hand swooped down, snatching up a fistful of pikes like they were twigs. "Mere droplets before the unyielding sea."

Found in the depths of an Ennead Clan ruin, this armor is a masterwork of transmutation—the bones of a bear, petrified with volcanic rock and extruded into fearsome, black shards. With a warrior inside, this was as close to a demon as the Ennead could conjure.

Accounts of the archangel Tyrael date back to the Golden Age of Magic, many telling of his vote to spare humanity from destruction. Depictions of him range widely, from crude drawings on stone walls to the most exquisite pieces of armor.

The earth of the Frigid Highlands trembled and split beneath the tribesmen's feet, and a torrent of hellfire engulfed them. They screamed as they were dragged down, down to the pits of Abaddon to join the legions of Baal.

When the Edyrem fought for the fate of humanity, they delved the depths of their power—some beyond the limits of death. When at last a "peace" was forged, they had already gone too far. Lost souls, doomed to fight a forgotten war.
For them, it will never be over.
On the day Garrosh became warchief, he only wanted to make his father proud. On the day they came for his throne, he thought he had.

Off duty at last, Athurfal rode out from Kor Valar toward the glacier, his favorite place to smoke his pipe. It was terrible bad luck that he met a strange man there – frozen through yet very much alive, pulsing with hateful magic. Athurfal would be forced to serve from that day hence. Duty beyond death.

Days had passed since Eiler smuggled the ancient armor home, yet he could not take his eyes off it. He skipped meals, ignored the door, and stayed awake all hours, transfixed by the helm's hollow gaze. On the sixth day, Eiler saw it nod. Reverently, he donned the armor, piece by piece, as it burned his flesh away.

The reports said General Guthr had vanished into the night, dragged from his tent by a wraith of black smoke. His soldiers were relieved, at first, to see him stagger back into camp. Their smiles dropped as he raised his axe.
Glory to the archangel of valor! He who drives our Heavenly Host to vanquish the powers of darkness! May he lead us to lasting victory.

He handed the dripping device back to his trembling novitiate, patting their back with his bloody hand and a toothy grin.
The crystalline corruption laced its way up Zorza's arm, erupting in beautiful fractals. Each sudden growth seemed to add new thoughts, new strengths...and a new wrath.

Good luck, laughed the blacksmith. "You can't put a dent anywhere on that armor. Used all my rare earths from the Pit to craft it, but..." He shrugged. "Out of my hands now. I'm afraid that madman will walk into your keep, fresh as daisies."
Worn by Guts, the Black Swordsman, this ancient armor feeds off the violent emotions of its wearer. All fear and pain are forgotten, replaced by a terrible bloodlust few can hope to control.

After a life of faithful service to the Light, Brave Bagosz had fallen. Killed by a necromancer and doomed to profane undeath. Heavy with grief, Bagosz's fellow paladins interred his undying remains deep beneath Omath's Redoubt. A dubious honor for the ultimate sacrifice.

What is man but meat? Meat that dreams of grandeur. So come closer, my little scholar. Let my gift remake you. From a pathetic pen...to the mightiest of swords. –Sha'lox the Tempter

The name's Jim Raynor, pal. And I won't be talked down to by anybody. Not even a Protoss.
Still hasn't paid off his tab at Joeyray's.

Balarc's grin almost broke through his visage of burning iron. "I hope you land a lot of blows before I crush your skull."

Unbroken by Loren's conquering boot, nor the fall of Sescheron. Stalwart before war's brutal face. Judge of men, juror of the righteous: this is the ancient way of the Blackthorn. Watch how from the shadows, we wrestle with the Balance! -Arbiter Odomace of the Blackthorn Tribe

Lock, stock, and two smokin' knuckles.
The path to power, you say? More blades. Here? Blade. There? Blade. And finally... you got it, blade. -Unknown

To suffer is to know Truth.

With their knowledge of all that grows, the Master Brewer concocts wonderous libations and brings a little comfort to the folk of the Glen.

With powerful cold magicks, these icy titans protect their frozen lands from the depredations of the outside world.

Some are born with power beyond their ability to control. Try as they may, some of our greatest heroes often leave destruction in their wake.

Following in the footsteps of the Horadrim, the Order of the First Ones stand against the machinations of Hell. They too covet the magic of "the Cube" and look to wield its power for the good of Sanctuary.

This enigmatic figure arrived from the west, collecting Lilith's blood petals as they made their way across Kehjistan, through the Dry Steppes and up to Scosglen. To what ends is known only to this horned wanderer.

The nature of Sanctuary is chaos. Maeven of Kurast embraced this fact, and called out to the ancient forces that embody bedlam and turmoil. The gift: eldritch power. The cost: sanity, in becoming a vessel for whirling madness.

The Yshari Sanctum... in my time, it was marvelous. I could sit in the grand library with my spice tea, reading masterworks of elemental theory, astral prophecy, transmutation -- millennia of learnings, gathered under one roof! It's a shame the Yshari couldn't gather themselves... -Ayuzhan of Caldeum

Through handling the Sightless Eye, the oracles of Skovos Isle have gained the ability to glimpse the future without the artifact, though not as clearly. These visions have led the Seers to the mainland in hopes of diverting foreseen disasters.

Upon discovering the sacred oasis and donning the ancient mask found within, T'jier became one with the oasis. Thus began his days of helping those lost among the sands. In exchange for knowledge of their deepest secret, T'jier would happily heal their ailments and send them on towards their destination.
Rumored to be crafted from the carcass of the infamous succubus Blackjade, many have donned the terrifying garment believing it to grant the powers of seduction.

Some who are touched by Lilith develop an insatiable hunger for that which is not theirs. Far beyond simple greed, these followers hold covetousness as a virtue and approach the acquisition of their desires with religious fervor.

Sailors tell of a sorcerer betrayed on the Twin Seas, cast to the depths by superstitious fools. There, the sorcerer drank of darkness known only to the Drowned and soon rose again to the surface. A wraith of the Seas' revenge.

At the height of the Age of Magic, the arcane arts were celebrated openly; performed on stage and public square in dazzling displays, much like the birds of the deep jungle that flaunt their radiant plumage.
Widowed, alone, and left to find their own salvation, this dark figure lurks within the shadows, carrying the burden of their losses and the weight of Mother's words.
Some believed the Oracle was a messenger of the Light, capable of wondrous miracles. Others suspected a fiend beneath the porcelain facade, seducing fools with tears of gold.
Who can see the way to salvation?

Who can see the way to salvation?
The talent of this sorcerer blossomed at the very moment their life was about to end on the great altar. In a way, the ritual was successful, as the innocent was sacrificed and the sorcerer born.
A new beginning from a bloody end.

The Kehjistan desert is filled with corpses who braved the open sands. Those who survive will sometimes report hearing a jingling of coins and a sweet voice on the air, promising to lead them to safety. They were wise not to listen.
Beware what glitters out on the dunes.
Don this mantle and know the Sun as more than a celestial body. Know the Sun as a source of purest elemental fire.
Don this mantle and know the Sun as more than a celestial body. Know the Sun as a source of purest elemental fire.

With cries rivaling that of the Que-Hegan's sacred throng, they burst forth in chants: "Again and again he quenched the flames of Hatred with his body," they sang. "And his ashes became Light, and Day!"

Darkness is a dominating force of nature. We all know it, we all endure it. But within that nature, contemplate the lotus, the intricate flower that blooms from the mire. So too should your sorcery be. -Ernethel, Instructor of the Yshari
This attire bears images said to resemble celestial construction, as described by mystics capable of preternatural vision most divine.
Moths are symbolic of death, transformation, and the mysteries of the afterlife. As a moth is drawn to the light of a fire so too is this mystic drawn to uncovering those secrets.

Suits of this macabre armor have recently been unearthed in deepest Kehjistan. During the Sin War, they belonged to a cabal of powerful religious zealots who followed the Cathedral of Light and the Prophet. Unfortunately like many other heroes of the time, they were eventually corrupted and turned away from the Light.
We Invoke the Hydra's name and Summon her to our realm, that she may Enhance our formidable power. -The Hydra Triad

Through a carefully guarded process, rare crystals found only in Kehjistani mines are fused with demon bone to create armors of superior quality. The shards are living crystals that chip and crack during combat, only to later grow anew.
An alchemical fusion of metal, crystal, and bone.
A torrent of power erupted from their body as they finished the incantation. When the dust settled, only they were left standing, lightning still surging through their form.

The deep forests of Scosglen hide a sorcerer falsely accused and cast out from their homeland. Branded a witch, heretic, and betrayer of their people, they now live as a recluse in the woods, using their powers to cull the hordes of Hell that threaten Sanctuary.
A seer plays a dangerous game, reaching into the mists between worlds. What takes one's hand may offer answers, but it may not wish to let go.
Beware the voices in the mist.
