Beware the voices in the mist.
When Aerin was a child, they befriended a murder of crows that would frequent their home. When Aerin manifested their sorcerous power, they adopted the corvid as their mystical signature.
When Aerin was a child, they befriended a murder of crows that would frequent their home. When Aerin manifested their sorcerous power, they adopted the corvid as their mystical signature.

Years of research beneath the glacier had rendered Sivalir numb. The touch of his fingers. The warmth of his face. The life in his eyes, gone – replaced by terrible, frozen clarity. It was all he'd ever hoped for.

While the High Council of Zakarum dominated Old Kurast, advisers into the ways of sorcery were a necessity. Both reviled and valued for their insights, these individuals were forced to walk a fine line, often with lethal consequences.
Caution, restraint, sentiment...these are shackles that bind humanity. I, for one, refuse to accept them. -Zoltun Kulle
Do the ends justify the means?
In the eyes of most, Kael'thas betrayed his own people for petty power. In his own eyes, though? Everything he did, he did for Silvermoon.
In the eyes of most, Kael'thas betrayed his own people for petty power. In his own eyes, though? Everything he did, he did for Silvermoon.
Little is known of Habacalva, sorceress of the Zann Esu who freed the flaming hydras. The histories speak of her in hushed tones, as though the pages themselves might burst into flame.
Little is known of Habacalva, sorceress of the Zann Esu who freed the flaming hydras. The histories speak of her in hushed tones, as though the pages themselves might burst into flame.

The drums of distant thunder roused Mellal from her trance, and slowly she raised her arms to the sky. The clouds above darkened. The drums grew louder. And as the first sparks danced on Mellal's fingertips, she smiled. "So we begin."

A whisper that tickles your ear. A flutter that makes you flinch. You hasten your step, your worn boots squelching in the alley's mud. A smooth chuckle seems to echo between the gutted rafters above you. You must run, or else she will feast.
The fine wine of their fear.

A dusty book lies open before you. You read the first line: a warning. It prohibits the use of this necromantic tract for certain magical lineages. You flick the book shut with a burst of ice. It's coming with you.
In her youth, Jaina was a candle in the dark. When the whole world seemed poised for war, she lit the path to peace.

It is said that when the Age of Faith dawned, the mages' sun set in Estuar. Laranae of the Ennead saw it coming. All of her wealth, she bore to the West to build a domain of her own, shrouded in the sands of Aranoch. A haven for the wonders of magic. A myth to all who would threaten it.

At Imperius' command they stood under the Crystal Arch, birthplace of all their kind. It was there they faced the Lord of Terror and his demon horde. It was there they earned victory with their lives.

Nelece had barely been accepted by the Zann Esu. True, she could freeze the ambient air with a thought, but this was a base requirement. To attain the perfection expected of a sorceress, Nelece would have to suffer...to sit atop the highest peak until the winds obeyed her will.

The lost and lonely hear her laughter like silver chimes in autumn. Eagerly, they follow the sound, out of safety and into the shadows where she awaits with arms outstretched, delighted to receive them.
There is no need to fear.
In our darkest days, we abide in the archangel of hope! She whose faith never waivers, even as the Prime Evils rise again! May she forever tend our gardens of hope and preserve us against despair.
Champion of the Silver City Sorcerer Equipment

Let the name of Bartuc be damned. Let Jazreth be erased from memory. Let Zoltun Kulle's work crumble. Let Hell flow into me, so that my power may eclipse them all... -Maledictus IV of Jael'j the Blasphemer
A demon does not ask for permission.
The Flames of Abaddon Sorcerer Equipment

This scroll reveals all, Procurator Daycen said. "Seems that foolish princes and generals played with phantoms, conjuring weapons that cannot be killed. Nothing in here about exorcism spells..." He lowered the scroll, his features contorted. "But that was your plan all along, wasn't it?"
In the days of old, when the kings of D'Nur forgot and despised the sacred doctrines... thy embrace was felt, thy cleansing fire purged evil from our ranks! -Ligra Luvultengi IV
Age of the Slayer Sorcerer Equipment

I have sacrificed all that our world might live. I have sullied my honor, I have discarded my rank and standing, and I have even broken our own most ancient traditions. But never think that I would, for one moment, regret my actions. -Tassadar

You have this position, Raelan, because I have need of your purifying fire. The Light's children can be...unruly. Burn the heresy out. Get the truth however you want. Your methods will not be questioned. -Urivar
Nothing stays a secret for long.

The wounded brigand found himself on his back, staring up at a towering figure swathed in sparkling spicules. "What are you?" he spat, clutching his flank as now-iridescent blood spilled through his fingers. Her only answer: "Order."
Shut that gaping maw of yours and witness me in all my splendor! Sailing upon the golden Argentek, snacking on men's eyes like grapes, and sipping their tears as wine! -The Lioness of Denshar
Deity of the Desert Sorcerer Equipment

Champion. Priest. Titles all. It matters not, Sorcerer Firrdaz whispered. "For I receive power from worlds that lie outside your ken." A howling wind arose from beyond the veil, and ignited his dark dagger with an unrelenting fire...

Her mana seemed to surge in rhythm with the ancient dragon's heartbeat. An inchoate frostbolt began to materialize above her palm. "Got a message from 'the one in the dress' right here." She hurled it with her all.

Recorded history fails to say when the Spiritborn first communed with the realm beyond. Antiquities like the "Veilwalker" date the practice as far back as the Mage Clan Wars. The Spiritborn themselves believe their ways are as old as Sanctuary.
It took guile, cunning, and a little trickery for Bwonsamdi to escape his own mortality. Who better to shepherd the dead than one who understands life so well?
We touch the soil to call Balazan, the crawling devourer below. Lend us your skill to draw close to our foes and your patience once death is assured.
We reach to the sky to call to Kwatli, the soaring seeker above. Lend us your sight and precision of mind to catch our prey unaware.
We beat our chests and shout to the lowlands to call Wumba, the mighty guardian. Lend us your strength and courage to defend all that we love.
We pace in the heat and wet of the jungle to call Rezoka, the fierce hunter. Lend us your cunning to stalk our quarry and strike with terrible fury.
Blood is the conduit through which spirit may flow into being. It carries the voices of our ancestors. Their passion and pain. Their love and their hate. -Maka

Among the temple's lofty protrusions lies a room of mirrors. Chernok steps into the still chamber, eyeing dim reflections of himself. He grins as the wind howls through, heralding rosy-fingered dawn. The mirrors flood with opulent gold, and utter is the glory that incinerates him.
You deserve more than to be chained to mortality, and the more you thirst, the more you will understand. -Zir
Blood of an Ancient, born anew.

Frozen beads snaked their way up her blue fingertips. A dark command to move rattled in her veins, yet her body obeyed not. Mere moments from becoming a cloud of blood and ice. Lips broke apart, and warm words escaped: "Join me, spirit."

Near the end of the feast, the drums suddenly quickened, reviving the guests for one last dance. But their smiles soon faded as they watched their partners change. Pointed teeth bared. Eyes glowing scarlet.

I will be Hatred's herald. He cut his thumb. "I will serve the true lords of this world." He drew a symbol in blood, reciting blasphemies in some unknown tongue. With each guttural syllable, hot scars spread across his body...

It was under a pale light that night when Spiritborn Perep found her friends, rounded up by brigands. Her gleaming glaive made no sound with each graceful slice, rending sinew and bonds alike. Thus did the Moon exact justice, and the Sun soon warmed the evildoers' corpses...
Slaves to might! Forsake any warmth or memory! Slaves to fury! Before we fall to the carrion-eaters, even Hell's armies will kneel before us! -Daemon Knight Archills
Remember the fall of the Betrayer Angel! He who lost faith in victory! He who conspired with evil to spawn abominations! Let his hubris and its consequence remind us never to stray.
Champion of the Silver City Spiritborn Equipment

The land cries out against you. Her every winnowed field, her every razed forest bears witness against you. And when she sends her champion against you, will you shame yourself with false tears as you are culled? -Achuil of Tiklan

Anjuli had lost count of the nights spent in the cold, calling out into the Spirit Realm for the Leopard to approach. When at last it pounced from behind and sunk its claws in her shoulders, she let out a whoop of joy. "You've got me! Or have I got you?"

They say the Spirit Realm shuddered as an inhuman scream echoed through the jungle from Travincal. Many spiritborn raced to confront whatever evil lay inside, but they arrived to meet Baal, Lord of Destruction, waiting with open arms.
The harder you fight, the deeper they sink.
The Flames of Abaddon Spiritborn Equipment

Haldan's elder brother stood to inherit everything. The family fortune, lordship of their lands, and the love of their people. Refusing to live in his brother's shadow, Haldan summoned a shade to kill him. A mortal sin that condemned Haldan to darkness.
Bitter in life. Poison in death.
As the cat winds her way across the dunes, her paws barely move the sand. Protector by day, warrior by night, to meet her gaze is to be judged.
Goddess of the Sun. Eye of the Moon.

The spirits don't care about our mortal concepts like 'good' or 'evil,' do they? No, no, nothing that human still remains in this spectral armor. This husk carries a far more base desire: to crush anyone that dares stand in their way! -Tribesman Tuktol
Worker of grief! Eternal is thy struggle, for against thee do a multitude of enemies conspire, in order to forfeit thy soul to the worms. Yet thou rise! -Ligra Luvultengi IV
Age of the Slayer Spiritborn Equipment

His pinched skin, tented between golden spikes—this was Griga's music. With childlike delight she ran her coarse fingers through every barb, every stud of her masterpiece: Gagn himself, suspended just above her, his face transfixed in a most pleasant horror...
Heron! All-hunter, all-seer. Avert not your wings from this demon-haunted world, but grant us swift deliverance! In the name of your avatar, we pray for your strength.
You see, at this point, I'm pretty much the queen bitch of the universe.

Running, panting, sweat-drenched. Frantic. Hakna stumbles into the sacristy of an old cathedral. He has pissed off the wrong people. He hears the coffers ring. Is there a priest here? He turns his head to look—the final mistake he ever made.

Beware, beware! As a hazy vision of water leads many to their gasping deaths, so too do these illusory huntresses lure raiders and tomb-robbers to their timely end... -excerpt from Legends of Old Kehjistan

We are Thornblood, now and forever. Ours is the rose, the thorn, and the sting. She laid a bloody polearm into the arms of her fallen comrade, and leaned over, kissing the slain's forehead. "Death becomes you, as well as all who dared prune you."
Can you imprison a flame? Though you bring cages of stone and chains of malice, I am the blaze that cannot be contained!
Come then, student of Drek'Thar. Power is all around you... so reach your hand out and bid the elements. Let stone and wind harken your cry. Let the earth defend you!

Where once stood a rebellious king now towered an emperor born of pure defiance. His golden visage cracked with a laugh that seemed to peal in every corner of the heavens. "I have awakened to far more than emptiness..."

They locked me in a cage of silence and called it Sanctuary! They shackled me with morality, and called it freedom. Tonight, I shatter the chains. The Era Apocalyptika is upon us... -the Mad Warlock Rojang
The Flames of Abaddon Warlock Equipment

Xianshi's best came at her with their squeaky-clean blades, thinking themselves so very capable. Fools, all. When the last of them fell, Onibi knelt in the rubble listening to their final breaths fading. Now...the summoning could begin.

Ryze's shovel strikes something soft beneath the ancient stone. Not dirt. Not bone. Movement. The gravedigger freezes, his sweat mixing with the cold rain, as a phantasm's face rises from the earth sloughing spectral wisps. Then a howl: "THANKS FOR SAVING ME THE TROUBLE."

The altar-stones cracked under his hand, groaning as they stretched into new, humiliating forms. Garag looked on with an approving grin, watching once-holy symbols become restraints and barbs. "Your Light will be a silent witness to your sin tonight," he promised the empty pews.
Behold, those who have power, and who are not afraid to wield it. Behold...the warlocks! -Gul'dan

Nature is full of traps. Webs. Vines. But when a succubus gets their hooks in you, what material do they use? Your own desire, your own folly. You are your own downfall! Master thyself above all! Or else they will hold dominion over you... -Magister Nairan, a week before his disappearance

What manner of beast darkens our land, gives rise to our fears? Whether it be a novel abomination or powerful death dealer adorned in trophies, we cannot say. But we'll ready the wards and noisemakers!
What lurks in the long winter?

SNO: My lord, where do we hold our court tonight? I have not broken fast in weeks since we supped on the greasy idiots of Backwater.
My lady, Cerrigar has a festival tonight. Anniversary of Astaroth's fall.
Ach, you do love to spoil me... she said, licking her lips.

Translation: Curses? You think you know the meaning of curses, my feeble Paladin? No, no. The skies don't darken for you. The earth doesn't groan under your step. You are the Light's own. Warlock Darcha pushed her scarred face into her fulsome mask with a hiss of energy. "Allow me to show you...in your dreams."

The intruder reels from the incense-fumes like a drunk, his limbs unresponsive. A litany of curses refuse to leave his lips as he slumps across the altar. The visage of a grand snake-queen emerges before him. "Hope I taste good," he thinks as her maw widens...

Every eye festooning Krykh was born of a ritual few Warlocks have appetite for, and even fewer the nerve. To make way for the Panops required sacrificing one's own eyes for infernal beyond-sight. A price Krykh gladly paid...

Hail to Razham life-vore, hail to Redstar end-bringer. The cult leader's voice rang out in the blood-drenched cave. "Hail to the powers who claim this land." He raised a grotesque skull covered in flames, opened its jaw, and imbibed the pitch-black fluid that poured out of it. "Next...we devour Estuar."

Name's Van Sashka. Game's demons. He tips his wide-brimmed hat with his intricately infernal arm, which catches your eye. "Oh, this? Just a tool o' the trade. You can call me a...collector." He grins, the sparkle of his teeth blinding you.
Style and panache can't be taught.

I've dug deep until I hit the smell of mold and misery, of dying flora and crawling fauna. The underworld is not just molten rock and the screams of the damned... Far more things hold sway that would horrify you if you knew. Let them be. -Mashka of Natsalarwaka

I confess to my brothers and sisters that I have greatly sinned. In thought and deed have I invited Hell. Consorted with the engines of suffering, conspired to bring about the passing of the old. Al'Diabolos, may he usher in the new! -Confession IX of the Demonstongue Tract
Hear now the hymn of Hell!
As a chaotic force of nature, a god-tier mix of mischief and defiance, Ne Zha proves that you can choose your own path—even if you have to burn down the old one to do it...
Ne Zha's legend as heavy hitter for the Heavens grew far and wide... So, too, did his prowess. Even the mighty tremble!

Sacred heir of Draenor's life-spirit...draw near, god of ravens! Though brought low by Sethe's curse, your spirit soars on the wings of prophecy and far-seeing wisdom. Show us why you were worshipped across worlds! Show us the true power of shadows...
High on the cliffs, against the clouds, a lion's form catches the waning sun. "A good omen," claim the Spiritborn, hopeful for a bloodless night.
There is a reason the jaguar is so revered among the Spiritborn. From the time they are young, the cats display great intuition of the realm beyond, often "seeing" what human eyes cannot.
One foot in the realm of spirits.
It's a rare thing indeed for a wildcat of Nahantu to be born with white fur. To see one is an auspicious blessing. To capture and tame one would be a gift fit for a king.
According to legend, the Vizjerei's fortune was guarded by a beast, called to heel from the Realm of Terror itself. True or not, the Vizjerei were happy to encourage the rumor.
You taste metal in the air as thunder rolls in from the distance. Soon, a terrible roar. The whitefire demon approaches. And it has chosen you.
The Lord Eater Mount & Mount Armor
Ash'adar is as swift and soft as the moons' light. The Watchers know this, and learn by her example.

SNO: Mount changes color in-game. Fiery orange during the day, blue at night.

Translation: Daughter of the moon, niece of the sun.
Ten thousand strong, the angels burst forth from the clouds and fell upon the gathered army of the underworld, tearing it asunder. -The Books of Jarl, Volume IV
Oh, Sha'lawai, once so strong and sure of foot, fell below the darkness! Out she comes to haunt our nights. We hide from her. We weep for her. -Umbaru Folk Song

When it's late on the road and ye hear rumblin' from on far? Ye turn around, lad. Got plenty of life to live 'fore you think to join up with the dead, ridin' unholy beasts. A ghastly fate. -Griddem of Braestig

I've rifled through many a tome, not all of 'em approved by your Church! But that's how I've conceived this special saddle, see—one that'll repel the beast's inner fury and keep the rider safe! But, erm, I need a volunteer to test it. You in? -Acanel the Asterist
Far from the eye of the living, a rare flock of felines swirl around the cursed tel. What immortal hand or paw could have devised this dread rite?
Some of the Swarm's finest strains, straight from the Koprulu sector. Although if one of them gets out? You're gonna need more than one stimpack.
You'd have to be insane to try riding that!
The Sector's Finest Prestige Mount & Mount Armor

How does it move? breathed the court mage from Lut Gholein, her fingers trembling. She pressed her outstretched digit into its spine. The bone yielded to her touch, sliding apart easily as the creature let out a tiny mewl. The necromancer nearby leaned in and whispered, "I have no idea."

Recent battle had unearthed a glimpse of something beneath the hoarfrost—a nose, or ears? Dresha of Nevesk tugged at the shape out of curiosity, then recoiled in horror as the entombed being burst out of the icy ground. Face to face with true majesty, honed of ice and magic, Dresha did the only thing he could...run like the wind.
Of all the aviaries in the aerie, you had to bring this beauty to mine? whistled Armorer Frellaf, jealousy brimming in their tone. "Glorious animal. Keep it unharmed or I'll kill you myself."
A kiss of death from above.
Age of the Slayer Prestige Mount & Mount Armor

Their presence is neither abomination nor curse–beautiful and terrible, as storms are. In a place where demons teem and the very air sings with heat, the fell horde moves with innate dignity. Perfect. Unafraid.
Flames of Abaddon Prestige Mount & Mount Armor

The ethercat stuck its head out through the rip between worlds, face to face with one Sorcerer Dervan. The two exchanged quizzical looks. "Burning Hells!" Dervan shouted, as the realization flashed across his mind: maybe, just maybe, making your town portals last longer does funny things to the fabric of reality.

Don't you set your heart on the Far River, boy. Unnatural place. Dog-faced lizards. Birds of no feather. Fish-dragons, with boilin' eyes like a witch's cauldron. If you go'n get eaten, I won't dry your mother's tears! -Farmer Hashel
This is no beast of burden, but an animal of war! bellowed the mercenary commander. "Forsake your mount, and you forsake your life itself! I expect you both back by dusk, bathed in victory's blood!"

Your letter mystified us all, my dear Paratyma. Where on Sanctuary did you chance upon this basilisk? Were you...inebriated when you reported these crystalline formations, pellucid scales? Your theories of a null bramble nonwithstanding, the College asks for a certain rigor to these fanciful reports. -Scholar Jacio
A chimera of a different color.
Born from the blood of the willing, these steeds carry Lilith's Chosen and her message of salvation across all of Sanctuary.
Cloven hooves for all her children.
Bred in the Fields of Judgment below the Alabaster Monastery, attendants say the steeds are suffuse with His radiant energy.
The reach of the Church is great, and this is in no small part due to the power and endurance of its warhorses.
Carrying the Light to the far corners of Sanctuary.
The Peace Warders of the Triune spread their message across Sanctuary, astride powerful steeds draped in symbols of the Three.
Noble beasts that bear a terrible burden.
Many of Sanctuary's heroes face pain and torment in their lives, undaunted. Even their mounts bear the burden of their masters' struggles.
There is no joy without suffering.
Both life and death suffuse the swamps of Hawezar. There exists a rotting affliction that destroys animal flesh, yet promotes plant growth.
With the dark power of his unholy sword, The Lich King raised his once faithful steed into the ranks of the undead.
The steed of The Lich King, both in life and death.
Not all of Sanctuary's killers look like villains clad in black. Some dress in bright fineries bought with the lives of others.
Members of the Celestial Court speed across Sanctuary on steeds that seem to be made of stardust, etched with cosmic geometries, carrying their esoteric magic far and wide.
When the Old Gods roamed Sanctuary, they rode upon the most powerful of steeds. They would place powerful runes upon their coats and dressed them in nature's armors.
The towns and villages of Xiansai are widespread. A strong horse and stronger barding are vital to travelers in the most dangerous regions.
The pride of the Xian traveler.
The golden symbols of the cathedral, shown as irresistible beacons for Klath-Ulna's vengeance. And any he attended would soon peal no more.
The road to revenge is paved with blood and gold.
Honor their dead with offerings of flowers and replica skulls to appease visiting spirits.
The invading barbarian lords greatly admired the regal steeds of the west, creating several stud farms throughout the countryside.
The invading barbarian lords greatly admired the regal steeds of the west, creating several stud farms throughout the countryside.
Adorning this beautiful steed are tack and trappings painstakingly crafted from the finest silks and leathers, with a lantern of polished oak and mild bronze.
The coursers thunder across the plain, driven by their druidic riders to corral the oncoming storm.

Tales have been told of an elusive and mysterious creature, a beautiful steed that seemingly glows with ethereal lights dancing on its form. It rides hastily in the wind, captivating any fortunate enough to see it pass.
This gruesome collection of horse and human flesh smacks of the foulest necromancy. Soulless tools for a soulless rider.
Charge boldly through the ice and snow atop a courser born of winter itself.
A cerulean and midnight conveyance to a realm of enchanting delight.

The merchants of Kehjistan are known to travel across most of the Eastern Continent. With mounts first bred on the plains west of Dahlgur Oasis, the merchants always return to the fields when visiting Kehjistan proper.

The taste of the Ancient's lost magic was intoxicating. The wearer of the Pearl began scouring Sanctuary, desperate for more forbidden knowledge and power.
When Korelan of Westmarch died, he was buried atop his beloved horse. Each was prepared in full regalia to ride on into death...until a needful stranger crossed their path.
Though seemingly safe for human contact, the alchemized demon-bone and crystal barding has had an unforeseen effect on equine physiology.
Many who suffer dwell in the shadows, as though judgment would deepen their pain. Few ride through town with agony laid bare: a revelation for all to see.
At last, the cold grip closes. Blackness spreads. Fear gives way to night. The endless and empty night. - Askari proverb
Nocturne of Steel Mount & Mount Armor
